詩人興聖嗣之克肖，而深歎其爲瑞也。蓋麟乃仁厚之物也，而公子之德似之，則聖人過化存神之妙，豈不足徵哉？宜詩人興而歎之也。想其
translation_en:
…the great strength of Xia, the great ordering of Shang, and Zhou’s joint receipt of its great foundation surely had their reasons! Nevertheless, the Duke of Zhou appended to a line of the Book of Changes the words, “The tiger watches intently”: this means humbling oneself before worthy men with single-minded resolve. He also said, “The cauldron has yellow ears and a metal carrying bar; constancy is beneficial”: this means employing worthy men without misgivings. These statements and the principle of drawing out men’s abilities illuminate one another. Yet within only a few generations, the chief minister failed to conduct government himself, and Huangfu favored only those with abundant stores of wealth. Alas! Here lies the distinction between order and disorder, security and peril, in a state. Let those who rule others take warning from this!

Book of Odes
“The qilin’s feet; the noble lord’s virtuous sons. Ah, the qilin!”
Han Xi

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “This composition deftly brings out the meaning of ‘auspicious sign’; its conception is excellent and may serve as a model.” [The closing words of this comment appear after the opening of the next comment in the transcription.]

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Most writers on this topic discuss the qilin’s feet and [the lord’s sons?] in parallel, apparently losing sight of their relative importance. This composition alone grasps the purport; I select it.” [The wording and placement of the opening portion are doubtful.]

Examiner Mao, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It captures the meaning of the ‘Airs of Zhou and the South.’”

Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Refined and elegant.”

The poet uses an evocative comparison to show how the sage’s descendants resemble him, and deeply admires them as an auspicious sign. For the qilin is a benevolent and generous creature. If the virtues of the lord’s sons resemble its qualities, does this not sufficiently attest to the wondrous power by which the sage transforms wherever he passes and exerts a spiritual influence wherever he abides? It is fitting that the poet should use this comparison and express his admiration. We may imagine his…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
意謂夫我文王后妃備徽柔之儀刑盡思齊之
家法其德之盛固難名矣而化之所及不有可
言者乎是故麟以至仁而其趾亦至仁我公子
濡德之至則宜其敏德之速貴不驕而富不侈
蓋有不言而喻之機觀化之久則宜其感化之
深不作好而不作惡蓋有不動而變之妙慈祥
愷悌體仁足以長人凡其本之身心而達之事
爲之著藹藹乎太和之洋溢也易直子諒而厚
德足以載物凡其始于幾微而擴之行事之頃
===
洋洋乎至愛之流通也公子之德如此不但如
麟之趾而已于嗟其即麟也乎誠以太平無象
麟出以象其象今旣與之同仁則興王之業有
所基至治無形麟出以形其形今旣與之同德
則靈長之祚有所賴自其跡而觀物之不可以
爲人人之不可以爲物而形類大有不同矣奚
可比擬哉自其理而論人之未始不爲天天之
未始不爲人而禎祥則一致矣奚啻彷彿哉是
則以物爲瑞瑞之瑞也以人爲瑞不瑞之瑞也
punctuated: 意謂夫我文王后妃，備徽柔之儀刑，盡思齊之家法，其德之盛固難名矣，而化之所及，不有可言者乎？是故麟以至仁，而其趾亦至仁。我公子濡德之至，則宜其敏德之速，貴不驕而富不侈，蓋有不言而喻之機；觀化之久，則宜其感化之深，不作好而不作惡，蓋有不動而變之妙。慈祥愷悌，體仁足以長人，凡其本之身心而達之事爲之著，藹藹乎太和之洋溢也；易直子諒，而厚德足以載物，凡其始于幾微而擴之行事之頃，洋洋乎至愛之流通也。公子之德如此，不但如麟之趾而已。于嗟，其即麟也乎！誠以太平無象，麟出以象其象，今旣與之同仁，則興王之業有所基；至治無形，麟出以形其形，今旣與之同德，則靈長之祚有所賴。自其跡而觀，物之不可以爲人，人之不可以爲物，而形類大有不同矣，奚可比擬哉？自其理而論，人之未始不爲天，天之未始不爲人，而禎祥則一致矣，奚啻彷彿哉？是則以物爲瑞，瑞之瑞也；以人爲瑞，不瑞之瑞也。
translation_en:
…the meaning is that our King Wen and his consort fully embodied an exemplary pattern of beautiful gentleness and perfected the household discipline celebrated in “Thinking of the Worthy” (Si qi). The fullness of their virtue is indeed difficult to describe; yet can something not be said of those reached by their transforming influence? Thus, because the qilin is supremely benevolent, even its feet are supremely benevolent. Our lord’s sons have been thoroughly steeped in virtue, so it is fitting that they should advance swiftly in virtue: noble without arrogance and wealthy without extravagance. Here lies the working of understanding attained without words. Having long witnessed moral transformation, they should fittingly be deeply transformed by it: indulging neither personal likes nor personal dislikes. Here lies the marvel of change brought about without movement. Kindly, gracious, joyful, and brotherly, they embody benevolence sufficiently to lead others. In all that is rooted in their minds and persons and manifested in their deeds, supreme harmony overflows in abundant richness. Gentle, upright, “zi,” and trustworthy [?], their ample virtue suffices to sustain all things. In all that begins in the subtlest stirrings and expands into action, utmost love flows forth in abundance. Such is the virtue of our lord’s sons: they do not merely resemble the qilin’s feet. Ah, are they not the qilin itself!

Indeed, supreme peace has no visible image; the qilin appears to give it an image. Now that they share its benevolence, the enterprise of establishing kingly rule has a foundation. Perfect government has no visible form; the qilin appears to give it form. Now that they share its virtue, the dynasty’s enduring good fortune has something upon which to depend. Viewed in their outward manifestations, an animal cannot be a human, nor a human an animal; their forms and kinds differ greatly. How could they be compared? Discussed in terms of their underlying principle, however, humanity has never been other than Heaven, nor Heaven other than humanity; as auspicious signs they are one. How could this be merely a resemblance? Thus, to regard an animal as an auspicious sign is to find auspiciousness in an auspicious portent; to regard a human being as an auspicious sign is to find auspiciousness in what is no portent.

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
若詩人者亦可謂善言天德而善觀王化歟抑
論之周家以仁厚立國故本支百世不顯亦世
皆文王亹亹令聞爲之也是故一索而得武王
之伐暴救民再索而得周公之制禮作樂若毛
衛魯聃曹滕之賢不可勝數則詩人麟趾爲不
虛矣說者謂此詩爲關雎之應觀於此益信
是生后稷降之百福黍稷重穋稙穉菽麥
奄有下國俾民稼穡有稷有黍有稻有
秬奄有下土纘禹之緒
李希顏
同考試官教諭章　批〔深得詩人推本之意〕
錄之
同考試官教諭黃　批〔天爲民生稷稷奉天粒民〕
〔此作發揮透徹刻之〕
考試官學正毛　批〔得頌體〕
考試官教授林　批〔正而葩〕
===
詩人原聖人之生受天休而國有所啓立民命
□□有所承甚矣聖人之生不偶然也受天休
punctuated:
若詩人者，亦可謂善言天德而善觀王化歟！抑論之，周家以仁厚立國，故本支百世，不顯亦世，皆文王亹亹令聞爲之也。是故一索而得武王之伐暴救民，再索而得周公之制禮作樂。若毛、衛、魯、聃、曹、滕之賢，不可勝數，則詩人麟趾爲不虛矣。說者謂此詩爲關雎之應，觀於此益信。
「是生后稷，降之百福。黍稷重穋，稙穉菽麥。奄有下國，俾民稼穡。有稷有黍，有稻有秬。奄有下土，纘禹之緒。」
李希顏
同考試官教諭章，批〔深得詩人推本之意〕錄之。
同考試官教諭黃，批〔天爲民生稷，稷奉天粒民〕〔此作發揮透徹，刻之〕
考試官學正毛，批〔得頌體〕
考試官教授林，批〔正而葩〕
詩人原聖人之生，受天休而國有所啓，立民命□□有所承。甚矣，聖人之生不偶然也！受天休
translation_en:
…Such a poet may indeed be said to speak well of Heaven’s virtue and to discern well the transforming influence of kingship! Moreover, the house of Zhou founded its state upon benevolence and generosity. Thus its main line and collateral branches endured for a hundred generations, illustrious from generation to generation: all this was brought about by King Wen’s tireless labors and excellent reputation. Thus, at the first seeking came King Wu, who attacked the tyrant and rescued the people; at the second came the Duke of Zhou, who established rites and made music. Worthies such as those of Mao, Wei, Lu, Dan, Cao, and Teng were too numerous to count. The poet’s praise in “The Qilin’s Hooves” was therefore no empty claim. Commentators say that this poem is the response to “Guanju”; what we have seen here makes this still more convincing.
“Thus she gave birth to Hou Ji, upon whom were bestowed a hundred blessings: millet and panicled millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain, early-sown and late-sown crops, beans and wheat. He possessed the states below and enabled the people to sow and reap. There were panicled millet and millet, rice and black millet. He possessed the lands below and continued the work of Yu.”
Li Xiyan.
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, commented: “He has deeply grasped the poet’s intention to trace things to their source.” Include it in the record.
Associate Examiner Huang, an Instructor, commented: “Heaven brought forth Hou Ji for the people; Hou Ji obeyed Heaven and fed the people with grain.” “This composition expounds the meaning thoroughly. Print it.”
Examiner Mao, a School Instructor, commented: “It captures the form of the hymn.”
Examiner Lin, a Professor, commented: “Correct and richly adorned.”
The poet traces the birth of the sage to its source: he received Heaven’s favor, and thereby the state had its beginning; he secured the people’s livelihood, and □□ there was something to carry on [?]. How far the sage’s birth was from being accidental! He received Heaven’s favor …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以立民命魯之封國有自來矣哉閟宮之詩魯
僖公脩廟而作也意謂我魯之爲國封建雖基
於周公而肇造實由於后稷誠以后稷應期而
誕生正天之所資以立民也苟爲民而不降之
以百福則稷亦何所爲哉故黍稷重穋之殊名
命之以爲降育之惠稙穉菽麥之異種貽之以
爲開麗之仁是皆百福之降也但見天以是而
錫之申嘉貺於冲漠之表稷以是而荷之膺寵
命於昭格之中故有邰之封在堯無所於吝而
===
室家之卽在稷不以爲貪是稷雖封於堯而實
受福於天者矣然稷之膺命而有國正以奉天
以澤民也澤民而不教之稼穡則民亦何所立
哉故匪且有且而遍若黍若稷於天下載耕載
穫而溥曰稻曰秬於域中是皆稼穡之事也但
見無適而非耕則無適而非稷之奄有無往而
非土則無往而非稷之成能故六府允脩之功
在禹雖不可及而生民粒食之績在稷實有所
承是稷不唯有功於魯抑有功於禹矣是則古
punctuated: 以立民命，魯之封國有自來矣哉！《閟宮》之詩，魯僖公脩廟而作也。意謂我魯之爲國，封建雖基於周公，而肇造實由於后稷，誠以后稷應期而誕生，正天之所資以立民也。苟爲民而不降之以百福，則稷亦何所爲哉？故黍稷重穋之殊名，命之以爲降育之惠；稙穉菽麥之異種，貽之以爲開麗之仁。是皆百福之降也。但見天以是而錫之，申嘉貺於冲漠之表；稷以是而荷之，膺寵命於昭格之中。故有邰之封，在堯無所於吝，而室家之卽，在稷不以爲貪。是稷雖封於堯，而實受福於天者矣。然稷之膺命而有國，正以奉天以澤民也。澤民而不教之稼穡，則民亦何所立哉？故匪且有且，而遍若黍若稷於天下；載耕載穫，而溥曰稻曰秬於域中。是皆稼穡之事也。但見無適而非耕，則無適而非稷之奄有；無往而非土，則無往而非稷之成能。故六府允脩之功，在禹雖不可及，而生民粒食之績，在稷實有所承。是稷不唯有功於魯，抑有功於禹矣。是則古
translation_en: …to establish the people's livelihood: the enfeoffment of Lu indeed had its origins far in the past! The poem “The Secluded Temple” was composed when Duke Xi of Lu restored the ancestral temple. Its meaning is that, although the establishment of our state of Lu through enfeoffment was founded upon the Duke of Zhou, its beginnings actually derived from Hou Ji. For Hou Ji was born at the appointed time, and was precisely the one upon whom Heaven relied to establish the people's livelihood. If Heaven intended him to serve the people but did not send down upon him a hundred blessings, what could Ji have accomplished? Thus, the differently named grains—broomcorn and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening varieties—were bestowed upon him as Heaven's favor in sending down nourishment; the different crops—early-sown and late-sown grains, beans and wheat—were given to him as its benevolence in bringing forth abundance [?]. All these were the descent of a hundred blessings. We see Heaven bestowing these upon him, extending its gracious gifts from beyond the silent and formless realm; and Ji receiving them, accepting Heaven's favoring mandate amid its manifest presence. Thus, Yao was unstinting in granting him the fief of Tai, while Ji did not consider it covetous to settle his household there. Although Ji was enfeoffed by Yao, it was truly from Heaven that he received his blessings. Yet Ji's acceptance of the mandate and possession of a state were precisely so that he might serve Heaven and benefit the people. If he benefited the people without teaching them to sow and reap, how could they sustain themselves? Thus, “fei qie you qie” [?], and he spread broomcorn and foxtail millet throughout the world; he plowed and harvested, and spread rice and black millet throughout the realm. These were all the tasks of sowing and reaping. We see that wherever one went there was cultivation, and thus everywhere lay within Ji's encompassing possession; wherever one traveled there was soil, and thus everywhere Ji brought his abilities to fulfillment. Hence, although Yu's achievement in duly ordering the Six Resources was unsurpassable, Ji's achievement in enabling the people to eat grain truly carried on that work. Ji therefore rendered service not only to Lu, but also to Yu. Thus, the ancients…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
人其生有自其出有爲如此此周人之所由生
而我魯之所以有國也歟抑論之魯人頌稷而
追及於禹何也傳曰微禹吾其魚乎是功之大
莫過於禹與稷也故孟子以禹稷並稱而周公
尊之以配天不亦宜哉然魯終不能纘禹之緒
蓋僖公以私勞寵其臣而卑公室以私恩崇其
母而輕宗廟則不復伯禽之魯矣噫此夫子一
變至道之言其有所感也夫
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕春公會戎于潛〔隱公〕
〔二年〕
===
吉來猷
同考試官教諭彭　批〔王德王道發明殆盡〕
得聖人垂憲要旨
考試官學正毛　批〔謹嚴〕
考試官教授林　批〔得旨〕
聖人脩經大一統以明王德之體外四夷以明
王道之用蓋王德施之以仁體也王道制之以
punctuated:
人其生有自，其出有爲如此。此周人之所由生，而我魯之所以有國也歟？抑論之，魯人頌稷而追及於禹，何也？傳曰：「微禹，吾其魚乎！」是功之大，莫過於禹與稷也。故孟子以禹稷並稱，而周公尊之以配天，不亦宜哉？然魯終不能纘禹之緒。蓋僖公以私勞寵其臣而卑公室，以私恩崇其母而輕宗廟，則不復伯禽之魯矣。噫！此夫子一變至道之言，其有所感也夫！
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕。春，公會戎于潛〔隱公〕〔二年〕。
吉來猷
同考試官教諭彭　批〔王德王道發明殆盡〕：得聖人垂憲要旨。
考試官學正毛　批〔謹嚴〕。
考試官教授林　批〔得旨〕。
聖人脩經，大一統以明王德之體，外四夷以明王道之用。蓋王德施之以仁，體也；王道制之以
translation_en:
… men thus had a source from which they sprang and a purpose for which they came forth. Was this not the origin of the people of Zhou and the reason that we in Lu possessed a state? Yet let us consider: why, when the people of Lu praised Ji, did they trace matters back to Yu? The Commentary says: “Were it not for Yu, would we not be fish?” Thus none surpassed Yu and Ji in the greatness of their achievements. Hence Mencius spoke of Yu and Ji together, and the Duke of Zhou honored Ji by making him the companion of Heaven in sacrifice. Was this not fitting? Yet Lu ultimately failed to carry on Yu’s legacy. Duke Xi favored his ministers for services rendered to him personally, thereby diminishing the ducal house; out of private affection he exalted his mother, thereby slighting the ancestral temple. Lu was consequently no longer the Lu of Bo Qin. Alas! When the Master said that with one transformation Lu could attain the Way, surely some such feeling moved him!
Spring and Autumn Annals
“Spring, the first month of the king’s calendar.” 〔First year of Duke Yin〕 “In spring, the duke met the Rong at Qian.” 〔Duke Yin〕〔Second year〕
Ji Laiyou

Examiner Mao, Director of Studies, commented: 〔“Careful and rigorous.”〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, commented: 〔“Grasps the purport.”〕
When the sage edited the Classic, he exalted the unity of rule to illuminate the substance of kingly virtue, and treated the barbarians of the four quarters as outside the realm to illuminate the functioning of the kingly Way. For kingly virtue is exercised through benevolence: this is its substance. The kingly Way regulates through …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
義用也自非聖人豈能脩此哉慨自黍離既降
王德之不明久矣經於正月之上而書王何也
蓋王德莫大於覆載之無私也周德既衰天下
已不知有王而況望其能覆載耶聖人懼王德
之衰也故爲此書若曰天下皆王朔之是遵而
無遠焉者可不有以全其體哉必也合八荒於
我闥之中自内以至於外囿萬象於同胞之内
由親而及其踈以賔禮親諸侯則若侯甸至鎮
藩之頒政職以文德格遠人則若甸采至蠻流
===
之被聲教若海外一有失所則興滅繼絶治亂
持危以撫綏之如此則至德洽於民心非明王
德之體乎自徐戎雜處王道不明久矣經於會
潛之戎而舉號何也蓋王道莫先於華夷之有
辨也魯君既會天下已不知有夷而況望其能
膺懲耶聖人懼王道之微也故爲此書若曰徐
戎實族類之異而非可會者可不有以全其用
哉必也以鳥獸不可與群則外而不内以豺狼
不可相昵則踈而不親九畿雖許之來享而必
punctuated:
義，用也。自非聖人，豈能脩此哉？慨自黍離既降，王德之不明久矣。經於正月之上而書王，何也？蓋王德莫大於覆載之無私也。周德既衰，天下已不知有王，而況望其能覆載耶？聖人懼王德之衰也，故爲此書。若曰：天下皆王朔之是遵，而無遠焉者，可不有以全其體哉？必也合八荒於我闥之中，自内以至於外；囿萬象於同胞之内，由親而及其踈。以賔禮親諸侯，則若侯甸至鎮藩之頒政職；以文德格遠人，則若甸采至蠻流之被聲教。若海外一有失所，則興滅繼絶，治亂持危，以撫綏之。如此，則至德洽於民心，非明王德之體乎？
自徐戎雜處，王道不明久矣。經於會潛之戎而舉號，何也？蓋王道莫先於華夷之有辨也。魯君既會，天下已不知有夷，而況望其能膺懲耶？聖人懼王道之微也，故爲此書。若曰：徐戎實族類之異，而非可會者，可不有以全其用哉？必也以鳥獸不可與群，則外而不内；以豺狼不可相昵，則踈而不親。九畿雖許之來享，而必
translation_en:
…righteousness is its operation. Who but the Sage could have compiled this? Alas, ever since “Millet Drooping” (Shu li) was relegated to a lower rank, kingly virtue has long remained obscure. Why does the Classic write “the king’s” before “first month”? Because nothing in kingly virtue is greater than impartially sheltering and sustaining all things. Once Zhou’s virtue had declined, the world no longer recognized a king; how much less could one expect him to shelter and sustain it? The Sage feared the decline of kingly virtue and therefore wrote this. It is as though he said: All under Heaven follow the king’s calendar, however distant they may be; can one fail to preserve this virtue’s substance in its entirety? One must gather the eight distant reaches within one’s own gates, extending from the inner regions to the outer, and embrace all beings as children of the same parents, reaching from those close at hand to those far removed. Drawing the regional lords close through guest ritual is exemplified by the allocation of governmental duties throughout the zones of service, from the hou and dian zones to the zhen and fan zones. Bringing distant peoples to allegiance through civil virtue is exemplified by the extension of the ruler’s influence and instruction from the dian and cai zones to the man and liu zones. If anyone beyond the seas should lose their proper place, one must restore extinguished states, continue severed lines of succession, bring order to disorder, and support those in peril, thereby comforting and pacifying them. In this way, supreme virtue would permeate the people’s hearts. Would this not illuminate the substance of kingly virtue?
Ever since the Xu Rong dwelt intermingled with the central states, the Kingly Way has long remained obscure. Why does the Classic explicitly name as Rong those met at Qian? Because nothing takes precedence in the Kingly Way over distinguishing the Hua from the Yi. Once the lord of Lu had met with them, the world no longer recognized them as Yi; how much less could one expect him to chastise them? The Sage feared the weakening of the Kingly Way and therefore wrote this. It is as though he said: The Xu Rong are indeed of a different kind and are not people with whom one may hold such a meeting; can one fail to preserve the Kingly Way’s operation in its entirety? Since one cannot flock together with birds and beasts, they must be kept outside rather than admitted within; since one cannot be intimate with jackals and wolves, they must be kept at a distance rather than drawn close. Although those in the nine zones are permitted to come and present offerings, one must…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
設溝涂以固其防六服雖與之來王而必奮武
衛以正其限若夷人一有不恭則殷武入阻冗
戎薄伐以震懾之如此則大防嚴於天下謂非
王道之用矣乎噫以王德爲體以王道爲用聖
人何惓惓於王哉人君而知此義則知所以爲
王矣抑論之仁義之道可相有而不可偏廢也
春秋立教亦詳切矣而漢唐宋諸君乃有結婚
姻於外夷處羌胡於境内正朔不及於燕雲教
化不行於河北則併王德王道而失之矣噫爲
===
人君者何莫學夫春秋
秋七月己未同盟於亳城北　公會晉侯
宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔俱〕
襄公十有一年
朱録
同考試官教諭彭　批
〔畧本鄭書爲盟髙本以爲會亦徒勦成說可厭是篇依傳成文詞氣典雅宜録〕
考試官學正毛　批　褒貶有則
punctuated:
設溝涂以固其防；六服雖與之來王，而必奮武衛以正其限。若夷人一有不恭，則殷武入阻，冗戎薄伐，以震懾之。如此，則大防嚴於天下，謂非王道之用矣乎？噫！以王德爲體，以王道爲用，聖人何惓惓於王哉！人君而知此義，則知所以爲王矣。抑論之，仁義之道可相有，而不可偏廢也。《春秋》立教亦詳切矣，而漢唐宋諸君乃有結婚姻於外夷、處羌胡於境内，正朔不及於燕雲，教化不行於河北，則併王德王道而失之矣。噫！爲人君者，何莫學夫《春秋》？
秋七月己未，同盟於亳城北。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔俱〕襄公十有一年。
朱録。
同考試官教諭彭，批：〔畧本鄭書爲盟，髙本以爲會，亦徒勦成說，可厭。是篇依傳成文，詞氣典雅，宜録。〕
考試官學正毛，批：褒貶有則。
translation_en:
…establish ditches and roads to secure the defenses. Although those in the six service zones are permitted to come and acknowledge the king, military defenses must be vigorously maintained to enforce their boundaries. If the foreign peoples show any disrespect, then mighty forces enter the difficult terrain and attack the Rong [?], striking them with awe. Thus the great boundary is strictly maintained throughout the realm: can this be denied to be the practical operation of the Kingly Way? Ah! Taking kingly virtue as the substance and the Kingly Way as its application—how earnestly the Sage concerned himself with true kingship! A ruler who understands this principle will understand how to be a true king. Moreover, benevolence and righteousness must coexist; neither may be neglected. The instruction established by the Spring and Autumn Annals is detailed and explicit. Yet some rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song contracted marriage alliances with foreign peoples and settled Qiang and Hu within their borders. Their calendar and authority did not extend to Yan and Yun, and their moral transformation did not reach Hebei. Thus they forfeited both kingly virtue and the Kingly Way. Ah! Why do rulers not study the Spring and Autumn Annals?
“In autumn, in the seventh month, on the jiwei day, they jointly swore a covenant north of Bocheng.” “The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu to attack Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu.” [Both passages:] the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
Zhu Lu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor: [The abridged version follows Zheng in writing “covenant,” while Gao’s version takes it as a “meeting” [?]. These merely plagiarize established explanations and are tiresome. This essay develops its argument in accordance with the commentary; its language and tenor are classical and elegant. It merits inclusion.]
Comment by Examiner Mao, School Instructor: “Its praise and blame follow proper standards.”

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批　明健
貳國從霸而渝信可譏霸主服貳而推誠可予
蓋以小事大貴乎信以大事小存乎誠此春秋
於亳北之盟蕭魚之會其書法有不同歟夫自
北林師集諸侯之怒鄭甚矣鄭伯要晉而結盟
亳北人固喜子展之謀也春秋何以同刺之哉
蓋晉自悼公復霸君明臣忠上懷下競鄭若能
仗信而果於從之則晉猶前日之晉也夫何欲
致晉師之伐則出師伐宋以開兵端既爲亳北
===
之盟又從楚伐宋以背前約唯依違於子囊之
歸向慢鬼神所不辭展轉於晉人之從違蹐國
家所弗顧詩曰士也不類二三其德又曰君子
屢盟亂是用長其鄭之謂矣故夫亳北之盟而
書同蓋以爲既同而復畔久矣哉鄭之渝信矣
乎逮夫東門觀兵楚人之北駕敝矣晉悼納鄭
而講會蕭魚人謂隋子展之計也春秋何以會
美之哉蓋鄭自簡公當國伐蔡怒楚從楚畔晉
使晉無誠以待之則鄭猶前日之鄭也所幸納
punctuated:
考試官教授林批：明健。
貳國從霸而渝信，可譏；霸主服貳而推誠，可予。蓋以小事大，貴乎信；以大事小，存乎誠。此春秋於亳北之盟、蕭魚之會，其書法有不同歟？夫自北林師集，諸侯之怒鄭甚矣。鄭伯要晉而結盟亳北，人固喜子展之謀也，春秋何以同刺之哉？蓋晉自悼公復霸，君明臣忠，上懷下競。鄭若能仗信而果於從之，則晉猶前日之晉也。夫何欲致晉師之伐，則出師伐宋，以開兵端；既爲亳北之盟，又從楚伐宋，以背前約。唯依違於子囊之歸向，慢鬼神所不辭；展轉於晉人之從違，蹐國家所弗顧。詩曰：「士也不類，二三其德。」又曰：「君子屢盟，亂是用長。」其鄭之謂矣。故夫亳北之盟而書同，蓋以爲既同而復畔。久矣哉，鄭之渝信矣乎！逮夫東門觀兵，楚人之北駕敝矣。晉悼納鄭而講會蕭魚，人謂隋子展之計也，春秋何以會美之哉？蓋鄭自簡公當國，伐蔡怒楚，從楚畔晉。使晉無誠以待之，則鄭猶前日之鄭也。所幸納
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: “Clear and vigorous.”

A wavering state that follows the hegemon but breaks faith deserves censure; a hegemon who wins over a wavering state by extending his sincerity deserves approval. For a small state serving a great one, faithfulness is paramount; for a great state dealing with a small one, sincerity is essential. Is this why the Spring and Autumn Annals employs different wording for the covenant north of Bo and the meeting at Xiaoyu?

When the armies assembled at Beilin, the feudal lords’ anger against Zheng was intense. The Earl of Zheng sought an agreement with Jin and concluded a covenant north of Bo. People certainly applauded Zizhan’s strategy. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals censure Zheng with the word “jointly”? Since Duke Dao had restored Jin’s hegemony, its ruler had been discerning and its ministers loyal; those above cherished their subordinates, and those below strove to serve. Had Zheng relied on good faith and resolutely followed Jin, Jin would still have been the same Jin as before. Why, then, did Zheng, wishing to provoke an attack by Jin’s armies, send troops against Song and thereby initiate hostilities? Having concluded the covenant north of Bo, it again joined Chu in attacking Song, thus violating the earlier agreement. It merely wavered according to Zिनang’s movements, unhesitatingly slighting the spirits; it shifted between obedience and defiance toward Jin, heedless of the peril it brought upon its state [?]. The Book of Odes says: “The man is inconstant; his conduct changes again and again.” It also says: “The lords repeatedly swear covenants; thereby disorder grows.” These words surely describe Zheng. Thus, in recording the covenant north of Bo with the word “jointly,” the text means that, having joined in the covenant, Zheng rebelled again. How long Zheng had persisted in breaking faith!

By the time the troops were displayed at the eastern gate, Chu’s northward expeditions had become exhausted. Duke Dao of Jin accepted Zheng’s submission and arranged a meeting at Xiaoyu. People said this followed Zizhan’s plan [?]. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals praise him with the word “meeting”? Since Duke Jian had assumed rule in Zheng, it had attacked Cai and angered Chu, then followed Chu and rebelled against Jin. Had Jin treated it without sincerity, Zheng would still have been the same Zheng as before. Fortunately, he accepted…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
厈㒓而禁侵掠伏智瑩㶑楚之謀遣叔肸而告
諸侯從魏絳息民之策故雖陳牲而不歃血踰
二紀而鄭不敢貳心雖結言而不加兵歷三駕
而楚不敢爭霸易曰信及豚魚又曰有孚盈缶
終來他吉此之謂矣故夫蕭魚之役而書會若
曰不盟而自信偉矣哉悼之推誠矣乎噫惡鄭
者欲天下之守於信也美晉者欲天下之進於
誠也而二君之得失昭然矣抑論之悼公此會
雖城濮之役有不是過誠善之善矣然工於撫
鄭而拙於謀陳明於治楚而暗於通吳何也蓋
天資固美而學問未充故歟然以春秋尊尚詐
力之時而有此會亦空谷之足音也悼亦賢矣
哉
===
禮記
禮者殊事合敬者也樂者異文合愛者也
禮樂之情同故明王以相沿也故事與
時並名與功偕
劉應熊
punctuated:
厈㒓而禁侵掠，伏智瑩㶑楚之謀，遣叔肸而告諸侯，從魏絳息民之策。故雖陳牲而不歃血，踰二紀而鄭不敢貳心；雖結言而不加兵，歷三駕而楚不敢爭霸。《易》曰：「信及豚魚。」又曰：「有孚盈缶，終來他吉。」此之謂矣。故夫蕭魚之役而書會，若曰不盟而自信，偉矣哉，悼之推誠矣乎！噫！惡鄭者，欲天下之守於信也；美晉者，欲天下之進於誠也。而二君之得失昭然矣。抑論之，悼公此會，雖城濮之役有不是過，誠善之善矣。然工於撫鄭而拙於謀陳，明於治楚而暗於通吳，何也？蓋天資固美而學問未充故歟？然以春秋尊尚詐力之時而有此會，亦空谷之足音也。悼亦賢矣哉！

禮記

禮者，殊事合敬者也；樂者，異文合愛者也。禮樂之情同，故明王以相沿也。故事與時並，名與功偕。

劉應熊
translation_en:
…received [an illegible name or phrase: 厈㒓][?] and forbade incursions and plundering, [a garbled passage concerning Zhi Ying and a plan involving Chu][?], dispatched Shu Xi to inform the feudal lords, and followed Wei Jiang’s policy of giving the people respite. Thus, although sacrificial animals were arrayed, no blood oath was sworn, and for more than twenty-four years Zheng dared not divide its allegiance. Although pledges were exchanged without further military action, after three campaigns Chu dared not contend for hegemony. The Book of Changes says, “Trust extends even to pigs and fish.” It also says, “Sincerity fills the earthen vessel; in the end, other good fortune comes.” This is what those words mean. Thus, when the Spring and Autumn Annals records the undertaking at Xiaoyu as a “meeting,” it is as though it says that trust arose of itself without a covenant. How magnificent was Duke Dao’s extension of sincerity!

Ah! To condemn Zheng is to wish that all under Heaven should remain faithful to their word; to praise Jin is to wish that all under Heaven should advance in sincerity. The successes and failures of the two rulers are thereby plainly revealed. Furthermore, consider this meeting held by Duke Dao: even the undertaking at Chengpu did not surpass it. Truly it was the best of good achievements. Yet why was he adept at conciliating Zheng but inept in his designs concerning Chen, discerning in dealing with Chu but undiscerning in establishing relations with Wu? Was it because his natural gifts were excellent but his learning was not yet complete? Nevertheless, that such a meeting should have occurred in the Spring and Autumn period, when deceit and force were esteemed, was like hearing footsteps in an empty valley. Duke Dao was indeed worthy!

Record of Rites

“Rites differ in their practices but unite in reverence; music differs in its forms but unites in affection. The essential sentiments of rites and music are the same, and thus enlightened kings have continued them in succession. Accordingly, practices accord with their times, and names correspond to achievements.”

Liu Yingxiong

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授翁　批〔發明詳盡深達禮樂之本者〕
考試官學正毛　批〔禮樂情同處是如此講〕
考試官教授林　批〔疏通〕
記者原禮樂之本同稽諸古而無不同也蓋人
心同乎愛敬也然則聖人之制作雖異而何嘗
不同哉樂記之旨如此謂夫禮樂之情固本乎
和序之妙然先王之制作通其意而已而何嘗
泥其迹哉是故大之三百小之三千禮也禮極
===
節文度數之詳其爲事固殊矣然以虔恭寅畏
爲之綱可以固肌膚之會以整齊嚴肅爲之紀
可以中周旋之規禮非殊事合敬矣乎被之五
音播之六律樂也樂有清濁疾徐之倫其爲文
固異矣然而歌咏以養性情宣優柔平中之趣
舞蹈以養血脉敷欣慕懽樂之容樂非異文合
愛矣乎是則禮同於敬樂同於愛禮樂之情同
如此則制作其有不同乎哉是故明王御世固
嘗制禮以昭度也而敬之寓於禮者則因其故
punctuated:
同考試官教授翁　批〔發明詳盡，深達禮樂之本者。〕
考試官學正毛　批〔禮樂情同處，是如此講。〕
考試官教授林　批〔疏通。〕
記者原禮樂之本同，稽諸古而無不同也。蓋人心同乎愛敬也，然則聖人之制作雖異，而何嘗不同哉？樂記之旨如此。謂夫禮樂之情，固本乎和序之妙，然先王之制作，通其意而已，而何嘗泥其迹哉？是故大之三百，小之三千，禮也。禮極節文度數之詳，其爲事固殊矣。然以虔恭寅畏爲之綱，可以固肌膚之會；以整齊嚴肅爲之紀，可以中周旋之規。禮非殊事合敬矣乎？被之五音，播之六律，樂也。樂有清濁疾徐之倫，其爲文固異矣。然而歌咏以養性情，宣優柔平中之趣；舞蹈以養血脉，敷欣慕懽樂之容。樂非異文合愛矣乎？是則禮同於敬，樂同於愛。禮樂之情同如此，則制作其有不同乎哉？是故明王御世，固嘗制禮以昭度也，而敬之寓於禮者，則因其故
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Weng, Professor, comments: “The exposition is thorough and exhaustive, reaching deeply into the foundation of ritual and music.”
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “This is how the shared essential character of ritual and music should be explained.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Clear and coherent.”
The compiler traces ritual and music to their common foundation and, examining antiquity, finds no divergence. Human hearts share love and reverence; thus, although the sages’ institutions differ, how could they ever fail to accord? Such is the purport of the Record of Music. The essential character of ritual and music is indeed rooted in the subtle workings of harmony and order. Yet in establishing their institutions, the former kings merely gave expression to this underlying intent: when did they ever cling to its outward forms?
Thus, the three hundred greater observances and the three thousand lesser observances constitute ritual. Ritual encompasses the utmost detail in ceremonial forms, measures, and numbers, and its practices certainly differ. Yet with devout respect and reverent awe as its guiding framework, it can maintain the proper disposition of the body; with orderliness and solemnity as its governing principle, it can make every movement conform to the rules. Does ritual not unite differing practices in reverence?
Setting sound to the five notes and disseminating it through the six pitch standards constitutes music. Music has its ordered distinctions of high and low, fast and slow, and its patterns certainly differ. Yet singing nourishes the nature and feelings, expressing the spirit of gentleness, ease, balance, and moderation; dancing nourishes the blood and vital channels, displaying the bearing of delight, admiration, and joy. Does music not unite differing patterns in love?
Thus ritual finds its unity in reverence, and music finds its unity in love. If the essential character of ritual and music accords in this way, how could their institutions fail to accord? Therefore, when enlightened kings governed the world, they certainly established ritual to make standards manifest; but as for the reverence embodied in ritual, they followed what had come before…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而無所紛更聖人立極固嘗作樂以新政也而
愛之寓於樂者則襲其舊而無少變易見於設
施之間者事也時以作事事之不同時之殊也
而敬未嘗殊也事不與時而並乎發於稱述之
間者名也功以成名名之不同功之異也而愛
未嘗異也名不與功而偕乎吁禮樂之所以同
者本然之妙也禮樂之所以異者制作之末也
君子欲行禮樂可不求其所同哉抑論之揖讓
見於唐虞放伐出於商周此事與時並也大章
===
大韶之盡善大濩大武之盡美名與功偕也然
必聖人在天子之位建中和之極而後禮可制
樂可作故始也法天地以爲禮樂終也又贊天
地之所不能嗚呼是豈可易言哉
事君先資其言拜自獻其身以成其信
楊廷亨
同考試官教授翁 批 講先資成信處明盡
可嘉
考試官學正毛 批 明暢
punctuated:
而無所紛更。聖人立極，固嘗作樂以新政也，而愛之寓於樂者，則襲其舊而無少變易。見於設施之間者，事也；時以作事，事之不同，時之殊也，而敬未嘗殊也。事不與時而並乎？發於稱述之間者，名也；功以成名，名之不同，功之異也，而愛未嘗異也。名不與功而偕乎？吁！禮樂之所以同者，本然之妙也；禮樂之所以異者，制作之末也。君子欲行禮樂，可不求其所同哉？抑論之，揖讓見於唐虞，放伐出於商周，此事與時並也；《大章》《大韶》之盡善，《大濩》《大武》之盡美，名與功偕也。然必聖人在天子之位，建中和之極，而後禮可制，樂可作。故始也法天地以爲禮樂，終也又贊天地之所不能。嗚呼！是豈可易言哉？

事君先資其言，拜自獻其身，以成其信。
楊廷亨

同考試官教授翁批：講先資成信處，明盡可嘉。
考試官學正毛批：明暢。
translation_en:
…without making disruptive changes. When a sage establishes the supreme standard, he has indeed composed music to renew government; yet the love embodied in music follows what has been handed down, without the slightest alteration. What appears in practical arrangements consists of undertakings. Undertakings arise in response to their times: their differences reflect differences in the times, while reverence has never differed. Do not undertakings thus go together with their times? What emerges in praise and commemoration consists of names. Achievements establish names: differences in names reflect differences in achievements, while love has never differed. Do not names thus accompany achievements? Ah! What ritual and music share is the subtle excellence of their inherent nature; their differences lie in the subsidiary details of their institution. Can the gentleman who wishes to put ritual and music into practice fail to seek what they share?

To discuss this further: deferential yielding appeared under Tang and Yu, while banishment and punitive conquest arose under Shang and Zhou. This illustrates undertakings accompanying their times. The complete goodness of Great Brilliance (Dazhang) and Great Continuance (Dashao), and the complete beauty of Great Deliverance (Dahu) and Great Martiality (Dawu), illustrate names accompanying achievements. Yet only when a sage occupies the position of Son of Heaven and establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony can ritual be instituted and music composed. Thus, at the outset, he models ritual and music upon Heaven and Earth; in the end, he further assists Heaven and Earth in what they cannot accomplish. Alas! How could this be spoken of lightly?

“In serving a ruler, one first relies upon one’s words, then bows and offers oneself [?], thereby fulfilling one’s pledge.”
Yang Tingheng

Associate Examiner Weng, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of ‘first relies upon’ and ‘fulfilling one’s pledge’ is clear and exhaustive—worthy of praise.”
Examiner Mao, School Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批　充裕
人臣之事君始有以藉其言終有以踐其言蓋
言非艱而行唯艱也苟不於其言而踐之則豈
善事其君者哉敘表記者意謂君臣之相遇自
古爲難而君子之進身以正爲貴是故幽居而
不盜固無心於仕進也然幼學所以爲壯行之
基而凡經綸事業有至有義有考以造其精篤
行而不倦固無意於南征也然窮經所以爲致
用之地而凡參贊規模有耨有聚有安以究其
===
極如欲致君於堯舜之君歟則先資其言曰如
何而陳善如何而閉邪凡多聞質而守之者鑿
鑿乎皆有定說矣豈待見君而後思爲之贊襄
哉如欲澤民於堯舜之民歟則先資其言曰如
何而熙載如何而亮工凡精知畧而行之者斷
斷乎已有成算矣豈待臨民而後思爲之康濟
哉夫事君先資其言則量而後入非入而後量
者矣夫然後拔茅而進以投魚水之懽人未必
不以先資之言爲筌蹄也君子曰事君所貴可
punctuated:
考試官教授林，批：充裕。

人臣之事君，始有以藉其言，終有以踐其言。蓋言非艱，而行唯艱也。苟不於其言而踐之，則豈善事其君者哉？敘《表記》者意謂君臣之相遇，自古爲難，而君子之進身，以正爲貴。是故幽居而不盜，固無心於仕進也；然幼學所以爲壯行之基，而凡經綸事業，有至、有義、有考，以造其精。篤行而不倦，固無意於南征也；然窮經所以爲致用之地，而凡參贊規模，有耨、有聚、有安，以究其極。如欲致君於堯舜之君歟，則先資其言，曰如何而陳善，如何而閉邪，凡多聞質而守之者，鑿鑿乎皆有定說矣，豈待見君而後思爲之贊襄哉？如欲澤民於堯舜之民歟，則先資其言，曰如何而熙載，如何而亮工，凡精知畧而行之者，斷斷乎已有成算矣，豈待臨民而後思爲之康濟哉？夫事君先資其言，則量而後入，非入而後量者矣。夫然後拔茅而進，以投魚水之懽，人未必不以先資之言爲筌蹄也。君子曰：「事君所貴可
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Ample and substantial.”

In serving his ruler, a minister must at the outset have words on which to draw, and ultimately have the means to put those words into practice. For speaking is not difficult; acting is what is difficult. If he does not put his words into practice, how could he serve his ruler well? The compiler of the “Record of Exemplary Conduct” meant that a fitting encounter between ruler and minister has always been difficult to achieve, and that what matters in a gentleman’s advancement is correctness. Thus, dwelling in obscurity without stealing a position, he certainly has no thought of pursuing office. Yet learning in youth provides the foundation for action in maturity; in every undertaking of ordering affairs, there are attainment, rightness, and examination [?], through which he reaches its refined essentials. Steadfast in conduct and untiring, he certainly has no intention of “setting forth southward.” Yet thoroughly investigating the classics provides the basis for practical application; in every plan for assisting the work of transformation, there are cultivation, accumulation, and settled mastery, through which he explores its utmost limits.

If he wishes to bring his ruler to the stature of Yao and Shun, he first draws upon his words: how should he set forth goodness, and how should he bar evil? In everything concerning hearing widely, testing what he hears, and holding to it, he already has definite explanations, firmly established. How could he wait until he meets his ruler before considering how to assist him? If he wishes to bestow blessings upon the people so that they become like the people of Yao and Shun, he first draws upon his words: how should he make affairs flourish, and how should he assist in accomplishing the work? In everything concerning precise understanding, grasping essentials, and putting them into practice, he already has settled plans, firmly determined. How could he wait until he governs the people before considering how to bring them peace and succor?

To draw first upon one’s words in serving a ruler is to assess one’s capacities before entering office, rather than enter office and only then assess them. Only afterward does he advance, like uprooted thatch drawing its fellows along, to enter the joyful accord of fish and water. Others may well regard the words upon which he previously drew as fish traps and rabbit snares, to be discarded once their purpose is achieved. The gentleman says: “What is prized in serving one’s ruler—one may…”

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
賤可富可貧而吾之信不可亂亂觀光而往以際
風雲之會人未必不以先資之論爲敝屣也君
子曰儒有可親可近可殺而吾之信不可辱以
君不及堯舜若撻之市也故怠則張而相之廢
則埽而更之凡廟堂之弼亮皆巖穴之脩藏也
敢曰匪彝慆淫脩之家而壞之國耶以民不如
堯舜若推之溝也故脩六禮以節之明七教以
興之凡朝著之經綸皆山林之講貫也敢曰播
敷造譽守於窮而變於達耶夫未仕也言以發
===
其藴既仕也行以踐其實此古之事君受祿不
誣而受罪益寡歟我思古人若莘野數語傅岩
三篇眞資言成信者也後世若孔明之出師表
亦庶幾乎然進以禮退以義道也行或使之止
或尼之命也使時不我遇而必於成信則若昌黎之
三上相書楊龜山之晚年一出皆足爲盛德之累噫
此出處誠聖賢之大節也安可不自珍重也哉
第貳場
論
punctuated:
賤、可富、可貧，而吾之信不可亂。亂觀光而往，以際風雲之會，人未必不以先資之論爲敝屣也。君子曰：「儒有可親、可近、可殺，而吾之信不可辱。」以君不及堯舜，若撻之市也，故怠則張而相之，廢則埽而更之。凡廟堂之弼亮，皆巖穴之脩藏也。敢曰匪彝慆淫，脩之家而壞之國耶？以民不如堯舜，若推之溝也，故脩六禮以節之，明七教以興之。凡朝著之經綸，皆山林之講貫也。敢曰播敷造譽，守於窮而變於達耶？夫未仕也，言以發其藴；既仕也，行以踐其實。此古之事君，受祿不誣而受罪益寡歟？我思古人，若莘野數語、傅岩三篇，眞資言成信者也。後世若孔明之出師表，亦庶幾乎！然進以禮，退以義，道也；行或使之，止或尼之，命也。使時不我遇而必於成信，則若昌黎之三上相書、楊龜山之晚年一出，皆足爲盛德之累。噫！此出處誠聖賢之大節也，安可不自珍重也哉！

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…be held lowly, be made wealthy, or be made poor, but my trustworthiness cannot be shaken. [The repeated character here is doubtful: ?] When one goes forth to behold the realm’s splendor and encounters an auspicious meeting of ruler and minister, others may well regard the principles drawn upon beforehand as worn-out sandals to be discarded. The gentleman says: “A scholar may be befriended, approached, or killed, but my trustworthiness cannot be dishonored.” He regards his ruler’s failure to equal Yao and Shun as though he himself were being flogged in the marketplace. Thus, when the ruler grows remiss, he rouses and assists him; when affairs fall into neglect, he clears away abuses and renews them. All the assistance he renders at court comes from what he cultivated and stored up in seclusion among cliffs and caves. Would he dare indulge in misconduct and excess, cultivating himself at home only to undo that cultivation in governing the state? He regards the people’s failure to equal the people of Yao and Shun as though he himself were pushing them into a ditch. Thus he cultivates the six rites to regulate them and elucidates the seven teachings to uplift them. All his ordering of affairs at court comes from what he studied and mastered in the mountains and forests. Would he dare spread claims to manufacture a reputation, keeping his principles in obscurity but changing them upon attaining prominence?

Before taking office, one uses words to reveal what one holds within; after taking office, one uses conduct to put their substance into practice. Was this how those who served rulers in antiquity received stipends without deception and incurred ever fewer punishments? When I think of the ancients—the few words spoken in the fields of Shen and the three chapters associated with Fu Yan—they truly drew upon their words and fulfilled their pledges. In later ages, Kongming’s Memorial on Dispatching the Army came close to this as well! Yet advancing according to ritual propriety and withdrawing according to righteousness belong to the Way; whether something causes one to act or prevents one from acting belongs to fate. If the times afford me no opportunity, yet I insist on fulfilling my pledges, then cases such as Changli’s three letters submitted to the chief councilor and Yang Guishan’s emergence into office in his late years suffice to show how this can blemish eminent virtue. Alas! Taking office or remaining in retirement is truly a matter of cardinal principle for sages and worthies. How could one fail to cherish and safeguard one’s integrity?

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
君子以人治人
張九思
同考試官教諭張　批〔學治人教者教脩於道道率於性□□能〕
〔作終篇不離此意要是本色議論騁浮詞而鮮實味者□□下矣録之以式作者〕
考試官學正毛　批〔題本平易驟揚中作者率浮泛膚謭〕
〔使人讀求終篇而此作獨□□雅健且無一字無來歷乃大手筆也秋〕
考試官教授林　批〔有發揮〕
〔闈高選非子其誰〕
君子脩道以教人所以畏天命而悲人窮也夫
===
人受天地之中以生是人無弗具乎道也無弗
率乎性也而何俟君子之立教也哉蓋二氣交
運五行雜揉於是氣質有昏明强弱紛然雜出
於天下矣就其中言之昏弱者固戾天拂性而
不可與爲道其明者强者亦質之近似而陷於
一偏至此則人道於是乎窮而君子脩道之教
自不容已矣然君子豈樂爲如是之勞心哉天
以聰明睿智之資而私厚之是以經綸事業累
之也是故率性以澄源脩道以昭軌而人之弗
punctuated:
君子以人治人
張九思
同考試官教諭張，批〔學治人教者，教脩於道，道率於性，□□能〕〔作終篇不離此意，要是本色議論。騁浮詞而鮮實味者，□□下矣。録之以式作者。〕
考試官學正毛，批〔題本平易，驟揚中作者率浮泛膚謭〕〔使人讀求終篇，而此作獨□□雅健，且無一字無來歷，乃大手筆也。秋〕
考試官教授林，批〔有發揮〕〔闈高選，非子其誰？〕
君子脩道以教人，所以畏天命而悲人窮也。夫人受天地之中以生，是人無弗具乎道也，無弗率乎性也，而何俟君子之立教也哉？蓋二氣交運，五行雜揉，於是氣質有昏明强弱，紛然雜出於天下矣。就其中言之，昏弱者固戾天拂性，而不可與爲道；其明者强者，亦質之近似，而陷於一偏。至此，則人道於是乎窮，而君子脩道之教自不容已矣。然君子豈樂爲如是之勞心哉？天以聰明睿智之資而私厚之，是以經綸事業累之也。是故率性以澄源，脩道以昭軌，而人之弗
translation_en:
The Gentleman Governs People by What Is Human in Them
Zhang Jiusi

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Learning, governing people, and teaching [?]: teaching consists in cultivating the Way, and the Way consists in following human nature. □□ can…〕〔Throughout the composition, the author never departs from this idea; this is, in essence, authentic argument. Those who parade empty phrases with little substantive meaning are □□ inferior. It is recorded here as a model for writers.〕

Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is straightforward, but the compositions produced amid the bustle of the examination [?] are generally superficial and shallow.〕〔They make the reader seek the end of the piece [?], whereas this composition alone is □□ refined and vigorous. Moreover, not a single word lacks a source: this is the work of a master. Autumn…〕

Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔It develops the meaning.〕〔…a high selection in the examination: who but you?〕 [The transcription appears to divide “autumn examination” between the preceding comments.]

The gentleman cultivates the Way to teach others because he reveres Heaven’s mandate and grieves over people’s plight. Now, people are born endowed with the balanced principle of Heaven and Earth. Thus no one lacks the Way, and no one fails to follow their nature. Why, then, must they await the gentleman’s establishment of teaching? It is because the two vital forces operate together and the Five Phases intermingle. Consequently, material dispositions—clouded or clear, strong or weak—arise throughout the world in bewildering variety. Among these, the clouded and weak certainly oppose Heaven and contravene their nature, and cannot be partners in practicing the Way. Yet even those who are clear or strong have dispositions that merely approximate it and fall into partiality. At this point, the human Way reaches an impasse, and the gentleman’s teaching through cultivation of the Way becomes indispensable.

Yet does the gentleman delight in such taxing exertion of his mind? Heaven has especially favored him with the endowments of perceptiveness and wisdom, thereby burdening him with the work of ordering the world. Thus he follows human nature to clarify the source and cultivates the Way to make the proper course manifest; and as for people who fail to…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
若於訓弗協於極者鮮矣吾是以知人不知所
以自治也而望諸天天不能以治人也而責之
君子之一身則君子者負範圍曲成之責蓋有
推之而不能去者矣而人之所以翕然大順者
亦皆能知能行之道自然而然顧豈強其所本
無而責之以所難從哉請攄予思予未發之說
乾剛坤柔天地定矣屯難蒙昧人物出矣需以
飲食訟以爭鬭師以征伐此風氣漸闢事變多
奸而人道於是乎窮矣然有一人則有一人之
===
道雖其私欲橫流之中而本體之澄徹元貞之
渾厚何嘗遽爲之泯滅澌盡哉故聖人序卦師
之後必次之以王用三驅之比蓋謂天佑下民
故作之君師以相上帝撫且人之道何道也吾
見其冲然穆矣淵然深矣燦然析矣渾然壨矣
是乃天之載乎地之紀乎日月之精乎山川之
秀乎鬼神之能乎陰陽之用乎洪纖之化乎然
道發揚詡物者也故精也而實粗也遠也而實
近也大也而實細也微也而實顯也今夫人之
punctuated: 若於訓、弗協於極者鮮矣。吾是以知，人不知所以自治也，而望諸天；天不能以治人也，而責之君子之一身。則君子者，負範圍曲成之責，蓋有推之而不能去者矣。而人之所以翕然大順者，亦皆能知能行之道，自然而然，顧豈強其所本無，而責之以所難從哉？請攄予思，予未發之說。乾剛坤柔，天地定矣；屯難蒙昧，人物出矣；需以飲食，訟以爭鬭，師以征伐。此風氣漸闢，事變多奸，而人道於是乎窮矣。然有一人，則有一人之道。雖其私欲橫流之中，而本體之澄徹、元貞之渾厚，何嘗遽爲之泯滅澌盡哉？故聖人序卦，師之後必次之以王用三驅之比，蓋謂「天佑下民，故作之君師，以相上帝撫且」。人之道何道也？吾見其冲然穆矣，淵然深矣，燦然析矣，渾然壨矣。是乃天之載乎？地之紀乎？日月之精乎？山川之秀乎？鬼神之能乎？陰陽之用乎？洪纖之化乎？然道發揚詡物者也，故精也而實粗也，遠也而實近也，大也而實細也，微也而實顯也。今夫人之
translation_en:
…those who fail to follow instruction or conform to the supreme standard are few. From this I know that people, not knowing how to govern themselves, look to Heaven; yet Heaven cannot itself govern people, and the responsibility is placed upon the gentleman alone. The gentleman thus bears responsibility for ordering all things and bringing each to fulfillment in its particular circumstances—a responsibility he cannot cast off, however he might try. Moreover, the Way through which people unite in willing obedience is one they can all know and practice, naturally and spontaneously. How could it compel them to possess what they originally lacked, or demand that they follow what is difficult to obey? Let me unfold my thoughts and the explanation I have not yet expressed.

Qian is firm and Kun yielding: Heaven and Earth are established. Zhun signifies difficulty and Meng obscurity: people and things emerge. Xu concerns food and drink, Song contention, and Shi military campaigns. Thus, as prevailing conditions gradually develop, changing affairs give rise to much wrongdoing, and the human Way reaches an impasse. Yet wherever there is a person, there is the Way proper to that person. Even amid the unchecked torrent of selfish desires, how could the clarity of the original substance and the abundant integrity of primal goodness and steadfastness suddenly be obliterated and utterly exhausted? Thus, when the sage arranged the hexagrams, he invariably placed after Shi (The Army) the hexagram Bi (Holding Together), with its phrase, “The king employs a three-sided drive in the hunt.” The meaning is that “Heaven protects the common people, and therefore establishes rulers and teachers for them, to assist the Lord on High in nurturing [them?].”

What Way is this human Way? I see its serene reverence, its profound depth, its luminous distinctions, and its integral fullness [?]. Is this what Heaven sustains? The ordering pattern of Earth? The essence of sun and moon? The finest qualities of mountains and rivers? The powers of ghosts and spirits? The operation of yin and yang? The transformation of things great and small? Yet the Way unfolds and nurtures things. Thus, though refined, it is in fact also coarse; though distant, it is in fact near; though great, it is in fact minute; though subtle, it is in fact manifest. Now, as for the human…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道其倫君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友唯厥中其情
惻隱羞惡辭讓是非唯厥和其用則絲麻布帛
鐘鼓黍稷醴酪魚禽唯厥文其事則俯仰進退
升降闔闢張弛動靜唯厥質無是人則無是道
有是道未嘗不寓於人也使君子事事物物不
爲品節裁制而立法於天下則相戕相靡相攻
相取而勢窮矣而況能代天理物以對于天下
哉然則天之所以厚我者何如而可若此也嗚
呼此君子之立教其綱領安得不大節目安得
===
不詳哉是故教父子以蓼莪教上下以淇澳教
夫婦以關雎教兄弟以棠棣教朋友以伐木猶
未已也而教之以知仁聖義中和以正其趨教
之以孝友敬敏任恤以善其則教之以禮樂射
御書數以博其趣猶未已也而以祭祀教敬以
婚姻教親以鄉飲教讓以燕享教和太師陳詩
以教能命市納賈以教信考時同律以教同以
宮室車旗教辨以鄰鄙都鄙里教聯以保葬賙賓
教恤若此似可率民而歸之道也君子則曰禹
punctuated:
道，其倫君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友，唯厥中；其情惻隱、羞惡、辭讓、是非，唯厥和；其用則絲麻、布帛、鐘鼓、黍稷、醴酪、魚禽，唯厥文；其事則俯仰、進退、升降、闔闢、張弛、動靜，唯厥質。無是人則無是道，有是道未嘗不寓於人也。使君子事事物物不爲品節裁制而立法於天下，則相戕相靡，相攻相取，而勢窮矣，而況能代天理物以對于天下哉？然則天之所以厚我者何如，而可若此也？嗚呼！此君子之立教，其綱領安得不大，節目安得不詳哉？
是故教父子以《蓼莪》，教上下以《淇澳》，教夫婦以《關雎》，教兄弟以《棠棣》，教朋友以《伐木》。猶未已也，而教之以知、仁、聖、義、中、和，以正其趨；教之以孝、友、敬、敏、任、恤，以善其則；教之以禮、樂、射、御、書、數，以博其趣。猶未已也，而以祭祀教敬，以婚姻教親，以鄉飲教讓，以燕享教和。太師陳詩以教能，命市納賈以教信，考時同律以教同，以宮室車旗教辨，以鄰鄙都鄙里教聯，以保葬賙賓教恤。若此，似可率民而歸之道也。君子則曰：「禹
translation_en:
…the Way of human beings: in its relationships—ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend—it requires due balance. In its feelings—compassion, shame and aversion to wrongdoing, deference, and discernment of right and wrong—it requires harmony. In its implements and provisions—silk and hemp, cloth and silk fabrics, bells and drums, millet and grain, sweet wine and curds, fish and fowl—it requires refinement. In its activities—bowing and looking up, advancing and withdrawing, ascending and descending, closing and opening, tightening and relaxing, moving and resting—it requires substance. Without these human beings, there would be no such Way; wherever this Way exists, it invariably resides in human beings. If the gentleman did not establish appropriate distinctions and regulations for every affair and thing, thereby setting standards for all under Heaven, people would injure and wear one another down, attack and plunder one another, until their circumstances reached an impasse. How much less could he order things on Heaven’s behalf and answer to all under Heaven? How great, then, is the bounty Heaven has bestowed upon us—and how could we act thus? Alas! When the gentleman establishes instruction, how could its guiding principles fail to be broad, or its detailed provisions fail to be comprehensive?
Thus fathers and sons are taught through “The Tall Southernwood” (Liao e); superiors and subordinates through “The Bends of the Qi” (Qi ao); husbands and wives through “The Ospreys Cry” (Guan ju); brothers through “The Cherry Tree” (Chang di); and friends through “Felling Trees” (Fa mu). Nor does instruction end there. People are taught wisdom, benevolence, sagacity, righteousness, balance, and harmony to set their aspirations right; filial piety, brotherly affection, respectfulness, diligence, trustworthiness, and compassion to improve their standards of conduct; and ritual, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and calculation to broaden their pursuits. Nor does instruction end there. Sacrifices teach reverence; marriage teaches affection; village drinking ceremonies teach deference; and banquets teach harmony. The Grand Music Master presents poems to teach competence; markets are ordered to report prices to teach good faith; the seasons are examined and the pitch standards brought into agreement to teach concord. Palaces and dwellings, carriages and banners teach distinctions; neighborhood and territorial groupings [?] teach mutual association; protection, burial, relief, and hospitality [?] teach solicitude. With such measures, it would seem possible to lead the people back to the Way. Yet the gentleman says: “Yu…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之民已不及堯舜矣世變猶江河也容可不先
事爲隄防哉故有東膠上庠以作之有讀法木
鐸以震之有保氏司諫以匡之有宵雅以誘之
有皷篋以警之有射侯以明之有夏楚以記之
有宅里風聲以樹之有造士選士以彰之有移
郊移遂以懲之有五禁八成以威之如是而以
人治人之道盡乎曰末也天下之人不皆誦詩
讀書之人也農工商賈嬪婦臣妾是亦人也而
所以治之亦必教之生九穀毓園圃藩藪牧餙
===
八材通貨賄化絲枲斂疏材轉執事凡此其事
最粗淺也而亦皆量其人稽其敘辦其能趨其
功脩其政是精粗微顯大小遠近皆兼體而不
偏是故可以惇典可以定倫可以陶情可以粹
性可以厚生可以錫類故乾無亢坤無戰屯無
邅蒙無寇需無災訟無逋師無次是故公卿大
夫式於朝王伯亞疆媚於野元適俊秀興於學
夫婦昆季諧於家賔旅男女讓於途工匠商賈
平於市蠻流鎮藩賔於庭敷天之下其教昭如
punctuated: 之民已不及堯舜矣。世變猶江河也，容可不先事爲隄防哉？故有東膠上庠以作之，有讀法木鐸以震之，有保氏司諫以匡之，有宵雅以誘之，有皷篋以警之，有射侯以明之，有夏楚以記之，有宅里風聲以樹之，有造士選士以彰之，有移郊移遂以懲之，有五禁八成以威之。如是而以人治人之道盡乎？曰：末也。天下之人不皆誦詩讀書之人也，農工商賈嬪婦臣妾，是亦人也，而所以治之亦必教之。生九穀，毓園圃，藩藪牧，餙八材，通貨賄，化絲枲，斂疏材，轉執事，凡此其事最粗淺也，而亦皆量其人，稽其敘，辦其能，趨其功，脩其政。是精粗微顯大小遠近，皆兼體而不偏。是故可以惇典，可以定倫，可以陶情，可以粹性，可以厚生，可以錫類。故乾無亢，坤無戰，屯無邅，蒙無寇，需無災，訟無逋，師無次。是故公卿大夫式於朝，王伯亞疆媚於野，元適俊秀興於學，夫婦昆季諧於家，賔旅男女讓於途，工匠商賈平於市，蠻流鎮藩賔於庭。敷天之下，其教昭如
translation_en:
…the people under his rule already fell short of those under Yao and Shun. Changes in the world are like rivers in flow: can one possibly fail to build embankments before trouble arises? Thus there were the Eastern School and Upper School to rouse them; readings of the laws and the wooden-tongued bell to stir them; the Guardian and the Remonstrance Official to correct them; the Lesser Odes to guide them; the beating of the drum and opening of book boxes to alert them; archery targets to enlighten them; and the birch and thorn rods to impress lessons upon them. There were the examples and reputations of their local communities to establish them; the advancement and selection of scholars to distinguish them; transfers to the suburbs and outer districts to punish them; and the five prohibitions and eight established regulations to awe them. With these measures, is the Way of governing people as people exhausted? The answer is: not yet [?].

Not everyone in the world recites the Odes and reads the Documents. Farmers, artisans, merchants, women engaged in household work, and male and female bondservants are people too; governing them likewise necessarily entails teaching them. Growing the nine grains, tending gardens and orchards, raising animals in marshes and pastures [?], working the eight materials, circulating goods and valuables, processing silk and hemp, gathering plants and other materials, and moving between tasks as hired laborers—all these activities are exceedingly humble and simple. Yet in each case, one must assess the people, examine their ranks, distinguish their abilities, urge on their achievements, and put their administration in order. Thus the refined and the coarse, the hidden and the manifest, the great and the small, the distant and the near are all embraced without partiality. In this way one can uphold the enduring norms, establish human relationships, mold the feelings, purify human nature, enrich livelihoods, and extend blessings to others of one’s kind.

Thus, in the terms of the Changes, Qian has no overreaching, Kun no battle, Zhun no faltering, Meng no raiders, Xu no disaster, Song no flight, and Shi no encampment in retreat. Accordingly, dukes, ministers, and great officers serve as models at court; kings, regional chiefs, and subordinate leaders [?] enjoy favor in the countryside; principal heirs and outstanding youths [?] flourish in the schools; husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers live harmoniously at home; guests and travelers, men and women yield to one another on the roads; artisans and merchants deal fairly in the markets; and the peoples of the Man, Liu, Zhen, and Fan outer domains attend court as guests. Everywhere beneath Heaven, this teaching shines forth…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其化沛如故凡仁敬慈孝和義柔婉友恭信規
庶幾不違之謂中矣凡忿懥恐懼憂患親愛畏
敬哀矜庶幾不愆之謂和矣凡犧牲鼎鼐俎簠簋
籩豆琴瑟管磬庶幾成章之謂文矣凡祭祀喪
蜡射獮吉凶軍賓庶幾中節之謂質矣是真所
謂不識不知順帝之則遵王之路無黨無偏者
矣豈惟人也天地昭其觀日月麗其明山川永
其寧鬼神顯其歆陰陽布其順洪纖遂其育皆
以人治人之克拓也君子經綸之功如此則可
===
以答天心立民命矣是豈求之性分之外哉蓋
道人之所有也以其所固有而教之則觸之即
應感之即通固有莫之爲而爲者矣記曰人情
聖王之田也人情之田即道也性也君子以人
治之是乃脩禮以爲耕陳義以爲種本仁以爲
聚播樂以爲安而要之實講學爲耨之所致也
向使君子恃天聰明之盡而不加戒謹愼獨之
功則安能脩道立教之明效大驗至此哉雖然
堯舜性之也湯武反之也然堯學於務成昭舜
punctuated: 其化沛如。故凡仁敬慈孝、和義柔婉、友恭信規，庶幾不違之謂中矣；凡忿懥恐懼、憂患親愛、畏敬哀矜，庶幾不愆之謂和矣；凡犧牲鼎鼐、俎簠簋、籩豆、琴瑟管磬，庶幾成章之謂文矣；凡祭祀喪蜡、射獮、吉凶軍賓，庶幾中節之謂質矣。是真所謂「不識不知，順帝之則」、「遵王之路，無黨無偏」者矣。豈惟人也？天地昭其觀，日月麗其明，山川永其寧，鬼神顯其歆，陰陽布其順，洪纖遂其育，皆以人治人之克拓也。君子經綸之功如此，則可以答天心、立民命矣。是豈求之性分之外哉？蓋道，人之所有也。以其所固有而教之，則觸之即應，感之即通，固有莫之爲而爲者矣。《記》曰：「人情，聖王之田也。」人情之田，即道也，性也。君子以人治之，是乃脩禮以爲耕，陳義以爲種，本仁以爲聚，播樂以爲安，而要之，實講學爲耨之所致也。向使君子恃天聰明之盡，而不加戒謹愼獨之功，則安能脩道立教之明效大驗至此哉？雖然，堯舜性之也，湯武反之也。然堯學於務成昭，舜
translation_en:
…its transforming influence flows abundantly. Thus, in benevolence, reverence, parental kindness, filial devotion, harmony, righteousness, gentleness, graciousness, brotherly affection, respect, trustworthiness, and admonition, approaching freedom from deviation is called centrality. In anger, fear, anxiety, affection, awe, respect, sorrow, and compassion, approaching freedom from excess or error is called harmony. In sacrificial animals, cooking cauldrons, offering stands, grain vessels, bamboo baskets, pedestal dishes, zithers, pipes, and chime stones, approaching an ordered pattern is called cultural refinement. In sacrifices, mourning rites, year-end agricultural sacrifices, archery, autumn hunts, and auspicious, inauspicious, military, and guest ceremonies, approaching the proper measure is called substance. This truly is what is meant by “Without conscious knowledge or awareness, following the Lord on High’s pattern,” and “Following the king’s road, without faction or partiality.”

And is this confined to human beings? Heaven and earth display their spectacle clearly; the sun and moon shine with their radiance; mountains and rivers perpetuate their tranquility; ghosts and spirits manifest their acceptance of offerings; yin and yang spread their harmonious influences; and things great and small fulfill their growth. All this comes from extending the practice of governing people according to their own humanity. When the noble man’s work of ordering the world reaches this extent, he can answer Heaven’s intentions and establish the people’s livelihood. How could this require seeking anything outside one’s allotted nature? The Way is something people already possess. If they are taught through what is inherently theirs, they respond as soon as they are touched and understand as soon as they are moved. There are indeed things that come about without anyone deliberately bringing them about.

The Record of Rites says: “Human feelings are the field of the sage king.” This field of human feelings is precisely the Way, precisely human nature. When the noble man governs it according to humanity, he cultivates ritual as his plowing, sets forth righteousness as his sowing, roots himself in benevolence as his gathering, and spreads music as his means of bringing repose. Ultimately, however, this is achieved through the weeding that consists in discussing and pursuing learning. Had the noble man relied on the fullness of his Heaven-given intelligence [?], without adding the effort of vigilance, caution, and watchfulness over himself when alone, how could the clear results and great proofs of cultivating the Way and establishing instruction have reached such a degree?

Even so, Yao and Shun possessed this by nature; Tang and Wu returned to it through cultivation. Yet Yao studied under Wucheng Zhao, and Shun…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
學於君疇則雖大聖亦從事於學矣是故爲治
則曰帥仁曰德先曰綏猷曰陳常而其效至於
時雍風動不距輯寧永清蓋有天德則有王道
自有不可誣者而要之皆天爲之也竊怪後世
佛老以虛無寂滅鳴管商以權謀術數顯道於
是而益晦民於是而益窮豈天無意於斯人哉
天之所以責望君子時蓋有待也而君子之能
當其責以答天心以立民命者亦豈可以多得
哉吾於是乎有感
===
表
擬宋以范仲淹兼知延州謝表〔康定　元年〕
王士吉
同考試官教諭章　批〔撰語忠壯激奮有承元昊犖〕〔西夏之勢使希文自爲之不過鉅〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔表中說出仲淹經理西事〕〔殷實詳悉而忠愛溢於言表且駢儷得體宜錄以式〕
作者
考試官學正毛　批〔寓規諷於稱謝中表之可式者也〕
punctuated:
學於君疇，則雖大聖，亦從事於學矣。是故爲治，則曰帥仁，曰德先，曰綏猷，曰陳常，而其效至於時雍、風動、不距、輯寧、永清。蓋有天德，則有王道，自有不可誣者，而要之，皆天爲之也。竊怪後世佛老以虛無寂滅鳴，管商以權謀術數顯，道於是而益晦，民於是而益窮。豈天無意於斯人哉？天之所以責望君子，時蓋有待也；而君子之能當其責，以答天心，以立民命者，亦豈可以多得哉？吾於是乎有感。

表
擬宋以范仲淹兼知延州謝表〔康定元年〕
王士吉

同考試官教諭章，批〔撰語忠壯激奮，有承元昊犖〕〔西夏之勢，使希文自爲之，不過鉅〕。

同考試官教諭黃，批〔表中說出仲淹經理西事〕〔殷實詳悉，而忠愛溢於言表，且駢儷得體，宜錄以式〕作者。

考試官學正毛，批〔寓規諷於稱謝中，表之可式者也〕。
translation_en:
…studied under Jun Chou; thus even the greatest sages devoted themselves to learning. Hence, in governing, they spoke of leading through benevolence, taking virtue as the foremost guide, bringing peace through sound policies, and setting forth the constant norms. Their achievements extended to universal concord, transformation as if moved by the wind, the absence of resistance, settled peace, and lasting tranquillity. Where there is heavenly virtue, there is the Kingly Way: this is something that cannot be gainsaid. Ultimately, however, all of it is Heaven’s doing. I find it strange that in later ages the Buddhists and Daoists won renown through emptiness and extinction, while Guan Zhong and Shang Yang gained prominence through expedient schemes and manipulative techniques. The Way consequently became ever more obscure, and the people ever more impoverished. Could Heaven be indifferent to these people? In placing its expectations upon the gentleman, Heaven surely awaits the proper time. Yet how often can one find a gentleman able to shoulder that responsibility, answer Heaven’s intentions, and secure the people’s livelihood? At this I am deeply moved.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the Song appointment of Fan Zhongyan concurrently as Prefect of Yanzhou. 〔First year of Kangding (1040).〕
By Wang Shiji.

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is loyal, bold, and stirring. It conveys the force of confronting Yuanhao and Western Xia [?]. Even if Xiwen [Fan Zhongyan] had written it himself, he could not have surpassed this [?].〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The memorial describes Zhongyan’s management of affairs in the west substantively and in full detail. Loyalty and devotion overflow its words, and its parallel prose is appropriately composed. It should be recorded as a model〕 for writers.

Examiner Mao, School Instructor, comments: 〔It embeds admonition within expressions of thanks: a memorial worthy of serving as a model.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批〔表生〕
康定元年〔某〕月〔某〕日具官〔臣〕仲淹北蒙
聖恩以招討使兼知延州者〔臣〕誠惶誠恐稽首
頓首上言
伏以玉帳銅符飛風霜乎重鎮隼旗熊軾
施雨露於專城老將鳴劍馳伊吾欲驅榻
邊之鼾睡循吏解繩平渤海將救赤子於
潢池顧文武之兼官亶軍民之重柄非壯
猷之方叔幾於野鶴乘軒必全節之郭公
===
是謂熊羆當道方
今西事燃眉之急萬竈雲屯顧此延州累卵之
危孤城斗絕稽分野昔為白翟至天寶更
延安郡之名慨元昊今益跳梁雖范雍坐
保安軍之敗遊士門之寨嘆李將軍之不
得封侯登祁儺之臺思霍驃騎之無心治
第鄜川漾秀忍聽採花之歌延水涵清怒
觀救鴿之怪彼重圍解於雪夜強虜遁於
燈宵是蓋
punctuated:
考試官教授林，批〔表生〕。
康定元年〔某〕月〔某〕日，具官〔臣〕仲淹北蒙聖恩，以招討使兼知延州者。〔臣〕誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：
伏以玉帳銅符，飛風霜乎重鎮；隼旗熊軾，施雨露於專城。老將鳴劍馳伊吾，欲驅榻邊之鼾睡；循吏解繩平渤海，將救赤子於潢池。顧文武之兼官，亶軍民之重柄。非壯猷之方叔，幾於野鶴乘軒；必全節之郭公，是謂熊羆當道。
方今西事燃眉之急，萬竈雲屯；顧此延州累卵之危，孤城斗絕。稽分野，昔為白翟；至天寶，更延安郡之名。慨元昊今益跳梁，雖范雍坐保安軍之敗。遊士門之寨，嘆李將軍之不得封侯；登祁儺之臺，思霍驃騎之無心治第。鄜川漾秀，忍聽採花之歌；延水涵清，怒觀救鴿之怪。彼重圍解於雪夜，強虜遁於燈宵，是蓋
translation_en:
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔The memorial is lively [?].〕
On the 〔specified〕 day of the 〔specified〕 month of the first year of Kangding, your servant Zhongyan, holding the requisite offices, received [?] imperial favor and was appointed Commissioner for Pacification concurrently serving as Prefect of Yanzhou. Your servant, in utmost fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly prostrates himself, submitting this memorial:
I humbly consider that the commander's splendid tent and bronze credentials spread the stern authority of wind and frost over a strategic stronghold; the falcon banner and bear-decorated carriage extend the beneficence of rain and dew over a city entrusted to sole command. The veteran general, his sword ringing, gallops toward Yiwu, intent on driving away those who snore beside our couch. The benevolent administrator loosens the bonds of punishment and pacifies Bohai, seeking to rescue the people, like innocent children, from rebellion. An office combining civil and military duties indeed carries weighty authority over soldiers and civilians alike. Without the bold strategy of Fang Shu, its occupant would be little better than a wild crane riding in a dignitary's carriage. Only someone of Lord Guo's unimpaired integrity deserves to be called a mighty bear guarding the road.
At present, affairs on the western frontier are as urgent as flames at one's eyebrows: myriad campfires cluster like clouds. Here in Yanzhou, the danger is that of piled eggs; the solitary city stands steep and isolated. Examining the region's territorial divisions, it was formerly the land of the Baidi; in the Tianbao era its designation was changed to Yan'an Commandery. Alas, Yuanhao now grows ever more unruly, though Fan Yong has been held responsible for the defeat at Bao'an Military Prefecture [?]. Visiting the stockade at Shimen, I lament that General Li never received enfeoffment as a marquis; ascending the terrace at Qinuo [?], I recall how Huo, General of Agile Cavalry, had no inclination to build himself a mansion. The waters of Fuchuan ripple beautifully: how can one bear to hear the song of gathering flowers? The Yan River holds clear waters: with anger I regard the strange tale of rescuing a dove [?]. That the tight siege was lifted on a snowy night, and that the formidable enemy fled on the night of the Lantern Festival—this surely was …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天心降康欲挽銀河以洗甲兵之饑詎期
日旰忘食乃聞鼙鼓而思將帥之遺在饒方
受
神環遽參外闔至陝未温坐席復辱彤襜喜
溢蓬瀛光生草木茲葢伏遇
○○○
晉明出地
離照當天繩
祖武而重道崇儒固邦本而忍飢却貢寧用購
首二千錢之將深知稼穡之艱難何信蟠
===
胷十萬兵之名繆降
絲綸而寵疊是固
神武不殺兩階舞干羽之儀豈知夷狄無情
數載困疆場之備在丈夫當鷹揚鷙擊直
擣賀蘭山頭彼醜虜葢豨突狼奔反取金明
砦口此其志欲長驅席捲及此時宜固守
隄防唯充國謀在萬全是謂老成持重若
諸葛兵至七縱葢長亂賊奸雄在
punctuated: 天心降康，欲挽銀河以洗甲兵之饑。詎期日旰忘食，乃聞鼙鼓而思將帥之遺。在饒方受神環，遽參外闔；至陝未温坐席，復辱彤襜。喜溢蓬瀛，光生草木。茲葢伏遇○○○，晉明出地，離照當天，繩祖武而重道崇儒，固邦本而忍飢却貢。寧用購首二千錢之將，深知稼穡之艱難；何信蟠胷十萬兵之名，繆降絲綸而寵疊。是固神武不殺，兩階舞干羽之儀；豈知夷狄無情，數載困疆場之備。在丈夫當鷹揚鷙擊，直擣賀蘭山頭；彼醜虜葢豨突狼奔，反取金明砦口。此其志欲長驅席捲，及此時宜固守隄防。唯充國謀在萬全，是謂老成持重；若諸葛兵至七縱，葢長亂賊奸雄。在
translation_en:
…Heaven’s will bestowed peace, wishing to draw down the River of Heaven to wash away the hunger of arms and armor [?]. Who could have expected that, forgetting to eat until late in the day, Your Majesty would hear the war drums and think of overlooked commanders? While in Rao, I had just received the imperial ring of recall [?] and hastened to attend at the outer palace gate. On reaching Shaanxi, before I had even warmed my seat, I was again honored by the arrival of an imperial envoy’s red-curtained carriage. Joy overflowed through Penglai and Yingzhou, and radiance shone upon the grasses and trees.

This was because I humbly encountered ○○○: Your Majesty’s brightness rises above the earth, as in the hexagram Jin; your radiance illuminates the heavens, as in Li. Following your ancestors’ footsteps, you honor the Way and exalt Confucian learning; securing the foundations of the state, you endure hunger and decline tribute. You would employ even a general whose head carried a price of two thousand cash, profoundly understanding the hardships of sowing and reaping. Why trust the reputation of one said to hold a hundred thousand soldiers within his breast? Yet you have undeservedly sent down imperial commands, heaping favor upon me. This is indeed divine martial power that does not kill—the ceremony of dancing with shields and plumes between the two stairways. Yet who could have known that the foreign peoples would show no feeling, leaving the frontier defenses sorely pressed for several years?

A man should soar like an eagle and strike like a hawk [?], driving straight to the heights of the Helan Mountains. Those vile enemies, however, charged like boars and ran like wolves, instead capturing the entrance to Jinming Stockade. Their intention is to drive deep into our territory and sweep everything before them; at this moment, we should hold firm and strengthen our defenses. Chongguo’s plans sought complete security: this is what is meant by seasoned judgment and caution. But when Zhuge’s campaigns went so far as to release the enemy seven times, this only nurtured rebels and treacherous strongmen. Under [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖明巳洞燭乎邊情故愚臣乃濫叨乎兵柄循
墻莫遂覆餗何堪竊念臣性唯粗直饘粥
亦巳備嘗志在先憂園林胡敢封殖顧迂
踈而效螢爝何增
日月之光明乃往瞀以披
龍鱗頓喜
雷霆之開霽調官京兆盍懷蹇蹇之匪躬落
職江南將傚優優之布政愧四圖空獻悞
厠四賢之歌甘一筆行勾遑恤一家之哭
===
推麥舟之五百頒善飯之將而結其心第
徠移庫絹之三千散挾纊之軍以作其氣
以增築如明珠漱藏諸族可推赤心而招
勝以老逆鋒若細腰胡盧等營欲遣部將
其不意以斷來路更兼練兵積粟先爲莫
納汚藏垢容試錯節盤根大要建堡脩城出
天章閣賜筆無爲甘江湖之蓼終廢仰荷
宮莫再懃葵藿之忱久違
烏昧草進
punctuated:
聖明巳洞燭乎邊情，故愚臣乃濫叨乎兵柄。循墻莫遂，覆餗何堪？竊念臣性唯粗直，饘粥亦巳備嘗；志在先憂，園林胡敢封殖？顧迂踈而效螢爝，何增日月之光明？乃往瞀以披龍鱗，頓喜雷霆之開霽。調官京兆，盍懷蹇蹇之匪躬？落職江南，將傚優優之布政。愧四圖空獻，悞厠四賢之歌；甘一筆行勾，遑恤一家之哭？
推麥舟之五百，頒善飯之將而結其心；第徠移庫絹之三千，散挾纊之軍以作其氣。以增築如明珠、漱藏諸族，可推赤心而招勝；以老逆鋒，若細腰、胡盧等營，欲遣部將，其不意以斷來路。更兼練兵積粟，先爲莫納汚藏垢，容試錯節盤根。大要建堡脩城，出天章閣賜筆，無爲甘江湖之蓼，終廢仰荷宮莫再懃葵藿之忱，久違烏昧草進。
translation_en:
…Your sagely intelligence has already clearly discerned conditions on the frontier; thus your foolish servant has undeservedly been entrusted with military command. I could not achieve my wish to decline the appointment with due humility; how could I bear to overturn the sacrificial cauldron through failure in office? I reflect that my disposition is merely blunt and straightforward, and I have fully tasted a life sustained by gruel. My resolve is to be first to take on anxiety for the realm: how would I dare enlarge my private gardens and estates? Yet, inept and impractical, I offer only the light of a firefly or a little torch—what can that add to the radiance of sun and moon? Previously, in my blindness, I ventured to touch the dragon’s scales by remonstrating; suddenly, to my joy, your thunderous anger cleared. Transferred to office in Jingzhao, how could I fail to cherish unswerving devotion without regard for myself? Stripped of office and sent to Jiangnan, I would emulate a generous and measured administration. I am ashamed that my four diagrams were offered in vain and that I was mistakenly included in the song of the Four Worthies. I willingly accept striking out a name with a single stroke of the brush: how could I spare concern for the weeping of one household?
Following the example of the boatload of five hundred measures of wheat, I would distribute provisions to the generals who eat heartily and thereby win their hearts. Then [?], transferring three thousand lengths of silk from the treasury, I would distribute them among the troops, warming them as though they wore padded clothes, and thus raise their spirits. As for additional construction and such tribes as the Mingzhu and Shuzang [?], we could offer utter sincerity and summon them to allegiance and victory [?], thereby wearing down the rebels’ offensive. For encampments such as Xiyao and Hulu, I wish to dispatch subordinate commanders to take them unawares and cut off their approach routes. Furthermore, we should train troops and accumulate grain, first making preparations [?]. Bearing with impurity and concealing faults, allow me to try my ability against tangled roots and knotted joints—that is, difficult affairs. The essential point is to build forts and repair walls. Bring forth the brush bestowed at the Tianzhang Pavilion [?]; do not let me remain forever cast aside, enduring the bitterness of life far from court [?]. Looking up in gratitude for imperial favor, I would again exert my loyalty, like the mallow turning toward the sun [?]. Long absent … ‘darkness, hastily submitted’ [?] …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
恐樂羊子一篋謗書難逃投杼欲如趙韓
王半部論語深切銘盤憶藺言空達於王
曾孤晏殊握髮之雅慙六丈過稱於富弼
幸韓琦擊楫之同臣敢不彌勵忠貞約五
路而著律宏恢遠畧分六將以訓兵唯恤
窮民以固本根請蠲榷酤酒稅若革僭號
而正名分許易繒帛駝羊蓋擴造化好生
之仁抑敦
王師無戰之義誓不共鯨鯢戴紫蓋心隨江
水流西切欲隨鴛鷺拜
丹墀情與塞鴻向北必使膽驚鶴淚萬里煙
絕烽墩庶幾名協龍圖三農影鋤桑柘伏
===
願
清心愼德外寧獨抱乎內憂
制治保邦文事兼資乎武備拓
列聖未成之業華夷一家開累世太平之基玉
帛萬國臣無任瞻
天仰
punctuated: 恐樂羊子一篋謗書，難逃投杼；欲如趙韓王半部論語，深切銘盤。憶藺言空達於王曾，孤晏殊握髮之雅；慙六丈過稱於富弼，幸韓琦擊楫之同。臣敢不彌勵忠貞，約五路而著律，宏恢遠畧，分六將以訓兵？唯恤窮民，以固本根，請蠲榷酤酒稅；若革僭號，而正名分，許易繒帛駝羊。蓋擴造化好生之仁，抑敦王師無戰之義。誓不共鯨鯢戴紫蓋，心隨江水流西；切欲隨鴛鷺拜丹墀，情與塞鴻向北。必使膽驚鶴淚，萬里煙絕烽墩；庶幾名協龍圖，三農影鋤桑柘。伏願清心愼德，外寧獨抱乎內憂；制治保邦，文事兼資乎武備。拓列聖未成之業，華夷一家；開累世太平之基，玉帛萬國。臣無任瞻天仰
translation_en:
…I fear that, like Yue Yangzi with his basketful of slanderous letters, I may scarcely escape the distrust that made a mother cast aside her shuttle. I wish to emulate Zhao, Prince of Han, with his half-copy of the Analects, engraving its lessons deeply upon my basin. I recall that words concerning Lin reached Wang Zeng in vain [?], and that I failed to repay Yan Shu’s gracious eagerness to receive worthy men, even with his hair in his hands. I am ashamed of the excessive praise addressed to Fu Bi by the venerable Sixth Elder [?], but fortunate to share Han Qi’s resolve in striking the oar.

How dare your servant fail to redouble his loyalty and steadfastness, establish regulations to coordinate the five circuits, extend his far-reaching strategy, and assign six generals to train the troops? To relieve the impoverished people and strengthen the foundations, I request remission of the wine-monopoly taxes. If the usurped titles are abandoned and the proper distinctions of status restored, let trade in silks, camels, and sheep be permitted. This would extend the life-loving benevolence of creation and uphold the principle that the royal army achieves its ends without battle.

I swear never to share the purple canopy with those monstrous rebels; my heart follows the river waters flowing west. I ardently wish to join the ranks of court officials bowing before the vermilion steps; my feelings turn north with the wild geese of the frontier. I shall surely make the enemy’s courage quail at the crane’s ‘tears’ [?], so that beacon smoke ceases for ten thousand li. May I prove worthy of the name of Longtu, the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, while farmers hoe among mulberry and silkworm-thorn trees through the three farming seasons [?].

Prostrate, I pray that Your Majesty purify your heart and attend carefully to your virtue, retaining inward concern even when peace prevails abroad; establish good government and safeguard the realm, supporting civil affairs with military preparedness. Extend the enterprise left unfinished by the successive sage emperors, making Chinese and non-Chinese one family; lay the foundations of peace for generations to come, with the myriad states presenting jade and silk. Your servant, overwhelmed, gazes toward Heaven and looks up to…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叅塲
策
第一問
強書
同考試官教授劉　批　〔模寫我〕
===
祖宗及我
皇上制作之盛宛然虞廷喜起氣象非沐菁莪樸棫之化而有得者未易及此
考試官學正毛　批　〔揄揚妙極足以傳示天〕
〔下後世矣錄之〕
考試官教授林　批　〔善鳴〕
〔今日之盛〕
大哉聖人之道乎剛柔交錯天之所以爲
文也是故天地交而能養萬物文明以止
帝王之所以爲文也是故上下交而能綏
punctuated:
聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叅塲，策，第一問。
強書
同考試官教授劉批：〔模寫我〕祖宗及我皇上制作之盛，宛然虞廷喜起氣象，非沐菁莪樸棫之化而有得者，未易及此。
考試官學正毛批：〔揄揚妙極，足以傳示天〕〔下後世矣，錄之。〕
考試官教授林批：〔善鳴〕〔今日之盛。〕
大哉，聖人之道乎！剛柔交錯，天之所以爲文也。是故天地交而能養萬物，文明以止，帝王之所以爲文也。是故上下交而能綏
translation_en:
… Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling reverence, I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and make them known to you.
Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question.
Qiang Shu.
Associate Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “It depicts the splendor of the institutions established by our imperial ancestors and our present emperor, vividly evoking the atmosphere of joyful exertion at Shun’s court. Such an achievement would scarcely be possible for someone who had not benefited from the nurturing influence celebrated in ‘Luxuriant Southernwood’ (Jing e) and ‘Oak Trees’ (Pu yu), and gained understanding from it.”
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: “Its praise is supremely accomplished, worthy of transmission throughout the realm and to later generations. Include it in the record.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “It gives eloquent voice to the splendor of the present day.”
How great is the Way of the sage! The interweaving of the firm and the yielding is how Heaven forms its patterns. Thus Heaven and Earth interact and can nourish the myriad things. Cultural brilliance governed by restraint is how emperors and kings establish civilized order. Thus those above and those below interact and can bring peace to …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
萬民夫聖人作民君師唯其相上帝以憲
聰明故以春夏秋冬之四府見於政則見
其潔以齊和以讓清以肅貞以固以元亨
利貞之四德播於文則見其温以𢡟莊以
則英以毅疏以達而要其本不外乎一心
焉爾矣是故嚴肅不可間者敬也純粹不
可淆者誠也瑩徹不可蔽者靈也充周不
可涯者神也敬誠之輿也誠靈之牖也靈
神之樞也神聖之奥也此帝王之文可以
===
興可以觀可以徵可以範而豈若書生尋
章摘句循行數墨云乎哉請因明問所及
而具陳之夫帝王之所以建極昭訓則若
堯舜濬其源禹湯文武揚其瀾于時名臣
之所以賡歌矢音則若皐夔諧其聲伊傅
周召振其響嗣後豁達若漢高英明若唐
太宗仁恕若宋太祖固皆三代以下之令
主矣然不知執中精一德先制心慎德之
道而況以不學無術如蕭何房喬趙普爲
punctuated:
萬民。夫聖人作民君師，唯其相上帝以憲聰明，故以春夏秋冬之四府見於政，則見其潔以齊、和以讓、清以肅、貞以固；以元亨利貞之四德播於文，則見其温以𢡟、莊以則、英以毅、疏以達。而要其本，不外乎一心焉爾矣。是故嚴肅不可間者，敬也；純粹不可淆者，誠也；瑩徹不可蔽者，靈也；充周不可涯者，神也。敬，誠之輿也；誠，靈之牖也；靈，神之樞也；神，聖之奥也。此帝王之文，可以興，可以觀，可以徵，可以範，而豈若書生尋章摘句、循行數墨云乎哉？請因明問所及而具陳之。
夫帝王之所以建極昭訓，則若堯舜濬其源，禹湯文武揚其瀾；于時名臣之所以賡歌矢音，則若皐夔諧其聲，伊傅周召振其響。嗣後豁達若漢高、英明若唐太宗、仁恕若宋太祖，固皆三代以下之令主矣。然不知執中精一、德先、制心、慎德之道，而況以不學無術如蕭何、房喬、趙普爲
translation_en:
…the myriad people. When the sage becomes the people's ruler and teacher, he assists the Lord on High and takes His perceptiveness as his model. Thus, when the four repositories of spring, summer, autumn, and winter find expression in government, they appear as purity joined with order, harmony with deference, clarity with solemnity, and constancy with firmness. When the four virtues of origination, flourishing, benefit, and steadfastness spread through literary expression, they appear as warmth joined with earnestness [?], dignity with adherence to standards, brilliance with resolution, and openness with understanding. Yet their ultimate foundation lies in the heart alone. Hence, solemnity admitting no interruption is reverence; purity admitting no admixture is sincerity; luminous clarity admitting no obstruction is spiritual awareness; all-pervading fullness admitting no limit is spiritual efficacy. Reverence is the vehicle of sincerity; sincerity is the window of spiritual awareness; spiritual awareness is the pivot of spiritual efficacy; and spiritual efficacy is the inner mystery of sagehood. Such imperial literary expression can inspire, afford insight, provide evidence, and serve as a model. How could it resemble a mere scholar's searching through chapters, picking out phrases, following lines, and counting written characters? Allow me to set this out fully in response to the matters raised in your illuminating question.
As for how emperors established the supreme standard and made their teachings manifest, Yao and Shun deepened its source, while Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu raised its waves. As for how the eminent ministers of those times continued their songs and gave voice to their intentions, Gao and Kui harmonized their tones, while Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao amplified their resonance. Later, rulers as broad-minded as Gaozu of Han, as discerning as Taizong of Tang, and as humane and forgiving as Taizu of Song were certainly excellent sovereigns of the ages after the Three Dynasties. Yet they did not understand the Way of holding fast to the Mean with refinement and singleness of purpose, giving virtue precedence, disciplining the heart, and attending carefully to virtue. How much less could they do so when they took men lacking learning and skill, such as Xiao He, Fang Qiao, and Zhao Pu, as their …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
股肱彼豈能沃心輔德而致之王道哉故
大風有歌矣而憂愁之怨弗可克也立石
有句矣而巢剌之慚弗可洗也日出有詩
矣而袖文之詐弗可飾也此其駁亦甚矣
而何文之有欽惟我
太祖高皇帝以聖明文武之資立帝王自有之
中國而尤不自滿假
親註洪範朝夕省覽又揭書大學衍義於兩
廡皆所以
===
憲天經世以明王道以錫民極也至
諭叅政蔡哲則曰公聽無私與
觀心亭數語互相發明
諭起居注詹同則曰文以明義理通世務若
典謨及出師表之誠意溢出可以爲文所
以風天下之端趨向也及莊誦
皇陵一碑首言
骨肉流離之情次言干戈困苦之狀末言
金陵定鼎之吉蓋謂創業甚艱而守成當不
punctuated:
股肱，彼豈能沃心輔德而致之王道哉？故大風有歌矣，而憂愁之怨弗可克也；立石有句矣，而巢剌之慚弗可洗也；日出有詩矣，而袖文之詐弗可飾也。此其駁亦甚矣，而何文之有？
欽惟我太祖高皇帝，以聖明文武之資，立帝王自有之中國，而尤不自滿假。親註《洪範》，朝夕省覽，又揭書《大學衍義》於兩廡，皆所以憲天經世，以明王道，以錫民極也。至諭叅政蔡哲，則曰：「公聽無私。」與《觀心亭》數語互相發明。諭起居注詹同，則曰：「文以明義理，通世務。若《典》《謨》及《出師表》之誠意溢出，可以爲文。」所以風天下之端趨向也。及莊誦皇陵一碑，首言骨肉流離之情，次言干戈困苦之狀，末言金陵定鼎之吉，蓋謂創業甚艱，而守成當不
translation_en:
…as their chief supports, how could those ministers enrich their sovereigns’ minds, assist their virtue, and bring them to the kingly Way? Thus, there was the Song of the Great Wind, yet its sorrowful lament could not be overcome; there were verses inscribed on stone, yet the shame concerning Chao La [?] could not be washed away; there was a poem on the rising sun, yet the deception of writings concealed in a sleeve [?] could not be covered up. Such profound inconsistencies—what true literary accomplishment was there?
Reverently we reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed with sagely intelligence and civil and martial excellence, established China as the rightful domain of emperors. Yet he was especially careful not to become complacent. He personally annotated the Great Plan, examining it morning and evening, and had the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning displayed in writing along the two side galleries. All this served to model himself on Heaven and order the world, to illuminate the kingly Way and bestow upon the people an ultimate standard. In instructing Cai Zhe, an Administration Vice Commissioner, he said: “Listen impartially, without selfishness.” These words and the remarks in the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind illuminate one another. In instructing Zhan Tong, a Court Diarist, he said: “Writing serves to illuminate moral principles and comprehend the affairs of the world. When sincerity overflows, as in the Canons and Counsels and the Memorial on Dispatching the Army, it can constitute worthy writing.” This was how he guided all under Heaven toward a correct orientation. And when we solemnly recite the inscription on the imperial mausoleum stele, it first describes the feelings occasioned by the dispersal of his own kin, next the hardships of warfare, and finally the auspicious establishment of the capital at Jinling. Its underlying meaning is that founding the dynasty was exceedingly difficult, and that preserving its accomplishments should not…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
易也豈非所以啓佑後人咸以正無鈌者
哉至
閱江樓記大畧謂歷代建都之有異乃氣數
循環之未周次言奔騎織梭之備佳景黃
旗赤幟之收成功所以狀龍灣山形勝之
奇也末言構樓於上以鎮遐邇均地之中
以利公私所以申建都
金陵之故也二篇文不相蒙而意若相貫眞
明問所謂
天葩燦爛聲格鏗鏘文臣閣筆有不能爲者
也豈盤庚遷都成王營洛佶屈聱牙之文
可同日語哉若夫以
===
勑賜劉基回鄉諭以歸老桑梓盡考終之道以
誥賜湯和封國示以人臣無將威福不專之訓
非
大聖人手筆不能若是之簡核也至於
賜宋濂醉學士歌雖詞臣代言而君臣同德
之義豈不可窺測哉夫湯和武臣之翹楚
punctuated: 易也，豈非所以啓佑後人，咸以正無鈌者哉？至《閱江樓記》，大畧謂歷代建都之有異，乃氣數循環之未周；次言奔騎織梭之備佳景、黃旗赤幟之收成功，所以狀龍灣山形勝之奇也；末言構樓於上以鎮遐邇，均地之中以利公私，所以申建都金陵之故也。二篇文不相蒙，而意若相貫，眞明問所謂「天葩燦爛，聲格鏗鏘，文臣閣筆，有不能爲」者也。豈盤庚遷都、成王營洛佶屈聱牙之文可同日語哉？若夫以勑賜劉基回鄉，諭以歸老桑梓、盡考終之道；以誥賜湯和封國，示以人臣無將、威福不專之訓，非大聖人手筆，不能若是之簡核也。至於賜宋濂《醉學士歌》，雖詞臣代言，而君臣同德之義，豈不可窺測哉？夫湯和，武臣之翹楚
translation_en:
…easy. Was this not a means of enlightening and aiding later generations, so that all might act correctly and without failing?

As for the Record of the River-Viewing Tower (Yuejiang lou ji), its opening broadly explains that successive dynasties established their capitals in different places because the cycle of cosmic forces and destiny had not yet come full circle. It next speaks of galloping horsemen moving like weaving shuttles and furnishing a fine spectacle [?], and of yellow flags and red banners securing victory, thereby depicting the extraordinary strategic advantages of Longwan Mountain. Finally, it speaks of erecting a tower on its summit to secure places far and near, and of occupying a central position in the land to benefit public and private interests, thereby elaborating the reasons for establishing the capital at Jinling. The two compositions do not overlap in wording, yet their meanings seem interconnected. They truly exemplify what your discerning question calls “heavenly blossoms in radiant profusion, resonant in sound and form, such that literary officials lay down their brushes, unable to achieve the like.” How could the awkward, abstruse writings about Pan Geng’s relocation of the capital and King Cheng’s establishment of Luoyang be mentioned in the same breath?

As for the edict bestowed upon Liu Ji on his return home, it instructed him to retire to his native place and fulfill the way of bringing his life to its proper close. The proclamation granting Tang He his fief set forth the admonition that a minister must harbor no rebellious designs and must not exercise the powers of punishment and reward on his own authority. Only the writing of the great sage could be so concise and precise. As for the Song of the Drunken Academician bestowed upon Song Lian, although a literary official composed it in the sovereign’s voice, can we not discern in it the principle that ruler and minister share the same virtue? Now Tang He was an outstanding figure among military officials…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也劉基宋濂文臣之巨擘也而賜以
勑賜以
誥賜以歌所以保全功臣之恩寵遇儒臣之禮
兩盡之矣豈漢唐宋諸君彷彿其萬一耶
列聖相承繼述益隆若
爲善陰隲
孝順事實皆首紀以事中系以斷末咏以詩
眞萬世臣民之至寶也至於
三朝聖諭録燕對録乃大學士楊士竒李東
陽等所撰因以知
===
列聖體道謙冲大臣因事納誨誠明問所謂上
下交泰之時也逮我
皇上入紹正統與舜孝堯文並隆矣而又憂勤
惜大禹之寸陰終始念高宗之舊學故爲
敬一箴以頒示學宮此誠天德之本王道之
端也是故矢口成章吐詞爲經蓋嘗捧誦
平臺賜輔臣諸詩有曰聖學
朕所勉煥乎慕堯章又曰日與聖賢伍外誘難
punctuated:
也。劉基、宋濂，文臣之巨擘也。而賜以勑，賜以誥，賜以歌，所以保全功臣之恩、寵遇儒臣之禮，兩盡之矣。豈漢唐宋諸君彷彿其萬一耶？
