列聖相承，繼述益隆。若《爲善陰隲》《孝順事實》，皆首紀以事，中系以斷，末咏以詩，眞萬世臣民之至寶也。至於《三朝聖諭録》《燕對録》，乃大學士楊士竒、李東陽等所撰，因以知列聖體道謙冲，大臣因事納誨，誠明問所謂上下交泰之時也。
逮我皇上入紹正統，與舜孝、堯文並隆矣。而又憂勤惜大禹之寸陰，終始念高宗之舊學，故爲《敬一箴》，以頒示學宮。此誠天德之本、王道之端也。是故矢口成章，吐詞爲經。蓋嘗捧誦平臺賜輔臣諸詩，有曰：「聖學朕所勉，煥乎慕堯章。」又曰：「日與聖賢伍，外誘難
translation_en:
… Liu Ji and Song Lian were towering figures among the civil officials. By bestowing an imperial order, a proclamation, and a song, he fully expressed both his gracious concern to preserve meritorious servants and the ceremonial regard with which he honored Confucian ministers. Could the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song have approached even one ten-thousandth of this?
The successive sage emperors carried on this legacy, making it ever more splendid. Works such as Hidden Recompense for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi) begin each entry by recording an event, follow it with a judgment, and conclude by celebrating it in verse. These are truly supreme treasures for subjects of every age. As for the Record of Sagely Instructions of Three Reigns (Sanchao shengyu lu) and the Record of Informal Imperial Audiences (Yandui lu), these were compiled by Grand Secretaries Yang Shiqi, Li Dongyang, and others. Through them we learn how the successive sage emperors embodied the Way and remained humble, while their great ministers offered admonitions as circumstances arose. This was indeed what is called a time of harmonious communication between superiors and subordinates [the wording 誠明問 is doubtful].
When our present Emperor succeeded to the legitimate imperial line, his filial piety equaled Shun’s and his cultural accomplishments equaled Yao’s. Moreover, solicitous and diligent, he treasured every moment as did Yu the Great, and throughout his reign kept in mind Gaozong’s earlier learning. He therefore composed the Admonition on Reverent Single-mindedness (Jingyi zhen) and distributed it to the government schools. This is truly the foundation of heavenly virtue and the starting point of the kingly Way. Thus, whenever he opens his mouth, his words form polished compositions; whatever he utters becomes a canonical guide. I have reverently read the poems bestowed upon his assisting ministers at the Platform. One says: “In the learning of the sages I exert myself; / I admire the brilliance of Yao’s accomplishments.” Another says: “Daily I keep company with sages and worthies; / External temptations can hardly …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
相嬰至於
翊學有集大畧因輔臣講大學衍義而
賜是詩首言帝王所圖治務學當為先末言
萬化脩身始
朕念方拳拳大哉
王言眞可謂往聖繼絶學萬世開太平矣今春
恭謁
七陵紀述七言律以賜輔臣
御筆淋漓頃刻立就豈唯氣象閎闊敘事詳
===
悉渙天下之至文而
大孝精誠感格天地讀之令人感動此豈武
王之達孝所可企及哉且諸臣各為賡和
成帙此又數百年以前之所曠見者故嘗
莊誦
聖製有曰地天既交泰民物咸平康又曰君臣
上下俱一德庶政唯和洪業成信斯言也
所以肇
宗社億萬載靈長之休不在茲乎抑嘗合而論
punctuated: 相嬰。至於翊學有集，大畧因輔臣講《大學衍義》而賜是詩，首言「帝王所圖治，務學當為先」，末言「萬化脩身始，朕念方拳拳」。大哉，王言！眞可謂往聖繼絶學、萬世開太平矣！今春恭謁七陵，紀述七言律以賜輔臣，御筆淋漓，頃刻立就。豈唯氣象閎闊、敘事詳悉，渙天下之至文，而大孝精誠感格天地，讀之令人感動！此豈武王之達孝所可企及哉？且諸臣各為賡和成帙，此又數百年以前之所曠見者。故嘗莊誦聖製，有曰：「地天既交泰，民物咸平康。」又曰：「君臣上下俱一德，庶政唯和洪業成。」信斯言也，所以肇宗社億萬載靈長之休，不在茲乎？抑嘗合而論
translation_en:
…to entangle one another. As for the collection on assisting learning [?], broadly speaking, these poems were bestowed upon the assisting ministers on the occasion of their lectures on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi). The opening says: “For emperors and kings seeking good government, devotion to learning must come first.” The ending says: “All transformation begins with cultivating oneself; to this My thoughts are earnestly devoted.” Great indeed are these royal words! Truly, they may be said to carry forward the interrupted learning of the sages of old and inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations!

This spring, His Majesty reverently visited the seven imperial mausoleums and commemorated the occasion in seven-character regulated verse, which he bestowed upon the assisting ministers. His imperial brush flowed freely, completing the poems in an instant. Not only are their scope expansive and their narration detailed—supreme writings promulgated throughout the realm [?]—but their profound filial devotion and perfect sincerity move Heaven and Earth. Reading them stirs the heart! Could even King Wu’s universally acknowledged filial piety hope to attain this? Moreover, the ministers each composed matching verses, which were assembled into a volume. This, too, is something scarcely witnessed for several hundred years.

Thus, I have reverently recited His Majesty’s compositions, which include these words: “Earth and Heaven have entered harmonious communion; the people and all things enjoy peace and well-being.” And again: “Sovereign and ministers, above and below, all share one virtue; the many affairs of government are harmonious, and the great enterprise is accomplished.” These words are true indeed! Is this not where the foundation lies for the enduring blessings of the dynastic ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain through countless ages? Yet I have also sought to discuss these matters together…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之
聖祖也
列聖也
皇上也所以文之至治之極皆以務學爲本正
心爲要眞可謂得千聖以來不傳之秘也
中庸曰辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬
辟如四時之錯行如日月之代明此之謂
歟愚生仰瞻
天地日月不能繪描竊效擊壤康衢歌詠
太平久矣執事倘與其進敢擧王假日中爲
===
當宁獻
第二問
解中建
同考試官教諭張　批　周禮周公經制之書也疑之者
皇甫已然矣是篇條析無遺疏通證明能逆盖得聖人之心於數千載之上
考試官學正毛　批　〔者孟子謂如有用我執此以往于今可執此以往哉拭目以俟〕
考試官教授林　批　〔辨析周禮如此詳盡者絕少得周官之意〕
punctuated:
之，聖祖也，列聖也，皇上也，所以文之至、治之極，皆以務學爲本、正心爲要，眞可謂得千聖以來不傳之秘也。《中庸》曰：「辟如天地之無不持載、無不覆幬，辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。」此之謂歟？愚生仰瞻天地日月，不能繪描，竊效擊壤、康衢，歌詠太平久矣。執事倘與其進，敢擧「王假日中」爲當宁獻。

第二問
解中建

同考試官教諭張批：周禮，周公經制之書也。疑之者，皇甫已然矣。是篇條析無遺，疏通證明，能逆盖得聖人之心於數千載之上。

考試官學正毛批：〔者孟子謂：「如有用我，執此以往。」于今可執此以往哉？拭目以俟。〕

考試官教授林批：〔辨析周禮如此詳盡者絕少，得周官之意。〕
translation_en:
…considering them together: the Sagely Founder, the successive sage emperors, and His Majesty have all taken diligent learning as the foundation and rectifying the mind as the essential means of attaining the highest cultural accomplishment and the perfection of government. Truly, they may be said to have grasped the secret not transmitted by the thousand sages of the past. The Doctrine of the Mean says: “They are like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and cover everything; like the four seasons proceeding in succession; and like the sun and moon shining in turn.” Is this not what it means? This humble student gazes upward at Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, yet cannot depict them. I have long ventured to emulate the songs of “Striking the Ground” and “The Broad Thoroughfare,” singing the praises of an age of peace. If you, honored examiners, should approve my advancement, I venture to offer to the reigning sovereign the words, “The king arrives at midday.”

Second Policy Question
Xie Zhongjian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The Rites of Zhou is the Duke of Zhou’s book of institutions and regulations. Huangfu already expressed doubts about it. This essay analyzes its particulars without omission, elucidating and substantiating them. It succeeds in reaching back [?] to grasp the sage’s mind several thousand years ago.

Comment by Examiner Mao, Assistant Instructor: 〔[Opening character unclear: 者.] Mencius said: “If anyone should employ me, I would proceed with this.” Can one proceed with this today? I shall wipe my eyes and await the outcome.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔Very few analyze the Rites of Zhou so thoroughly. This essay grasps the intent of the Offices of Zhou.〕

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
讀周禮者非仰高鑽堅不足以得聖人之
心用周禮者非謨明弼諧不足以語帝王
之治夫周禮一書乃周公親治太平之跡
凡天文地理之所以範圍華夏夷貊之所
以怙冐禮樂刑政之所以敷賁昆虫鳥獸
之所以曲成皆等之討之以盡變播之撫
之以盡數經之綸之以盡利鼓之舞之以
盡神誠巨不可倫細不可破遠不可禦邇
不可泄者也奈何烈焰未寒穿鑿尤毒於
===
是數有所不周變有所不通利有所不流
神有所不運矣然而聖經昭如日星固無
恙也向微君子抱遺經究終始何以闡絶
學開羣疑哉請具陳之周禮何爲而作也
聖人見天下之賾擬其物宜而曲爲之制
見天下之動秩其會通而預爲之防是故
列之九職九賦以廣其蓄申之八統九兩
以嚴其馭聯之讀法保氏以作其勸教之
婚姻和難以洽其懽紛之田獵樂舞以昭
punctuated:
讀周禮者，非仰高鑽堅，不足以得聖人之心；用周禮者，非謨明弼諧，不足以語帝王之治。夫周禮一書，乃周公親治太平之跡。凡天文地理之所以範圍，華夏夷貊之所以怙冐，禮樂刑政之所以敷賁，昆虫鳥獸之所以曲成，皆等之討之以盡變，播之撫之以盡數，經之綸之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神。誠巨不可倫，細不可破，遠不可禦，邇不可泄者也。奈何烈焰未寒，穿鑿尤毒！於是數有所不周，變有所不通，利有所不流，神有所不運矣。然而聖經昭如日星，固無恙也。向微君子抱遺經，究終始，何以闡絶學，開羣疑哉？請具陳之。

周禮何爲而作也？聖人見天下之賾，擬其物宜而曲爲之制；見天下之動，秩其會通而預爲之防。是故列之九職九賦，以廣其蓄；申之八統九兩，以嚴其馭；聯之讀法保氏，以作其勸；教之婚姻和難，以洽其懽；紛之田獵樂舞，以昭
translation_en:
Those who read the Rites of Zhou cannot grasp the sage’s mind unless they look up to its heights and probe its depths; those who apply it cannot speak of the government of emperors and kings unless they plan intelligently and assist harmoniously. The Rites of Zhou records the Duke of Zhou’s own achievement of peaceful government. It encompasses the patterns of heaven and earth, shelters the peoples of Huaxia and the Yi and Mo, spreads the adornments of ritual, music, punishments, and administration, and brings insects, birds, and beasts to fulfillment according to their particular natures. It ranks and examines these things to encompass every transformation, distributes and nurtures them to exhaust every reckoning, orders and organizes them to realize every benefit, and inspires and animates them to give full scope to their numinous efficacy. Truly, in its greatness it has no peer; in its minuteness it admits no breach; in its far-reaching scope it cannot be checked; and in its closeness nothing escapes it. Yet before the fierce flames had cooled, forced interpretations proved still more pernicious! Thus its reckonings became incomplete, its transformations obstructed, its benefits impeded, and its numinous efficacy arrested. Nevertheless, the sage’s classic shines like the sun and stars and remains unharmed. Had gentlemen not cherished the surviving classic and investigated it from beginning to end, how could they have elucidated this interrupted tradition of learning and resolved the many doubts? Allow me to set the matter out fully.

Why was the Rites of Zhou composed? The sage perceived the intricacies of the world, considered what was appropriate to each thing, and devised institutions suited to its particulars. He perceived the movements of the world, ordered their points of convergence and connection, and established safeguards beforehand. Thus he arranged the nine occupations and nine levies to enlarge its reserves; elaborated the eight principles of governance and nine bonds to make its control rigorous; linked the reading of laws with the Guardian (baoshi) to encourage its people; taught the rules of marriage and the settlement of disputes to bring harmony to their relations; and embellished its practices with field hunts, music, and dance to make manifest …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其度纖之泉府山澤以阜其用總之王府
太宰以制其萑蓋莫不有妙道精義存焉
者而可輕議乎哉夫太宰既以九職任民
矣而復有九賦者蓋九職所貢出於農圃
藪牧工商嬪婦臣妾閑民是乃任民之稅
也九賦所斂出於邦中郊甸家削邦縣邦
都關市山澤幣餘是乃任地之稅也然地
之所供何莫非民之所出者哉既曰八統
馭民矣而又謂九兩繫民者蓋統曰親親
===
敬故進賢使能保庸尊貴達吏禮賓此以
治王畿之民也兩曰牧長主吏師儒宗友
此以治畿外之民也然兩之所繫何莫非
統之所馭者哉卿大夫以正月頒法是亦
足矣閭師每歲二十五家讀法二十餘次
蓋中人之性常必有過彼其異日將有賓
興之期故以讀法書德行道藝孝弟婣睦
敬敏任恤之實正所以寓陶鎔之術也雖
繁數何厭哉師氏教三德三行亦已足矣
punctuated: 其度，纖之泉府山澤以阜其用，總之王府太宰以制其萑。蓋莫不有妙道精義存焉者，而可輕議乎哉？夫太宰既以九職任民矣，而復有九賦者，蓋九職所貢出於農圃藪牧工商嬪婦臣妾閑民，是乃任民之稅也；九賦所斂出於邦中郊甸家削邦縣邦都關市山澤幣餘，是乃任地之稅也。然地之所供，何莫非民之所出者哉？既曰八統馭民矣，而又謂九兩繫民者，蓋統曰親親、敬故、進賢、使能、保庸、尊貴、達吏、禮賓，此以治王畿之民也；兩曰牧、長、主、吏、師、儒、宗、友，此以治畿外之民也。然兩之所繫，何莫非統之所馭者哉？卿大夫以正月頒法，是亦足矣。閭師每歲二十五家讀法二十餘次，蓋中人之性，常必有過，彼其異日將有賓興之期，故以讀法書德行道藝孝弟婣睦敬敏任恤之實，正所以寓陶鎔之術也。雖繁數，何厭哉？師氏教三德三行，亦已足矣。
translation_en:
…their standards; it attends in detail to [?] the Treasury Office and the mountains and marshes to enrich their resources, and brings matters together under the royal treasury and the Grand Steward to regulate their [?]. Surely subtle principles and profound meanings are present in all these arrangements: how could they be lightly criticized?

The Grand Steward already assigns the people their responsibilities through the nine occupations; why, then, are there also nine levies? The contributions of the nine occupations come from farmers, gardeners, workers in marshlands, herdsmen, artisans, merchants, women engaged in textile work, male and female servants, and people without regular occupations. These are taxes assessed upon the people. What the nine levies collect comes from the capital, the suburban and outlying fields, the domains designated jiaxiao [?], the outer districts, the larger domains, passes and markets, mountains and marshes, and surplus funds. These are taxes assessed upon the land. Yet what does the land supply that does not come from the people?

Having spoken of governing the people through the eight unifying principles, why does the text also speak of binding them together through the nine bonds? The unifying principles are affection for kin, respect for old associates, advancement of the worthy, employment of the capable, protection of those with meritorious service, honoring the noble, promoting officials, and treating guests with ritual courtesy. These govern the people within the royal domain. The bonds are regional rulers, local leaders, lords, officials, teachers, learned men, lineage heads, and friends. These govern the people outside the royal domain. Yet who among those held together by the bonds is not also governed through the unifying principles?

For ministers and grand masters to promulgate the laws in the first month would seem sufficient. Yet each year the Neighborhood Master reads the laws to groups of twenty-five households more than twenty times. People of middling character are inevitably prone to faults, and in time they will face the occasion for selection and ceremonial presentation as worthy candidates. Thus, by reading the laws and recording their actual accomplishments in virtuous conduct, learning and skills, filial devotion, fraternal respect, harmony with relatives by marriage and with fellow lineage members, reverence, diligence, trustworthiness, and care for those in distress, the means of molding their character are embedded in these practices. Frequent and repetitive though they may be, why should one tire of them? For the Mentor to teach the three virtues and the three forms of conduct would likewise seem sufficient…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
保氏既教以六藝又教以六儀蓋世禄之
家鮮克由禮彼其异日將有任子之用故
以儀藝責之中和孝友動容中禮節奏比
樂之學實所以運王成之機也雖嚴密何
過哉吾聞父母仇不共天兄弟仇不同國
今設官和難誅其先動禁其怒鬬若相悖
矣不知先王重民物之命唯欲攘無髀執
無兵故爲此制且辟之則仇可以釋不辟
則法可以執是亦伸孝子之情矣豈若唐
===
人議殺汪蕢之忍耶吾聞野麕惡無禮蝃
蝀恥淫奔今設法聽奔限以仲春會以途
次若相違矣不知先王行多婚之政不忍
男有鰥女有怨故爲此制謂凶喪不可爲
恍納采不能親迎是亦存烈女之節矣豈
若鄭人桑間濮上之淫耶以田獵言之所
謂春蒐夏苗秋獮冬狩以講武是蓋鄉遂
之民隨遠近而量征或春蒐則夏不苗或
秋獮則冬不狩但言其名當如是耳豈必
punctuated:
保氏既教以六藝，又教以六儀。蓋世禄之家，鮮克由禮，彼其异日將有任子之用，故以儀藝責之。中和孝友、動容中禮、節奏比樂之學，實所以運王成之機也，雖嚴密何過哉？
吾聞父母仇不共天，兄弟仇不同國。今設官和難，誅其先動，禁其怒鬬，若相悖矣。不知先王重民物之命，唯欲攘無髀，執無兵，故爲此制。且辟之則仇可以釋，不辟則法可以執，是亦伸孝子之情矣，豈若唐人議殺汪蕢之忍耶？
吾聞《野麕》惡無禮，《蝃蝀》恥淫奔。今設法聽奔，限以仲春，會以途次，若相違矣。不知先王行多婚之政，不忍男有鰥、女有怨，故爲此制。謂凶喪不可爲恍，納采不能親迎，是亦存烈女之節矣，豈若鄭人桑間濮上之淫耶？
以田獵言之，所謂春蒐、夏苗、秋獮、冬狩，以講武，是蓋鄉遂之民，隨遠近而量征。或春蒐則夏不苗，或秋獮則冬不狩，但言其名當如是耳，豈必
translation_en:
The Protector taught not only the Six Arts but also the Six Forms of Deportment. Members of families enjoying hereditary emoluments seldom manage to abide by ritual propriety. Since they would later enter service through hereditary privilege, they were held accountable for their mastery of deportment and the arts. Training in balance and harmony, filial devotion and brotherly affection, movements conforming to ritual, and rhythms harmonizing with music was indeed the means of setting in motion the accomplishment of kingly rule [?]. Though strict and meticulous, how could this be excessive?
I have heard that one must not share Heaven with an enemy who killed one’s parents, nor inhabit the same state as an enemy who killed one’s brother. Yet officials were established to reconcile feuds, punish whoever struck first, and prohibit angry fighting. These things seem contradictory. People do not understand that the former kings valued the lives of their subjects and all living things. They wished only that people should brandish no arms [?] and grasp no weapons; hence they established this institution. Moreover, if the enemy withdrew, the feud could be resolved; if he did not withdraw, the law could be enforced. This too allowed expression to a filial son’s feelings. How could it resemble the cruelty of the men of the Tang who proposed putting Wang Kui to death [?]?
I have heard that “The Wild Deer” condemns breaches of ritual propriety and “The Rainbow” regards illicit elopement as shameful. Yet rules were established permitting elopement, restricting it to the second month of spring and allowing meetings along the roads. These things seem inconsistent. People do not understand that the former kings pursued a policy of encouraging marriages, unable to bear that men should remain without wives or women should suffer resentment for want of husbands; hence they established this institution. This refers to those who, owing to bereavement, could not perform the marriage rites [?], or who had presented the betrothal gifts but could not personally escort the bride home. This too preserved the integrity of virtuous women. How could it resemble the licentiousness of the people of Zheng among the mulberry trees and beside the Pu River?
As for hunting, the spring sou, summer miao, autumn xian, and winter shou hunts were occasions for military training. The people of the townships and outlying districts were presumably levied in appropriate numbers according to their distance from the site. Those who joined a spring hunt might not join a summer hunt, and those who joined an autumn hunt might not join a winter hunt. The statement merely gives the appropriate names for these hunts. Must it necessarily be that …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
盡致於司徒而聽教於司馬以廢農業哉
以祭祀言之曰天神八變地祇六變人鬼
九變以致物是蓋樂舞之妙達洪纖而皆
格或六變而致祇不致物或八變而致物
不致神但言其理當如是耳豈必毛鱗在
囿沼而介羽在臺池以獻奇怪哉泉府有
收息之令蓋謂先王既不禁商賈之務末
亦不縱民以趨末彼王安石借此爲名而
行青苗乃神宗之能臣三王之民賊也山
===
澤有虞衡之征蓋謂先王既不爭民之利
亦不縱民以趨利彼管夷吾假此爲詞而
興鹽莢乃桓公之功臣三王之罪人也玉
府供玩好賜予之用明問此之瓊林大盈
非也蓋九功九賦不入玉府若獸魚之皮
毛觔骨則入以爲賜予玩好之需遂師之
野職野賦則入以爲佩服貨賄之用是斂
有藝入有經此豈後世天子私藏可並論
哉太宰掌百官兵衛之事明問比之丞相
punctuated: 盡致於司徒而聽教於司馬，以廢農業哉？以祭祀言之，曰天神八變、地祇六變、人鬼九變以致物，是蓋樂舞之妙，達洪纖而皆格。或六變而致祇不致物，或八變而致物不致神，但言其理當如是耳，豈必毛鱗在囿沼，而介羽在臺池，以獻奇怪哉？泉府有收息之令，蓋謂先王既不禁商賈之務末，亦不縱民以趨末。彼王安石借此爲名而行青苗，乃神宗之能臣、三王之民賊也。山澤有虞衡之征，蓋謂先王既不爭民之利，亦不縱民以趨利。彼管夷吾假此爲詞而興鹽莢，乃桓公之功臣、三王之罪人也。玉府供玩好賜予之用，明問此之瓊林大盈，非也。蓋九功九賦不入玉府，若獸魚之皮毛觔骨則入，以爲賜予玩好之需；遂師之野職野賦則入，以爲佩服貨賄之用。是斂有藝，入有經，此豈後世天子私藏可並論哉？太宰掌百官兵衛之事，明問比之丞相
translation_en:
…bring them all before the Minister of Education to receive instruction from the Minister of War, thereby neglecting agriculture?

As for sacrifices, the text speaks of eight changes of the music for the celestial spirits, six for the earthly spirits, and nine for the spirits of the dead, thereby summoning creatures. This means that the wondrous efficacy of music and dance reaches both great and small, bringing them all into attendance. Sometimes six changes summon earthly spirits but not creatures; sometimes eight changes summon creatures but not celestial spirits. It merely states that the underlying principle should operate thus. Must furred and scaled creatures actually appear in parks and ponds, and shelled and feathered creatures at terraces and pools, to present strange marvels?

The Treasury Office has a regulation for collecting interest. This means that the former kings neither prohibited merchants from pursuing commerce, the secondary occupation, nor gave the people free rein to rush into it. Wang Anshi invoked this as a pretext for implementing the Green Sprouts loan program. He was an able minister of Shenzong, but by the standards of the Three Kings, a despoiler of the people.

In the mountains and marshes, there were levies administered by the foresters and wardens. This means that the former kings neither competed with the people for profit nor gave them free rein to pursue it. Guan Yiwu used this as a justification for instituting the salt monopoly [?]. He was a meritorious minister of Duke Huan, but by the standards of the Three Kings, a guilty man.

The Jade Treasury supplies objects for enjoyment and bestowal. Your illuminating question apparently compares it to the Qionglin and Daying treasuries [?]; this is mistaken. The revenues of the nine categories of work and the nine levies did not enter the Jade Treasury. Such things as the hides, fur, sinews, and bones of beasts and fish did enter it, to supply gifts and objects for enjoyment. The proceeds of the rural services and rural levies administered by the District Masters entered it to provide personal ornaments, clothing, and valuables. Thus collections had limits, and receipts followed established rules. How could this be discussed on the same footing as the private treasuries of emperors in later ages?

The Grand Steward manages the affairs of the hundred officials and the military guards. Your illuminating question compares him to the Counselor-in-Chief…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
職銜非也蓋小宰司會分理財計況呂僕
雖掌兵必宰臣而後發召公雖制命必二
卿而後行是道有揆法有守豈若後世宰
相專䔲可彷彿哉夫以周禮本無可疑也
而執事舉數條爲問豈以是書爲瀆亂不
經戰國陰謀如何休諸人之說耶噫可歎
也嗣後漢有后蒼曹褒諸儀唐有貞觀開
元諸禮宋有開寶慶曆諸編皆承訛襲謬
非片言可盡者夫后蒼以下諸臣何人也
===
而敢議禮如此之易眞以管窺天以蠡測
海可謂不知量之甚矣若夫誣周禮曰劉
歆壞周禮者曰鄭康成夫歆之郡置市官
以得罪名教夫人皆知之彼康成傳註之
悮以貽患無窮人不得而知也蓋其說周
禮有五失而諸儒寧道孔悮諱言鄭非此
葉文康謂歆之罪小康成之罪大也而要
之康成羽翼六經之功豈可相掩哉生非
求知於人也姑述所聞以求解疑也謹對
punctuated: 職銜，非也。蓋小宰、司會分理財計，況呂僕雖掌兵，必宰臣而後發；召公雖制命，必二卿而後行。是道有揆，法有守，豈若後世宰相專䔲可彷彿哉？夫以《周禮》本無可疑也，而執事舉數條爲問，豈以是書爲瀆亂不經、戰國陰謀，如何休諸人之說耶？噫，可歎也！嗣後漢有后蒼、曹褒諸儀，唐有貞觀、開元諸禮，宋有開寶、慶曆諸編，皆承訛襲謬，非片言可盡者。夫后蒼以下諸臣何人也，而敢議禮如此之易？眞以管窺天，以蠡測海，可謂不知量之甚矣！若夫誣《周禮》曰劉歆，壞《周禮》者曰鄭康成。夫歆之郡置市官，以得罪名教，夫人皆知之；彼康成傳註之悮，以貽患無窮，人不得而知也。蓋其說《周禮》有五失，而諸儒寧道孔悮，諱言鄭非。此葉文康謂歆之罪小、康成之罪大也。而要之，康成羽翼六經之功，豈可相掩哉？生非求知於人也，姑述所聞，以求解疑也。謹對。
translation_en:
…the official title: that comparison is incorrect. The Junior Steward and the Grand Accountant divided responsibility for financial administration. Moreover, although Lü Pu [?] controlled the troops, they could be dispatched only through the chief minister; although the Duke of Shao issued commands, these could take effect only through the two ministers. Thus the Way supplied the guiding standards, and the laws had their appointed guardians. How could this resemble the monopolization of authority [?] by chief ministers in later ages?

The Rites of Zhou itself gives no grounds for doubt. Yet you, sir, have selected several passages for your question. Do you perhaps regard this book as corrupt, disorderly, contrary to canonical principles, and a product of Warring States intrigue, as He Xiu and others claimed? Alas, how lamentable! Subsequently, the Han had the ceremonial works of Hou Cang and Cao Bao; the Tang had the ritual codes of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras; and the Song had the compilations of the Kaibao and Qingli eras. All perpetuated errors and inherited misconceptions, more than a few words could exhaust. Who were Hou Cang and the officials who followed him, that they dared pronounce upon ritual with such ease? Truly, they were viewing heaven through a tube and measuring the sea with a ladle. Their failure to recognize their own limitations was extreme indeed!

As for the man who misrepresented the Rites of Zhou, that was Liu Xin; the man who ruined it was Zheng Kangcheng. Everyone knows that Liu Xin established market officials in the commanderies and thereby offended against the moral teachings governing social roles. But people fail to recognize the errors in Zheng Kangcheng’s commentaries and annotations, which bequeathed endless harm. His explanation of the Rites of Zhou contains five faults, yet scholars would sooner say that Confucius was mistaken than admit that Zheng was wrong. This is why Ye Wenkang said that Liu Xin’s offense was small and Zheng Kangcheng’s great. Ultimately, however, how could these faults obscure Kangcheng’s contribution to supporting and elucidating the Six Classics? I, this student, do not seek recognition from others. I have merely set forth what I have heard, in the hope of resolving my doubts. Respectfully submitted.

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第三問　董大經
同考試官教諭章　批　場中士子多難此問吾子
〔不唯事實詳悉而道理精明宏博之學通達之才可羨可羨〕
同考試官教諭黃　批　天文一策正以觀士子窮
〔理之學此作考據精到足破後世怪誕之說佳士也〕
考試官學正毛　批　是正人心息邪說文字
考試官教授林　批　見理詳明
聖經貫天地之道是故衆言無可信折諸
===
經天地妙太極之精是故聖經無可考折
諸理夫太極者動静之源也陰陽者法象
之本也陽以陰爲基陰以陽爲唱是故闔
闢互爲其根體用互藏其宅也別而言之
陽以燥爲性以奇爲數以剛爲體其爲氣
炎其爲形員浮而明動而吐皆是也凡陰
以濕爲性以偶爲數以柔爲體其爲氣凉
其爲形方沉而晴静而翕皆是也是故象起
於形也數起於質也名起於言也意起於
punctuated:
第三問　董大經

同考試官教諭章　批：場中士子多難此問，吾子〔不唯事實詳悉，而道理精明，宏博之學，通達之才，可羨可羨！〕

同考試官教諭黃　批：天文一策，正以觀士子窮〔理之學。此作考據精到，足破後世怪誕之說，佳士也！〕

考試官學正毛　批：是正人心、息邪說文字。

考試官教授林　批：見理詳明。

聖經貫天地之道，是故衆言無可信，折諸經；天地妙太極之精，是故聖經無可考，折諸理。夫太極者，動静之源也；陰陽者，法象之本也。陽以陰爲基，陰以陽爲唱，是故闔闢互爲其根，體用互藏其宅也。別而言之，陽以燥爲性，以奇爲數，以剛爲體，其爲氣炎，其爲形員，浮而明，動而吐，皆是也。凡陰，以濕爲性，以偶爲數，以柔爲體，其爲氣凉，其爲形方，沉而晴，静而翕，皆是也。是故象起於形也，數起於質也，名起於言也，意起於
translation_en:
Third Question — Dong Dajing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Many candidates in the examination hall found this question difficult. You, sir, 〔not only display detailed knowledge of the facts but also a penetrating understanding of principles. Such extensive learning and comprehensive ability—admirable indeed!〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: This policy question on astronomy was intended precisely to assess candidates’ learning in investigating 〔principle to its utmost. This essay’s examination of evidence is precise and thorough, sufficient to refute the bizarre doctrines of later ages. An excellent scholar!〕

Comment by Examiner Mao, Instructor: This is writing that rectifies people’s minds and puts an end to pernicious doctrines.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: His understanding of principle is detailed and clear.

The sages’ classics encompass the Way of Heaven and Earth. Thus, when the various assertions cannot be trusted, adjudicate them by the classics. Heaven and Earth wondrously embody the essence of the Supreme Ultimate. Thus, when the sages’ classics offer nothing by which to verify a matter, adjudicate it by principle. The Supreme Ultimate is the source of movement and stillness; yin and yang are the foundation of patterns and images. Yang takes yin as its foundation, and yin takes yang as its leader. Thus closing and opening are each the root of the other, and substance and function each harbor the other within their abode. Considered separately, yang has dryness as its nature, odd numbers as its numbers, and hardness as its substance. As vital energy it is hot; as shape it is round. Floating and bright, moving and issuing forth—all these belong to yang. Yin, in general, has moisture as its nature, even numbers as its numbers, and softness as its substance. As vital energy it is cool; as shape it is square. Sinking and clear [?], still and drawing inward—all these belong to yin. Thus images arise from form; numbers arise from material constitution; names arise from speech; meaning arises from …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
用也而莫非一理之磅礴也論造化者翟
衡於此而已矣苟於理一有未窮則荒唐
妖誕之言鴉鳴蟬噪以貫耳横胸其何以
精一自信卓然不爲其所動摇哉執事發
策舉諸子論天文者以質諸生蓋以考諸
生之究心理學何如也顧生不見異人與
異書其何以知之蓋嘗聞其梗槩矣令夫
一元之氣周流太虚之間未有天地先有
水火此一則神兩故化之理也唯火極清
===
則爲天爲日星爲風雷水極濁則爲山嶽
爲雨月爲霜雪此明問所謂發微而不可
禦爲氣清通而不可象爲神是也盈天地
間孰有離陰陽而可以爲造化者哉夫輕
清上浮曰天乃陰陽法象之最大者也晉
天文志謂天如磨形日月蟻行於上蓋惑
於日月右旋之説彼吕氏春秋及繁露分
九野十端皆妄也而况謂斷鼇鍊石尤爲
不經天一氣也可以鼇而立石而補有是
punctuated:
用也，而莫非一理之磅礴也。論造化者，翟衡於此而已矣。苟於理一有未窮，則荒唐妖誕之言，鴉鳴蟬噪，以貫耳横胸，其何以精一自信，卓然不爲其所動摇哉？執事發策，舉諸子論天文者以質諸生，蓋以考諸生之究心理學何如也。顧生不見異人與異書，其何以知之？蓋嘗聞其梗槩矣。
令夫一元之氣，周流太虚之間，未有天地，先有水火，此一則神、兩故化之理也。唯火極清，則爲天，爲日星，爲風雷；水極濁，則爲山嶽，爲雨月，爲霜雪。此明問所謂發微而不可禦爲氣、清通而不可象爲神是也。盈天地間，孰有離陰陽而可以爲造化者哉？
夫輕清上浮曰天，乃陰陽法象之最大者也。《晉天文志》謂天如磨形，日月蟻行於上，蓋惑於日月右旋之説。彼《吕氏春秋》及《繁露》分九野十端，皆妄也。而况謂斷鼇鍊石，尤爲不經。天一氣也，可以鼇而立、石而補，有是
translation_en:
…function; all are manifestations of the expansive working of a single principle. Those who discuss creation and transformation need only weigh the matter here [?]. If even one aspect of principle remains unexplored, then absurd and fantastic assertions will penetrate the ears and fill the breast like the cawing of crows and the rasping of cicadas. How could one then maintain refined and undivided conviction, standing firm without being shaken by them? You, honored examiner, have posed a policy question citing the various masters who discussed celestial phenomena, in order to question us students. Your purpose, surely, is to test how deeply we have applied ourselves to the study of principle. Yet I, a student, have encountered neither extraordinary men nor extraordinary books: how could I understand these matters? Still, I have heard their broad outlines.
Now [?], the primal qi circulates throughout the Great Void. Before Heaven and Earth existed, water and fire already existed. This exemplifies the principle that unity is numinous, while duality produces transformation. Fire, when supremely clear, becomes heaven, the sun and stars, and wind and thunder; water, when supremely turbid, becomes mountains, rain and the moon [?], and frost and snow. This is what your illuminating question means by saying that what issues from the subtle and cannot be resisted is qi, while what is clear and all-pervading and cannot be represented in an image is numinous. Of all that fills Heaven and Earth, what could bring about creation and transformation apart from yin and yang?
What is light and clear and floats upward is called heaven: it is the greatest manifestation of the patterns and images of yin and yang. The Treatise on Celestial Patterns in the History of the Jin states that heaven is shaped like a millstone, with the sun and moon moving over it like ants. This is surely a misconception arising from the theory that the sun and moon revolve to the right. The divisions into nine fields and ten divisions [?] in the Spring and Autumn Annals of Master Lü and the Luxuriant Dew are all unfounded. Still more contrary to the classics are the accounts of cutting off the giant turtle’s legs and smelting stones. Heaven is a single qi. Could it be propped up with a turtle and patched with stones? Could there be such a…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
理耶懸象著明曰日乃陰陽發見之尤盛
也屈原天問謂西北無光燭龍銜火以照
此蓋惑於天不足西北之說彼淮南子謂
行九州七舍皆妄也而況謂揮戈棄杖尤
爲不稽日一火也可以戈而麾杖而逐有
是理耶倬彼雲漢昭回于天詩之論天河
是也蓋析木形如匹練在箕斗之間故絶
漢曰天潢抵艮曰地紀若彼圖記之謂得
支石博物志之謂乘仙槎皆小人無忌憚
===
之言也彼君平雖善卜吾不知所卜何理
哉三五而盈三五而闕記之論月然也蓋
月形如水輪乃太陰之精故借光曰銀丸
黑子曰地影若酉陽書之謂得玉斧五經
通義之謂化蟾蜍齊東野人之語也彼有
黄雖善筮吾不知所筮何理哉以星言之
乃結在地五行之氣又受在天大明之光
者也星以五錯落若太白熒惑鎮辰歲星
與天日謂之七政吳澄謂有疾徐則謂金
punctuated: 理耶？懸象著明曰日，乃陰陽發見之尤盛也。屈原《天問》謂西北無光，燭龍銜火以照，此蓋惑於天不足西北之說。彼《淮南子》謂行九州七舍，皆妄也，而況謂揮戈棄杖，尤爲不稽。日一火也，可以戈而麾、杖而逐，有是理耶？「倬彼雲漢，昭回于天」，詩之論天河是也。蓋析木形如匹練，在箕斗之間，故絶漢曰天潢，抵艮曰地紀。若彼《圖記》之謂得支石、《博物志》之謂乘仙槎，皆小人無忌憚之言也。彼君平雖善卜，吾不知所卜何理哉！「三五而盈，三五而闕」，記之論月然也。蓋月形如水輪，乃太陰之精，故借光曰銀丸，黑子曰地影。若《酉陽書》之謂得玉斧、《五經通義》之謂化蟾蜍，齊東野人之語也。彼有黄雖善筮，吾不知所筮何理哉！以星言之，乃結在地五行之氣，又受在天大明之光者也。星以五錯落，若太白、熒惑、鎮、辰、歲星，與天日謂之七政。吳澄謂有疾徐，則謂金
translation_en:
…could there be such a principle? The sun is the celestial image suspended above and shining brightly; it is the most powerful manifestation of yin and yang. Qu Yuan’s Questions to Heaven says that the northwest has no light and that the Torch Dragon carries fire in its mouth to illuminate it. This is surely a misconception arising from the claim that Heaven is deficient in the northwest. The Huainanzi’s account of the sun traversing nine regions and seven stations is all false. How much more unfounded are the stories of brandishing a spear and casting aside a staff! The sun is simply fire: could one wave it back with a spear or pursue it with a staff? Could there be such a principle?

“Vast is that Cloudy Han, shining and wheeling across the heavens”: this is how the Book of Odes speaks of the Celestial River. Ximu resembles a bolt of white silk and lies between the Winnowing Basket and Dipper lodges. Thus, what crosses the River is called the Celestial Pool, and what reaches the northeast is called the Earth’s Guideline [?]. Accounts such as that in the Illustrated Records of obtaining a supporting stone, or that in Records of Diverse Things of riding an immortal’s raft, are all the unrestrained words of petty men. Although Junping was skilled in divination, I do not know what principle his divination discerned!

“In three times five days it waxes full; in three times five days it wanes”: this is how the Book of Rites discusses the moon. The moon is shaped like a wheel of water and is the essence of the Supreme Yin. Because it borrows light, it is called the Silver Ball; its dark markings are called the earth’s shadow. Accounts such as that in the Youyang Book of obtaining a jade axe, or that in Comprehensive Interpretations of the Five Classics of transformation into a toad, are the talk of rustic men from eastern Qi. Although Youhuang [?] was skilled in milfoil divination, I do not know what principle his divination discerned!

As for the stars, they are condensations of the qi of the Five Phases on earth and also receive the light of the Great Luminary in heaven. The five planets are scattered about: Taibai, Yinghuo, Zhen, Chen, and Suixing—Venus, Mars, Saturn, Mercury, and Jupiter. Together with “Heaven and the sun” [?], they are called the Seven Regulators. Wu Cheng says that their movements vary in speed, and thus says that Venus…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
水附日鎮星最疾辰星最遲理或然也若
夫妖星曰孛絶跡而去曰飛跡相連曰流
其詳見於漢書至於足萬二千五百二十
之名數者與物數相當也吾不能諳星官
豈敢遽以爲定數耶以風言之乃陰之周
旋不舍如天之旋轉不停者也風以八扶
搖若明庶清明條景閶凉與廣莫不周謂
之八風陸機謂有離合謂列子御風來而
草生去而木落理所無也若夫上下曰頽
===
日出曰暴陰風曰曀其詳見於爾雅至於
換七十二番花信者與七十二候相當也
然吾不能曉風角豈敢遽以爲實信耶雨
之所以降以陰陽相和而成故詩曰朝隮
于西崇朝其雨而豕涉波月離畢皆以爲
雨之兆是可信也至朱子謂雨如飯甑極
爲著明若董仲舒之用桐魚仲尼之識商
羊吾尚以未眞彼石牛黒蜧之說好事者
爲之者也何足辨乎雷之所以鳴以陽在
punctuated: 水附日，鎮星最疾，辰星最遲，理或然也。若夫妖星曰孛，絶跡而去曰飛，跡相連曰流，其詳見於《漢書》。至於足萬二千五百二十之名數者，與物數相當也。吾不能諳星官，豈敢遽以爲定數耶？以風言之，乃陰之周旋不舍，如天之旋轉不停者也。風以八扶搖，若明庶、清明、條、景、閶、凉，與廣莫、不周，謂之八風。陸機謂有離合，謂列子御風，來而草生，去而木落，理所無也。若夫上下曰頽，日出曰暴，陰風曰曀，其詳見於《爾雅》。至於換七十二番花信者，與七十二候相當也。然吾不能曉風角，豈敢遽以爲實信耶？雨之所以降，以陰陽相和而成，故《詩》曰：「朝隮于西，崇朝其雨。」而豕涉波、月離畢，皆以爲雨之兆，是可信也。至朱子謂雨如飯甑，極爲著明。若董仲舒之用桐魚，仲尼之識商羊，吾尚以未眞。彼石牛、黒蜧之說，好事者爲之者也，何足辨乎？雷之所以鳴，以陽在
translation_en:
…and Mercury accompany the sun; Saturn moves fastest and Mercury slowest. The principle may indeed be so. As for anomalous stars, a portentous star is called a bo; one that disappears without leaving a trace is called a “flying star,” and one whose traces form a continuous line is called a “streaming star.” These are described in detail in the History of the Han. As for their names and numbers totaling twelve thousand five hundred and twenty, this corresponds to the number of things. I am not thoroughly versed in the celestial asterisms: how would I dare hastily pronounce this a fixed number?

Speaking of wind, it is yin circulating without cease, like Heaven revolving without stopping. Wind swirls in eight forms: Ming shu, Qing ming, Tiao, Jing, Chang, Liang, Guang mo, and Bu zhou are called the eight winds. Lu Ji speaks of their separation and conjunction, saying that Liezi rode the wind, that grass grew when he came, and that leaves fell when he departed. This has no basis in principle. As for wind moving up and down, it is called tui; wind at sunrise is called bao; and an overcast wind is called yi. These are described in detail in the Erya, the Approaching Elegance. As for the succession of seventy-two flower-signaling winds, these correspond to the seventy-two seasonal periods. Yet I do not understand divination by wind direction: how would I dare hastily regard these as reliable signs?

Rain falls because it is formed through the harmonizing of yin and yang. Thus the Book of Odes says: “Clouds rise in the west at dawn; before the morning is over, it rains.” A pig crossing the waves and the moon approaching the asterism Bi are both taken as portents of rain; these are credible. Master Zhu’s statement that rain is like a rice steamer makes the matter exceptionally clear. As for Dong Zhongshu’s use of a paulownia-wood fish and Zhongni’s recognition of the shangyang rain bird, I still regard these as unverified. Those tales of stone oxen and black water-dragons were invented by lovers of marvels. Why should they merit debate?

Thunder sounds because yang is within…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
內不得出而奮故易曰動萬物者莫疾乎
雷而驚百里震夷廟是可信也至朱子所
謂雷如爆杖最爲親切若宋史之謝仙火
輿地記之往金門吾尚以爲未確彼石室
仙車之說好辨者爲之也何足難乎雲之
所以興者吾聞時雨將降山川出雲觸石
而出膚寸而合戴記公羊傳有是言矣保
章氏以五祲辨吉凶則青爲蟲白爲喪赤
爲兵荒黑爲水黃爲豐於理有之若尚書
===
中候及漢書之謂堯光璧漢鼎繆矣若夫金
枝玉葉見於崔豹古今註皆道聽塗說者
也是何足較是非哉雪之所以凝者吾聞
上天同雲雨雪紛紛天地陰溫則爲雨寒
則爲雪周詩大戴禮有是言矣韓詩外傳
謂凡草木花多五出雪獨六出以應太陰
之數於理有之若毛詩之咏蝃蝀謝道韞
之咏柳絮近矣若夫銅駞玉馬見於眞定
記皆喪心病狂者也是何足辨眞僞哉大
punctuated:
內不得出而奮，故《易》曰：「動萬物者莫疾乎雷。」而驚百里，震夷廟，是可信也。至朱子所謂雷如爆杖，最爲親切。若《宋史》之謝仙火、《輿地記》之往金門，吾尚以爲未確。彼石室仙車之說，好辨者爲之也，何足難乎？
雲之所以興者，吾聞時雨將降，山川出雲，觸石而出，膚寸而合，《戴記》《公羊傳》有是言矣。保章氏以五祲辨吉凶，則青爲蟲，白爲喪，赤爲兵荒，黑爲水，黃爲豐，於理有之。若《尚書中候》及《漢書》之謂堯光璧、漢鼎，繆矣。若夫金枝玉葉，見於崔豹《古今註》，皆道聽塗說者也，是何足較是非哉？
雪之所以凝者，吾聞上天同雲，雨雪紛紛，天地陰溫則爲雨，寒則爲雪，《周詩》《大戴禮》有是言矣。《韓詩外傳》謂凡草木花多五出，雪獨六出，以應太陰之數，於理有之。若《毛詩》之咏蝃蝀、謝道韞之咏柳絮，近矣。若夫銅駞玉馬，見於《眞定記》，皆喪心病狂者也，是何足辨眞僞哉？大
translation_en:
…within, unable to escape, and therefore surging forth. Thus the Book of Changes says: “For setting the myriad things in motion, nothing is swifter than thunder.” That it startles people a hundred li away and strikes the temple of Yi is credible. As for Master Zhu’s statement that thunder resembles an exploding firecracker, this is particularly apt. But the “Xie Xian fire” in the History of the Song and the account of “going to Jinmen” [?] in the Record of Geography still seem to me unsubstantiated. Those stories about stone chambers and immortals’ carriages were concocted by people fond of disputation. Why bother refuting them?
As for how clouds arise, I have heard that when seasonable rain is about to fall, mountains and rivers emit clouds: they emerge upon contact with rocks and gather in patches a few inches across. The Record of Rites compiled by Dai and the Gongyang Commentary contain these statements. The Protector of the Epochs distinguishes auspicious and inauspicious signs by the five kinds of atmospheric emanations: blue-green signifies insect infestation, white mourning, red warfare and famine, black flooding, and yellow a plentiful harvest. These have a basis in principle. But the accounts in the Supplementary Prognostications to the Book of Documents and the History of the Han concerning Yao’s radiant jade disk and the Han cauldron [?] are mistaken. As for the golden branches and jade leaves recorded in Cui Bao’s Notes on Antiquity and the Present, these are all hearsay picked up along the road. Why bother weighing their truth or falsehood?
As for how snow congeals, I have heard that clouds cover the heavens and snow falls thickly; when the yin of heaven and earth is warm, it becomes rain, and when cold, it becomes snow. The Poetry of Zhou and the Elder Dai’s Record of Rites contain these statements. The Outer Commentary on the Han Tradition of the Poetry says that the flowers of plants and trees mostly have five petals, whereas snow alone has six points, corresponding to the number of Greater Yin. This has a basis in principle. The singing of the rainbow in the Mao Poetry [?] and Xie Daoyun’s verse about willow catkins come close. As for the bronze camels and jade horses recorded in the Record of Zhending, these are all the inventions of people who have lost their senses. Why bother distinguishing the genuine from the false? Broadly …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
抵天地間無一物而非造化之跡無一物
而非陰陽之理故嘗合而論之日隨天而
轉月隨日而行星隨月而見天之半明半
晦日之半羸半縮月之半盈半虧星之半
動半靜皆陰陽之相兼相制欲一之不能
也若雪隨雨而凝雨隨雲而降雲隨風而
飛風隨雷而烈雷之出入風之上下雨之
作止雲之升降雪之消息何莫非陰陽之
其來幾微其究廣大哉明問乃謂諸子之
===
言有互相發明愚謂五星八風五祲六出
之外皆在門墻當麾之者也孟子曰盡信
書不如無書此之謂矣然則學者果何以
折羣疑乎本之繫辭以窮其原合之太極
圖以盡其蘊參之經世以極其變約之正
蒙以知其化終之晦翁語録以會其全則
造化之意言象數皆在我矣而奚必旁搜
博釆以玩物喪志哉敬以是爲明問復
第四問
punctuated:
抵天地間，無一物而非造化之跡，無一物而非陰陽之理。故嘗合而論之：日隨天而轉，月隨日而行，星隨月而見。天之半明半晦，日之半羸半縮，月之半盈半虧，星之半動半靜，皆陰陽之相兼相制，欲一之不能也。若雪隨雨而凝，雨隨雲而降，雲隨風而飛，風隨雷而烈，雷之出入，風之上下，雨之作止，雲之升降，雪之消息，何莫非陰陽之其來幾微、其究廣大哉？明問乃謂諸子之言有互相發明，愚謂五星、八風、五祲、六出之外，皆在門墻當麾之者也。孟子曰：「盡信書，不如無書。」此之謂矣。然則學者果何以折羣疑乎？本之《繫辭》以窮其原，合之《太極圖》以盡其蘊，參之《經世》以極其變，約之《正蒙》以知其化，終之《晦翁語録》以會其全，則造化之意、言、象、數皆在我矣，而奚必旁搜博釆，以玩物喪志哉？敬以是爲明問復。

第四問
translation_en:
…Generally, between Heaven and Earth there is nothing that is not a trace of the work of creation, nothing that does not embody the principles of yin and yang. Thus I have attempted to discuss these together: the sun turns with Heaven, the moon travels with the sun, and the stars appear with the moon. Heaven is half bright and half dark; the sun alternately exceeds and falls short [?]; the moon alternately waxes and wanes; and the stars alternate between motion and stillness. All these arise from yin and yang combining with and restraining one another; one cannot make them uniform. Likewise, snow congeals from rain, rain descends from clouds, clouds fly with the wind, and wind grows fierce with thunder. Thunder emerges and withdraws; wind rises and falls; rain begins and ceases; clouds ascend and descend; snow diminishes and grows. Which of these is not a manifestation of yin and yang, subtle in its beginnings and vast in its ultimate effects?

Your discerning question states that the various masters’ accounts illuminate one another. In my humble view, apart from their accounts of the five planets, the eight winds, the five baleful atmospheric portents, and the six points of snowflakes, all should be waved away from the gates of learning. Mencius said: “Better to have no Documents than to believe the Documents entirely.” This is what he meant.

How, then, should students resolve their many doubts? Take the Appended Statements (Xici) as the foundation to probe their source; bring them into accord with the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) to exhaust their underlying significance; consult Ordering the World (Jingshi) to explore their transformations fully; draw them together through Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng) to understand their processes of change; and conclude with the Recorded Sayings of Huiweng (Huiweng yulu) to comprehend the whole. Then the meanings, words, images, and numbers of creation will all be within our grasp. Why must we search far and wide and gather indiscriminately, losing our resolve through fascination with things? I respectfully offer this as my reply to your discerning question.

Fourth Question

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭彭　批〔評品古人具有典則〕〔爾雅〕
〔以尚友天下士爲心他日所就可是占矣〕
考試官學正毛　批〔論人盡道尚友不凡傑作〕
考試官教授林　批〔考覈精當〕
觀周詩考槃之咏而知隱居之志貴眞不
貴僞觀春秋孔父之褒而知守死之義貴
正不貴偏夫人孰不欲富貴而所欲有甚
於富貴者是故塵視軒冕銖視金玉而不
===
屑與鷄鶩爭食是之謂隱居之道人孰不
欲壽考而所欲有甚於壽考者是故肉視
虎狼氷視鼎鑊而不屑與草木同朽是之
謂守死之道就其中而論之遊關入壁狗
苟蠅營固非也而追踪洗耳階爵媒祿亦
不可也隨波逐流裂冠毀冕固非也而擬
跡結纓墮坑落塹亦不可也士君子不幸
而處此寧爲召忽之死勿爲管仲之仁寧
爲伯夷之清勿爲下惠之和不然其不畔
punctuated:
同考試官教諭彭　批〔評品古人，具有典則〕〔爾雅〕〔以尚友天下士爲心，他日所就，可是占矣〕。
考試官學正毛　批〔論人盡道，尚友不凡，傑作〕。
考試官教授林　批〔考覈精當〕。
觀周詩《考槃》之咏，而知隱居之志貴眞不貴僞；觀《春秋》孔父之褒，而知守死之義貴正不貴偏。夫人孰不欲富貴，而所欲有甚於富貴者，是故塵視軒冕，銖視金玉，而不屑與鷄鶩爭食，是之謂隱居之道。人孰不欲壽考，而所欲有甚於壽考者，是故肉視虎狼，氷視鼎鑊，而不屑與草木同朽，是之謂守死之道。就其中而論之，遊關入壁，狗苟蠅營，固非也；而追踪洗耳，階爵媒祿，亦不可也。隨波逐流，裂冠毀冕，固非也；而擬跡結纓，墮坑落塹，亦不可也。士君子不幸而處此，寧爲召忽之死，勿爲管仲之仁；寧爲伯夷之清，勿爲下惠之和。不然，其不畔
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Peng, Instructor, comments: 〔His assessments of the ancients consistently follow established standards.〕〔Refined and elegant.〕〔He aspires to take worthy men throughout the realm as his friends; from this one can foresee his future achievements.〕
Examiner Mao, Instructor, comments: 〔His judgments of men fully accord with the Way; his choice of worthy friends is extraordinary. A masterpiece.〕
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔His examination of the evidence is precise and sound.〕
Reading the song “Delighting in Seclusion” (Kao pan) among the Zhou poems, we learn that the resolve to live in retirement is valued for its sincerity, not its pretence. Reading the praise of Kongfu in the Spring and Autumn Annals, we learn that the righteousness of remaining steadfast unto death is valued for its rectitude, not its one-sidedness. Who does not desire wealth and rank? Yet there are things one desires more than wealth and rank. Thus one regards official carriages and caps as dust, and gold and jade as trifles, disdaining to compete for food with chickens and ducks. This is called the way of living in retirement. Who does not desire longevity? Yet there are things one desires more than longevity. Thus one regards tigers and wolves as mere flesh, and execution cauldrons as ice, disdaining to rot away together with the grasses and trees. This is called the way of remaining steadfast unto death.
To consider the distinctions within these principles: roaming through passes and entering fortified camps [?], scraping along like dogs and bustling about like flies, is certainly wrong. Yet following the example of the recluse who washed his ears, while using this as a ladder to rank and a means of obtaining an official stipend, is also unacceptable. Drifting with the waves and following the current, tearing one’s cap and destroying one’s ceremonial headgear, is certainly wrong. Yet imitating the man who tied his cap strings before dying, only to tumble into pits and ditches, is also unacceptable. If a gentleman has the misfortune to find himself in such circumstances, he should choose to die like Shao Hu rather than practise benevolence like Guan Zhong; he should choose the purity of Bo Yi rather than the accommodating spirit of Liuxia Hui. Otherwise, that he should not depart from…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道者幾希請詳陳之夫天有至粹地有至
精見之造化則明明爲日星秀爲華嶽瑞爲
麟鳳馨爲芝蘭其在於人名曰浩然之氣
執事所謂砥節礪貞佩仁握義是也外此
在朝不可以爲臣在家不可以爲子矣是
節氣豈非士君子立身行巳之要道耶陜
西自昔號多材之地然事勢有難易人品
有汚隆不可不倂論也夫蘇武使匈奴而
取雪齧之忠則忠矣然與叛臣繾綣於臨
===
別之頃至有兩鴈倶北飛一鴈獨南翔之
句是非疾惡之不嚴也亦故舊之情耳彼
張吉舉忠義勉人欲死西夏戰爭之難以
烽卒而若此非私淑子卿之教矣乎朱雲
劾張禹而借劒誅之正則正矣然與小人
爭論於談經之時至有五鹿嶽嶽朱雲折
其角之謠是非撝謙之不至也亦月旦之
評耳彼雍冲無上事而進疏欲誅元祐紛
更之臣以太學生而若此謂非黙契朱雲
punctuated:
道者幾希。請詳陳之。夫天有至粹，地有至精，見之造化，則明明爲日星，秀爲華嶽，瑞爲麟鳳，馨爲芝蘭。其在於人，名曰浩然之氣，執事所謂砥節礪貞、佩仁握義是也。外此，在朝不可以爲臣，在家不可以爲子矣。是節氣豈非士君子立身行巳之要道耶？陜西自昔號多材之地，然事勢有難易，人品有汚隆，不可不倂論也。
夫蘇武使匈奴而取雪齧之，忠則忠矣。然與叛臣繾綣於臨別之頃，至有「兩鴈倶北飛，一鴈獨南翔」之句，是非疾惡之不嚴也，亦故舊之情耳。彼張吉舉忠義勉人，欲死西夏戰爭之難，以烽卒而若此，非私淑子卿之教矣乎？朱雲劾張禹而借劒誅之，正則正矣。然與小人爭論於談經之時，至有「五鹿嶽嶽，朱雲折其角」之謠，是非撝謙之不至也，亦月旦之評耳。彼雍冲無上事而進疏，欲誅元祐紛更之臣，以太學生而若此，謂非黙契朱雲
translation_en:
…those who do not turn away from the Way would be few indeed. Allow me to explain in detail. Heaven possesses the utmost purity, and earth the utmost essence. Manifested in the workings of creation, these shine brightly as the sun and stars, rise in splendor as Mount Hua and the sacred peaks, appear as auspicious qilin and phoenixes, and give forth fragrance as angelica and orchids. In human beings, this is called the vast, flowing moral spirit. It is what you, honored sir, describe as tempering integrity and steadfastness, wearing benevolence and grasping righteousness. Without it, one cannot serve as a minister at court or as a son at home. Are not such integrity and moral spirit essential to the way a gentleman establishes himself and conducts his life? Shaanxi has long been renowned as a land rich in talent. Yet circumstances vary in difficulty, and human character ranges from base to lofty: both must be considered together.
When Su Wu went as envoy to the Xiongnu and took snow to eat, loyal he certainly was. Yet at the moment of parting he showed lingering affection for a minister who had defected, even producing the lines, “Two wild geese fly north together; one wild goose soars south alone.” This was not insufficient rigor in hating evil, but simply affection for an old friend. As for Zhang Ji, he encouraged others by invoking loyalty and righteousness, wishing to give his life amid the perils of war against Western Xia. For a mere beacon soldier to act thus—was this not to have taken Ziqing’s teachings as his model without having studied under him? When Zhu Yun impeached Zhang Yu and asked to borrow a sword to execute him, upright he certainly was. Yet he disputed with a petty man during a discussion of the Classics, giving rise to the ditty, “Wulu towers aloft; Zhu Yun breaks his horns.” This was not a failure to practice humility to the utmost, but simply an appraisal of a person’s merits. As for Yong Chong, he submitted a memorial despite having no business to report [?], wishing to execute the ministers responsible for the disruptive changes of the Yuanyou era. For a student of the Imperial University to act thus—could one say that he did not inwardly share Zhu Yun’s…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之心矣乎以責欒隱覇陵而辭上玄纁者
韓康也隱居教授而不見太守龐參者任
棠也以二人較之棠既不往見矣又何抱
兒獻薤有類於持筐男子耶必若康之乗
柴車而遁逃斯謂之正矣以辟穀隱終南
而致毋焚筆者种放也隱居守道而不見
太守喬玄者姜岐也以二子評之放既不
願仕矣又何耽酒營利見劾於手搏狀元
耶必若岐之脅嫁毋而益堅斯謂之高矣
===
王莽以紫色蛙聲簒漢于時申屠剛自避
河西孔奮自避茂陵亦人所難者若夫孫
思邈隱太白而不受國子博士田游巖號
東鄰而不受崇文館職其疾風之勁草乎
夫思邈知隋之必亡終隱而不肯出是也
遊巖初若有隱居求志之風矣何爲毋言
所移而乗傳受官自取坐黨裴炎之辱哉
太宗以龍姿日表興唐于時劉感不屈仁
杲李襲志不學尉佗亦世所罕者若夫李
punctuated:
之心矣乎？以責欒隱覇陵而辭上玄纁者，韓康也；隱居教授而不見太守龐參者，任棠也。以二人較之，棠既不往見矣，又何抱兒獻薤，有類於持筐男子耶？必若康之乗柴車而遁逃，斯謂之正矣。以辟穀隱終南而致毋焚筆者，种放也；隱居守道而不見太守喬玄者，姜岐也。以二子評之，放既不願仕矣，又何耽酒營利，見劾於手搏狀元耶？必若岐之脅嫁毋而益堅，斯謂之高矣。
王莽以紫色蛙聲簒漢，于時申屠剛自避河西，孔奮自避茂陵，亦人所難者。若夫孫思邈隱太白而不受國子博士，田游巖號東鄰而不受崇文館職，其疾風之勁草乎？夫思邈知隋之必亡，終隱而不肯出，是也。遊巖初若有隱居求志之風矣，何爲毋言所移，而乗傳受官，自取坐黨裴炎之辱哉？
太宗以龍姿日表興唐，于時劉感不屈仁杲，李襲志不學尉佗，亦世所罕者。若夫李
translation_en:
…the heart of Zhu Yun?

It was Han Kang who lived in seclusion at Baling by “ze luan” [?] and declined the dark and light-red silks offered by the emperor as a summons to office. It was Ren Tang who lived in seclusion, teaching, and refused to meet the Governor, Pang Can. Comparing these two, if Tang would not go to meet him, why did he hold a child and present shallots, behaving rather like the man holding a basket? Only conduct like Kang’s—riding off in a rough wooden cart to escape—can be called upright. It was Chong Fang who abstained from grain and secluded himself on Zhongnan, causing his mother to burn his writing brushes. It was Jiang Qi who lived in seclusion, maintaining the Way, and refused to meet the Governor, Qiao Xuan. Judging these two, if Fang was unwilling to serve, why did he indulge in wine and pursue profit, bringing impeachment upon himself by the “wrestling champion” [?]? Only conduct like Qi’s—growing still firmer when threatened with having his mother married off—can be called lofty.

Wang Mang usurped the Han with his purple coloration and frog-like voice, counterfeit marks of legitimacy. At that time Shentu Gang withdrew to Hexi, and Kong Fen withdrew to Maoling: these, too, were deeds difficult for others to accomplish. As for Sun Simiao, who secluded himself on Taibai and declined appointment as an Erudite of the Directorate of Education, and Tian Youyan, who styled himself “Eastern Neighbor” and declined a post at the Institute for the Veneration of Literature, were they not sturdy grasses in a fierce wind? Simiao knew that the Sui must fall, and remained in seclusion, refusing to emerge: this was right. Youyan initially seemed to possess the spirit of one who lives in seclusion to pursue his aspirations. Why, then, was he swayed by his mother’s words, riding the imperial relay transport to accept office and bringing upon himself the disgrace of being implicated as a partisan of Pei Yan?

Taizong, with his dragon-like bearing and sun-like countenance, raised up the Tang. At that time Liu Gan would not submit to Rengao, and Li Xizhi would not emulate Commandant Tuo: these, too, were men rarely seen in the world. As for Li…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
玄通不事黑闥而潰腹有不辭韓偓不阿
韋貽範而斷腕有不避其烈火之真金乎
夫劉感李玄通知唐之必興寧死而不苟
合是也李襲志初若有亡國圖存之節矣
何爲子言所搖而在唐北面卒受異姓茅
土之封哉梁鴻與妻同隱耕山自娛是能
以清刑寡妻也余竊見安慶孤危能血戰
自裁妻子赴井忠貞凛凛至今尚有生氣
闕可謂不負所學矣使鴻而處此則將同
===
舉案之妻死安慶乎蘇良嗣惡僧無道批
頰不撓是能以忠事賊后也段秀實見朱
泚稱帝唾罵不屈擊笏遇害氣節昂昂至
今令人毛竦秀實可謂不負天子矣使良
嗣而處此則將推批頰之忠事朱泚乎就
數子而通論之若蘇武余闕劉感李玄通
真得蹇六二之匪躬也大丈夫可死則死
之朱雲廾與龍逄同遊矣而何恐恐然攀
檻求生哉人臣無將將則必誅秀實見泚
punctuated:
玄通不事黑闥而潰腹有不辭，韓偓不阿韋貽範而斷腕有不避，其烈火之真金乎！夫劉感、李玄通知唐之必興，寧死而不苟合，是也。李襲志初若有亡國圖存之節矣，何爲子言所搖，而在唐北面，卒受異姓茅土之封哉？
梁鴻與妻同隱，耕山自娛，是能以清刑寡妻也。余竊見安慶孤危，能血戰自裁，妻子赴井，忠貞凛凛，至今尚有生氣，闕可謂不負所學矣。使鴻而處此，則將同舉案之妻死安慶乎？
蘇良嗣惡僧無道，批頰不撓，是能以忠事賊后也。段秀實見朱泚稱帝，唾罵不屈，擊笏遇害，氣節昂昂，至今令人毛竦，秀實可謂不負天子矣。使良嗣而處此，則將推批頰之忠事朱泚乎？
就數子而通論之，若蘇武、余闕、劉感、李玄通，真得蹇六二之匪躬也。大丈夫可死則死之，朱雲廾與龍逄同遊矣，而何恐恐然攀檻求生哉？人臣無將，將則必誅。秀實見泚
translation_en:
…Xuantong refused to serve Heita and did not shrink from having his belly ripped open; Han Wo refused to flatter Wei Yifan and did not flinch at the prospect of having his wrist severed. Were they not true gold tested in a raging fire? Liu Gan and Li Xuantong knew that the Tang would surely rise, and preferred death to an unprincipled accommodation: they were right. Li Xizhi initially seemed to possess the integrity to seek his fallen dynasty’s survival. Why, then, was he swayed by his son’s words to face north as a Tang subject and ultimately accept an enfeoffment from a ruling house of a different surname?
Liang Hong lived in reclusion with his wife, taking pleasure in tilling the hills. Thus, through his purity, he could set an example for his wife. I humbly observe that, when Anqing stood isolated and imperiled, Yu Que fought a bloody battle and took his own life, while his wife and children threw themselves into a well. His loyalty and steadfastness were awe-inspiring, and their vital force remains even today. Que may indeed be said to have lived up to what he had learned. Had Liang Hong been placed in this situation, would he have died at Anqing together with the wife who raised his meal tray in respect?
Su Liangsi detested a monk’s outrageous conduct and slapped his face without yielding. Thus he could serve the usurping empress with loyalty. When Duan Xiushi saw Zhu Ci proclaim himself emperor, he spat curses at him, refused to submit, struck him with a court tablet, and was killed. His towering integrity still makes one’s hair stand on end. Xiushi may indeed be said not to have failed the Son of Heaven. Had Liangsi been placed in this situation, would he have extended the loyalty shown in that slap to his service under Zhu Ci?
Considering these men together, Su Wu, Yu Que, Liu Gan, and Li Xuantong truly grasped the selflessness expressed in the second, yin line of the hexagram Jian, Obstruction. When death is called for, a true man should die. Zhu Yun could have joined Long Pang [?]; why, then, did he cling so fearfully to the railing, seeking to live? A minister must not harbor rebellious intent; if he does, he must be executed. Xiushi saw Zhu Ci…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
之叛逆有漸矣何至稱帝而後擊之茍哉韓
偓見南北司如水火况朱温睥睨神器之
時何不急流勇退哉此明問所謂驅陷阱
莫之知避昧女壯莫之過防其數子之謂
也若梁鴻韓康孫思邈遁清操不虧是眞漸
上九之羽可儀也彼种放田遊巖則沽虛
名索高價尋捷徑信如明問所言者凡此
皆陝中人物之表表者而是非高下又如
此明問謂何人爲師豈以生齊人知管晏
===
耶昔仲尼之論曰用之則行舍之則藏又
曰國有道不變塞焉國無道至死不變此
愚之所以銘盤而書紳也寧學聖人而未
至豈敢以一善成名哉此愚之志也亦執
事之所責望也
第五問
劉應熊
同考試官教授翁　批
陝西之患惟三邊爲急此策〔於致弊之由捄弊之法酌古準今歷歷條議無遺經世務之志〕
punctuated:
之叛逆有漸矣，何至稱帝而後擊之？茍哉！韓偓見南北司如水火，况朱温睥睨神器之時，何不急流勇退哉？此明問所謂驅陷阱，莫之知避；昧女壯，莫之過防，其數子之謂也。若梁鴻、韓康、孫思邈遁，清操不虧，是眞《漸》上九之羽可儀也。彼种放、田遊巖則沽虛名，索高價，尋捷徑，信如明問所言者。凡此皆陝中人物之表表者，而是非高下又如此。明問謂何人爲師，豈以生齊人知管晏耶？昔仲尼之論曰：「用之則行，舍之則藏。」又曰：「國有道，不變塞焉；國無道，至死不變。」此愚之所以銘盤而書紳也。寧學聖人而未至，豈敢以一善成名哉？此愚之志也，亦執事之所責望也。
第五問
劉應熊
同考試官教授翁　批
陝西之患，惟三邊爲急。此策〔於致弊之由、捄弊之法，酌古準今，歷歷條議無遺，經世務之志〕
translation_en:
…rebellion had developed by degrees. Why wait until he proclaimed himself emperor before striking him? How remiss! Han Wo saw that the Southern and Northern Administrations—the court officials and the eunuchs—were like fire and water. Moreover, when Zhu Wen was coveting the imperial throne, why did Han not courageously withdraw from the rushing current? Your discerning question speaks of rushing into pitfalls without knowing to avoid them, and of failing to recognize the warning that “the woman is strong” and to take ample precautions. Surely it refers to these men.
As for Liang Hong, Han Kang, and Sun Simiao, they withdrew into seclusion without compromising their unsullied integrity. They truly exemplify the topmost yang line of the hexagram Gradual Progress: “Its feathers may serve as an adornment.” Zhong Fang and Tian Youyan, however, sought empty reputations, demanded high prices, and looked for shortcuts to advancement, exactly as your discerning question says. All these were outstanding figures of Shaanxi, yet their merits and faults, their relative worth, differed in this way. Your discerning question asks whom to take as a teacher. Should being born in Qi mean knowing only Guan Zhong and Yan Ying?
Zhongni—Confucius—once said: “When employed, act; when set aside, withdraw.” He also said: “When the state possesses the Way, he does not change from what he was in adversity; when the state lacks the Way, he remains unchanged unto death.” These are the words that I, in my humble judgment, would inscribe on my basin and write upon my sash. I would rather study the sage’s example and fall short of it. How could I dare seek fame through a single good quality? This is my aspiration, and also what you expect and require of me.
Fifth Policy Question
Liu Yingxiong
Comment by Associate Examiner Weng, Professor:
“Of Shaanxi’s troubles, those of the Three Frontiers alone are urgent. This policy essay 〔considers the causes of the abuses and the methods of remedying them, weighing antiquity against present circumstances. It discusses each point distinctly, omitting nothing, [and shows] an ambition to attend to the affairs of governing the world [?].〕”

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正毛　批
〔守備邊方經略第一義便于之說行于邊最宜〕
考試官教授林　批
〔識時務者〕
治國有大經而以容民畜衆爲先務禦戎
無上策而以貴謀賤戰爲良圖蓋兵者國
之大事勝負變於斯須存亡繫於呼吸是
不可不愼也故未戰則以決勝爲難既勝
則以制勝爲難或謂先王耀德不觀兵唯
布威戰之令陳文告之詞而勿勤兵于遠
也不知教笞不可廢於家刑罰不可弛於
===
國誅伐不可偃於天下唯曰疆場之事愼
守其一而備其不虞夫狄人之擾邊其中
非有大志者皆可以謀勝而氣奪也至求
其爲變之始其積之皆有漸也其所以擾
邊無虛月爲吾兵之不能苦戰而金帛子
女之所交會也夫狄人擁親戚畜牛馬長
子孫安居而欲保軀命無異於華人也而
沿邊之民惴惴然不敢解甲又況兵刃相
接安能勇氣百倍而有投石超距之樂哉
punctuated:
考試官學正毛批：〔守備邊方，經略第一義。便于之說，行于邊最宜。〕

考試官教授林批：〔識時務者。〕

治國有大經，而以容民畜衆爲先務；禦戎無上策，而以貴謀賤戰爲良圖。蓋兵者，國之大事，勝負變於斯須，存亡繫於呼吸，是不可不愼也。故未戰則以決勝爲難，既勝則以制勝爲難。或謂先王耀德不觀兵，唯布威戰之令，陳文告之詞，而勿勤兵于遠也。不知教笞不可廢於家，刑罰不可弛於國，誅伐不可偃於天下。唯曰疆場之事，愼守其一，而備其不虞。夫狄人之擾邊，其中非有大志者，皆可以謀勝而氣奪也。至求其爲變之始，其積之皆有漸也。其所以擾邊無虛月，爲吾兵之不能苦戰，而金帛子女之所交會也。夫狄人擁親戚，畜牛馬，長子孫，安居而欲保軀命，無異於華人也。而沿邊之民惴惴然不敢解甲，又況兵刃相接，安能勇氣百倍，而有投石超距之樂哉？
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Mao, School Instructor: 〔Defending the frontier is the foremost principle of military planning. The argument concerning expedient measures [?] is especially suitable for application on the frontier.〕

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔One who understands the needs of the times.〕

Governing a state has its great guiding principles, but its foremost task is to accommodate the people and nurture the multitude. Resisting the Rong has no supreme strategy, but a sound plan values stratagems over battle. Warfare is a great affair of state: victory and defeat can change in an instant, and survival or destruction hangs upon a breath. One must therefore exercise utmost caution. Before battle, the difficulty lies in ensuring victory; after victory, the difficulty lies in maintaining mastery. Some say that the former kings displayed their virtue rather than their troops, merely issuing commands to inspire awe in warfare [?] and setting forth proclamations, without exhausting their armies on distant campaigns. They do not understand that corrective whipping cannot be abolished within the household, punishments cannot be relaxed within the state, and punitive campaigns cannot be discontinued throughout the realm. In frontier affairs, one can only say: steadfastly maintain a single purpose and prepare for the unforeseen.

Among the Di who raid the frontier, those who harbor no great ambitions can all be overcome through stratagems and deprived of their fighting spirit. If we seek the beginnings of their disturbances, we find that these have invariably developed by gradual accumulation. They raid the frontier without letting a month pass because our soldiers cannot endure hard fighting, and because it is a place where gold, silk, women, and children are gathered. The Di cherish their kin, raise cattle and horses, rear children and grandchildren, and wish to live peacefully and preserve their lives, no differently from the Chinese. Yet the people along the frontier are so apprehensive that they dare not take off their armor. How much more so when weapons clash! How could their courage increase a hundredfold, and how could they take pleasure in throwing stones and leaping distances as martial exercises?

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此三邊之所以紛紛多事也執事發策而
以是下詢承學蓋亦有見於此也今夫陜
西之患非止於夷狄也水旱之頻仍賦役
之繁重盜賊之竊發鬬訟之紛紜風俗之
偷薄老壯之逃散財用之空乏
藩祿之浩繁是皆可長慮也然尚可徐而
圖之也而事之急且大者孰有過於三邊
哉先朝自馮勝余子俊驅虜出套自後乍
來如風雨也而今春烽火接於秦隴胡馬
===
飲於涇泉蓋有不可忍言者矣今屯駐河
套而不去此其志豈有厭勢豈有已哉夫
三邊者陜西之藩籬也陜西者中原之門
戶也制治於未亂保邦於未危此豈非今
日第一義耶姑舉往事言之李鳴復謂關
外忠勇自備衣糧器械當增額爲攻守之
圖是矣而宋祁乃建五可誚之說則曰騎
多馬少也河決不塞也兵罷大習也重任
懦將也探候間諜無財募召也至謂邊將
punctuated: 此三邊之所以紛紛多事也。執事發策，而以是下詢承學，蓋亦有見於此也。今夫陜西之患，非止於夷狄也。水旱之頻仍，賦役之繁重，盜賊之竊發，鬬訟之紛紜，風俗之偷薄，老壯之逃散，財用之空乏，藩祿之浩繁，是皆可長慮也。然尚可徐而圖之也，而事之急且大者，孰有過於三邊哉？先朝自馮勝、余子俊驅虜出套，自後乍來如風雨也。而今春烽火接於秦隴，胡馬飲於涇泉，蓋有不可忍言者矣。今屯駐河套而不去，此其志豈有厭，勢豈有已哉？夫三邊者，陜西之藩籬也；陜西者，中原之門戶也。制治於未亂，保邦於未危，此豈非今日第一義耶？姑舉往事言之，李鳴復謂關外忠勇自備衣糧器械，當增額爲攻守之圖，是矣。而宋祁乃建五可誚之說，則曰騎多馬少也，河決不塞也，兵罷大習也，重任懦將也，探候間諜無財募召也。至謂邊將
translation_en: This is why the Three Frontiers are beset with so many troubles. In setting this policy question and condescending to consult us students on these matters, you, gentlemen, surely also recognize this. The troubles of Shaanxi today are not confined to the peoples beyond our borders. Repeated floods and droughts, heavy taxes and labor services, outbreaks of banditry, proliferating quarrels and lawsuits, increasingly lax and mean customs, the flight and dispersal of old and able-bodied alike, depleted finances, and the enormous stipends paid to the imperial princes—all warrant long-term concern. Yet these can still be addressed gradually. What matter is more urgent and consequential than the Three Frontiers? In earlier reigns, Feng Sheng and Yu Zijun drove the enemy out of the Hetao, but thereafter they have returned suddenly, like wind and rain. This spring, beacon fires stretched across Qin and Long, and the invaders’ horses drank from the waters of the Jing. There are things one cannot bear to recount. Now they are encamped in the Hetao and will not leave. Can their ambitions ever be satisfied, or their advance ever cease? The Three Frontiers are the protective fence of Shaanxi; Shaanxi is the gateway to the Central Plain. To establish order before disorder arises, and safeguard the realm before danger comes—is this not today’s foremost duty? Let me cite past affairs. Li Mingfu said that the Zhongyong troops beyond the passes supplied their own clothing, provisions, and weapons, and that their authorized numbers should be increased to provide for both attack and defense. This was right. Song Qi, however, advanced an argument identifying five grounds for reproach: many cavalrymen but few horses; breaches in the river embankments left unclosed; large-scale military drills discontinued; weighty responsibilities entrusted to cowardly generals; and no funds to recruit scouts and spies. He went so far as to say that the frontier generals…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不知休兵當宁不擾戍筭而欲抽減邊兵
是蓋有見當時之冗兵太濫也而豈定計
哉上官均謂蘭州塞地皆控戎馬要路當
積穀爲固守之策是矣而劉敞乃建四不
可之說則曰規小利也種落懷疑也築城
濫費秦州空竭也虜怨益深兵必不解也
至謂大舜不伐有苗漢武不征車師而乃
諫止城渭蓋見當時之支費太多也而豈
良圖哉起居舍人范純仁欲罷監牧營田
===
畝彼非以監牧之馬可以盡去也蓋陝西
四塞之地漕運不通若沙苑牧地募民耕
種則所獲穀食既可贍軍所得芻稈亦可
秣馬此一舉而兩得之計也樞密使文彥
博欲築熈州緩洮河者彼非以洮河之備
可以盡撤也蓋西番初附之時撫綏未盡
若進築河州漸恢遠畧則積粟未豐恐壞
根本番心未定幾喪前功此不欲速見小
之說也知涇州者夏竦也竦上十策請習
punctuated:
不知休兵，當宁不擾戍筭，而欲抽減邊兵，是蓋有見當時之冗兵太濫也，而豈定計哉？上官均謂蘭州塞地皆控戎馬要路，當積穀爲固守之策，是矣。而劉敞乃建四不可之說，則曰：規小利也，種落懷疑也，築城濫費、秦州空竭也，虜怨益深、兵必不解也。至謂大舜不伐有苗，漢武不征車師，而乃諫止城渭，蓋見當時之支費太多也，而豈良圖哉？

起居舍人范純仁欲罷監牧、營田畝，彼非以監牧之馬可以盡去也。蓋陝西四塞之地，漕運不通，若沙苑牧地募民耕種，則所獲穀食既可贍軍，所得芻稈亦可秣馬，此一舉而兩得之計也。

樞密使文彥博欲築熈州、緩洮河者，彼非以洮河之備可以盡撤也。蓋西番初附之時，撫綏未盡，若進築河州，漸恢遠畧，則積粟未豐，恐壞根本；番心未定，幾喪前功。此不欲速、見小之說也。

知涇州者夏竦也，竦上十策，請習
translation_en:
…did not know when to rest the troops, while the sovereign did not disturb garrison arrangements [?]; yet he wished to withdraw and reduce the frontier troops. This was presumably because he saw that surplus troops had become excessively numerous at the time. But how could this constitute a settled plan? Shangguan Jun argued that the frontier lands around Lanzhou commanded the key routes used by enemy cavalry, and that grain should be stockpiled as a means of holding them securely. This was correct. Yet Liu Chang advanced four objections: that this sought petty gains; that the tribal groups harbored suspicions; that building fortifications incurred excessive expenditure and exhausted Qinzhou; and that the enemy’s resentment would deepen, ensuring that hostilities would not cease. He went so far as to say that the great Shun did not attack the Youmiao and that Emperor Wu of Han did not campaign against Cheshi, and thus remonstrated against fortifying Wei. Presumably he saw that expenditure at the time was too great. But how could this constitute a sound strategy?

Fan Chunren, a Court Diarist, wished to abolish the horse-pasturage establishments and cultivate their lands. He did not mean that all the horses maintained by these establishments could be dispensed with. Shaanxi was a region enclosed by natural barriers on all four sides, inaccessible to grain transport by water. If people were recruited to cultivate the pasturelands of Shayuan, the grain harvested could support the army, while the fodder and stalks obtained could feed the horses. This was a plan to achieve two benefits through one measure.

Wen Yanbo, Commissioner of Military Affairs, wished to fortify Xizhou and defer work in the Tao River region. He did not mean that all defenses along the Tao River could be withdrawn. When the western tribes had only recently submitted, efforts to pacify and reassure them were still incomplete. If one advanced to fortify Hezhou and gradually extended operations farther afield, grain reserves would not yet be plentiful, and there was a danger of undermining the base. The tribes’ allegiance was not yet settled, and earlier achievements might all but be lost. This was an argument against seeking haste and fixing one’s attention on small gains.

The prefect of Jingzhou was Xia Song. Song submitted ten proposals, requesting training in…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
強弩以爲奇兵其與蘇軾之增脩弓箭以
立社戶相同也然邊臣以竦爲怯蓋于時
元昊僣號西陲將帥正當枕戈必滅此而
後朝食而爲此策不過遷延自全耳不然
何羌人榜得竦首賞錢二千如此其侮狎
哉知慶州者范仲淹以馬鋪砦旬日築城
而名大順其與龐籍增築招安以斷賊路
相同也然輔臣反以爲迂蓋于時文正經
理西事羌人皆呼老子貟軍中一范驚破
===
膽者也而謂之迂不過夷簡挾私造謗耳
不然何宋朝人物以范仲淹爲第一哉學
士王堯臣欲屯兵環慶大畧謂各砦兵寡
勢分賊至不能追擊願益團土兵分屯渭
涇慶秦四路所以防衝突也至畢仲游謂
城寨清野俟其機會此先爲不可勝之說
是或一道也司馬光乞留諸州屯兵蓋謂
腹内地廣兵稀緩急不能控禦故願抽取
邊兵屯駐永興所以重根本也至韓琦謂
punctuated: 強弩以爲奇兵，其與蘇軾之增脩弓箭以立社戶相同也。然邊臣以竦爲怯，蓋于時元昊僣號，西陲將帥正當枕戈，必滅此而後朝食，而爲此策，不過遷延自全耳。不然，何羌人榜得竦首賞錢二千，如此其侮狎哉？知慶州者范仲淹，以馬鋪砦旬日築城而名大順，其與龐籍增築招安以斷賊路相同也。然輔臣反以爲迂，蓋于時文正經理西事，羌人皆呼老子，貟軍中一范，驚破膽者也。而謂之迂，不過夷簡挾私造謗耳。不然，何宋朝人物以范仲淹爲第一哉？學士王堯臣欲屯兵環慶，大畧謂各砦兵寡勢分，賊至不能追擊，願益團土兵，分屯渭、涇、慶、秦四路，所以防衝突也。至畢仲游謂城寨清野，俟其機會，此先爲不可勝之說，是或一道也。司馬光乞留諸州屯兵，蓋謂腹内地廣兵稀，緩急不能控禦，故願抽取邊兵屯駐永興，所以重根本也。至韓琦謂
translation_en:
…training with powerful crossbows to form a special striking force. This resembled Su Shi’s proposal to augment and repair bows and arrows and organize households into archery associations. Yet frontier officials regarded Xia Song as timid. At that time Yuanhao had usurped the imperial title, and the commanders on the western frontier ought to have slept with their weapons at the ready, determined to destroy him before taking their morning meal. To advance such a proposal amounted merely to delaying matters to preserve himself. Otherwise, why would the Qiang have posted a proclamation offering two thousand in cash for Song’s head, treating him with such contempt?

Fan Zhongyan, prefect of Qingzhou, built a walled stronghold at Mapu Stockade within ten days and named it Dashun. This resembled Pang Ji’s expansion of the fortifications at Zhao’an to cut off the enemy’s routes. Yet the chief ministers instead considered him impractical. At that time Wenzheng—that is, Fan Zhongyan—was managing affairs in the west; the Qiang all called him “the old master,” and “one Fan in the army” struck terror into their hearts [?]. Calling him impractical was merely Yijian’s malicious slander, prompted by private resentment. Otherwise, why would Fan Zhongyan be ranked foremost among the notable men of the Song dynasty?

Academician Wang Yaochen wished to station troops in Huanqing. His argument, in outline, was that each stockade had too few soldiers and that their strength was dispersed, so that when the enemy arrived they could not pursue and attack. He requested that more local troops be organized and stationed separately in the four circuits of Wei, Jing, Qing, and Qin, as a means of guarding against incursions. As for Bi Zhongyou’s proposal to fortify the stockades, clear the countryside of supplies, and await an opportunity, this was the doctrine of first making oneself invincible; it too might be a viable approach.

Sima Guang requested that garrison troops be retained in the various prefectures. He argued that the interior covered a vast area but had few troops, making it impossible to maintain control and defend it in an emergency. He therefore wished to draw troops from the frontier and station them at Yongxing, thereby strengthening the strategic heartland. As for Han Qi’s statement that…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
招兵擾賊使自困弊此多方以悞之之說
是或一策也凡此諸臣爲國建明大抵皆
忠謀勝筭惜乎仁宗諸君苟一時之安而
不爲國遠慮此洛陽無寧杌之日而關中
無息肩之期也明問有曰關中之地在漢
唐土沃兵精號百二形勝而先朝諸臣亦
成駿功矣今師旅疲於攻守財用秏於調
發郡邑困於應辦誠哉是言也豈果天時
地利人和不同哉非也夫謂陜西軍糧之
===
匱遏有由矣虜騎不時刼掠屯田往往不
秋一也三邊初派年例固原一鎮繫近年
增設而未之及二也連年脩堡築墻糜費
不貲三也全省每因災傷蠲免租稅而軍
糧無所處補四也倉官汚吏百計侵削五
也若夫兵威之不振其機在上不在下夫
城濮無功子玉卽戮新秦無徵太守必誅
潘美從征譬以匣劒陳曙失律斬之軍門
此古之制也今也進不責之以成功退不
punctuated:
招兵擾賊，使自困弊，此多方以悞之之說，是或一策也。凡此諸臣爲國建明，大抵皆忠謀勝筭。惜乎仁宗諸君苟一時之安，而不爲國遠慮，此洛陽無寧杌之日，而關中無息肩之期也。
明問有曰：「關中之地，在漢唐土沃兵精，號百二形勝，而先朝諸臣亦成駿功矣。今師旅疲於攻守，財用秏於調發，郡邑困於應辦。」誠哉是言也！豈果天時、地利、人和不同哉？非也。夫謂陜西軍糧之匱遏，有由矣。虜騎不時刼掠，屯田往往不秋，一也；三邊初派年例，固原一鎮繫近年增設，而未之及，二也；連年脩堡築墻，糜費不貲，三也；全省每因災傷蠲免租稅，而軍糧無所處補，四也；倉官汚吏百計侵削，五也。
若夫兵威之不振，其機在上不在下。夫城濮無功，子玉卽戮；新秦無徵，太守必誅；潘美從征，譬以匣劒；陳曙失律，斬之軍門。此古之制也。今也進不責之以成功，退不
translation_en:
…recruit troops and harass the enemy, causing them to wear themselves out: this is the doctrine of misleading them by manifold means, and it too may be a viable strategy. All these ministers’ proposals for the state were, by and large, loyal counsels and sound calculations for victory. Regrettably, Renzong and the other rulers sought only security for the moment and gave no thought to the state’s long-term interests. Thus Luoyang had no day of peaceful repose [?], and Guanzhong had no prospect of laying down its burdens.
Your illuminating question states: “In Han and Tang times, Guanzhong had fertile soil and excellent troops. It was renowned for strategic advantages by which two could withstand a hundred, and ministers of earlier reigns also achieved great deeds there. Now the armies are exhausted by attack and defense, financial resources are depleted by mobilization and requisitions, and prefectures and counties are distressed by the demands they must meet.” How true these words are! Can it really be that the advantages of timing, terrain, and human solidarity have changed? No. There are reasons for the shortage and obstruction [?] of military grain supplies in Shaanxi. First, enemy cavalry raid unpredictably, and military agricultural colonies often yield no harvest. Second, when annual allocations were first assigned to the Three Frontiers, the garrison command at Guyuan, established only in recent years, was not included. Third, successive years of repairing forts and building walls have entailed enormous expenditure. Fourth, taxes throughout the province are frequently remitted because of natural disasters, but there is no means of replacing the resulting shortfall in military grain. Fifth, granary officials and corrupt clerks devise a hundred ways to embezzle and siphon off supplies.
As for the failure to restore military might, its determining cause lies with those above, not those below. When Ziyu failed at Chengpu, he was immediately put to death; when levies were not forthcoming in Xinqin [?], the prefect was certain to be executed. When Pan Mei accompanied a campaign, a sword in its case was used as an admonitory comparison [?]; when Chen Shu violated military discipline, he was beheaded at the army’s gate. Such were the rules of antiquity. Nowadays, when commanders advance, they are not held responsible for achieving success; when they retreat, they are not…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
加之以嚴憲彼何苦而以死犯豺狼之鋒
哉故賊來則退縮賊去則佯追失事則破
調相推同事則裝點相庇害幾村幾堡則
欺牖獲數馬數級則誇大此三邊積弊蓋
有年矣明問又舉賈晁趙張之術可施於
今可謂慮遠而詳說矣夫以賈誼三表五
餌之術而設官是緣木以求魚也以晁錯
徙民塞下之策以徙民是張羅以驅鳥也
唯趙充國分屯要害賦農積穀之策張敞
===
輸粟贖過增脩守具之言可行於今至於
李嗚復諸人之說在今亦有采而行之者
矣而我食終不富兵終不强夫宋事可鑒
也意者難得頗牧韓范之臣司干城者歟
昔歐陽脩言於朝曰國家所憂不在於無
兵也無將也無財也無禦戎之策也無可
任之臣也唯在謹號令之頒明賞罰之施
責功效之實以是施之於今而實行伍寛
力役省縻費廣屯蓄禁侵漁重犒賞正刑
punctuated:
加之以嚴憲，彼何苦而以死犯豺狼之鋒哉？故賊來則退縮，賊去則佯追；失事則破調相推，同事則裝點相庇；害幾村幾堡則欺牖，獲數馬數級則誇大。此三邊積弊，蓋有年矣。
明問又舉賈、晁、趙、張之術可施於今，可謂慮遠而詳說矣。夫以賈誼三表五餌之術而設官，是緣木以求魚也；以晁錯徙民塞下之策以徙民，是張羅以驅鳥也。唯趙充國分屯要害、賦農積穀之策，張敞輸粟贖過、增脩守具之言，可行於今。至於李嗚復諸人之說，在今亦有采而行之者矣，而我食終不富，兵終不强。夫宋事可鑒也，意者難得頗、牧、韓、范之臣司干城者歟？
昔歐陽脩言於朝曰：「國家所憂，不在於無兵也、無將也、無財也、無禦戎之策也、無可任之臣也，唯在謹號令之頒，明賞罰之施，責功效之實。」以是施之於今，而實行伍，寛力役，省縻費，廣屯蓄，禁侵漁，重犒賞，正刑
translation_en:
…subject them to strict punishment. Why, then, would they risk death by facing the blades of these jackals and wolves? Thus, when the raiders come, they retreat; when the raiders leave, they feign pursuit. When operations fail, they shift responsibility onto one another through transfers [?]; when serving together, they embellish their reports and shield one another. When several villages and forts suffer damage, they conceal it through deception [?]; when they capture a few horses or take a few heads, they exaggerate their achievements. These entrenched abuses along the Three Frontiers have persisted for years.
Your discerning question also raises the methods of Jia, Chao, Zhao, and Zhang as potentially applicable today. Its considerations may indeed be called far-reaching and its discussion detailed. Yet to establish offices using Jia Yi’s methods of the Three Exemplary Practices and Five Baits [?] is like climbing a tree to seek fish. To relocate people using Chao Cuo’s policy of settling people along the frontier is like spreading nets to drive birds away. Only Zhao Chongguo’s policy of establishing agricultural garrisons at strategic points, assigning agricultural work, and accumulating grain, and Zhang Chang’s proposals for redeeming offenses through grain contributions and expanding and repairing defensive equipment, can be implemented today. As for the proposals of Li Wufu [?] and others, some have already been adopted and implemented in our time. Yet our provisions remain insufficient and our troops remain weak. The experience of the Song can serve as a warning. Might the problem be the difficulty of finding ministers like Lian Po, Li Mu, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan to serve as the realm’s defenders?
Ouyang Xiu once said at court: “What should concern the state is not a lack of troops, generals, wealth, strategies for resisting the Rong, or ministers who can be entrusted with responsibility. It lies solely in issuing commands with care, applying rewards and punishments clearly, and demanding actual results.” Apply this today: fill the ranks, ease labor service, reduce wasteful expenditure, expand agricultural garrisons and reserves, prohibit embezzlement and exploitation, make rewards to the troops generous, and put punishments in order…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
威嚴簡閱則師旅何疲於攻守財用何耗
於調發郡邑何困於應辦哉凡此必有大
幹旋而後能運事幾大力量而後能壓人
心大識慮而後能消變故此在
廟堂必有成算矣愚也白面書生止知俎豆
之事也倘得進而立玉階方寸地亦惟曰
明王慎德四夷咸賓以效梓人之忠謹對
punctuated: 威，嚴簡閱，則師旅何疲於攻守，財用何耗於調發，郡邑何困於應辦哉？凡此必有大幹旋而後能運事幾，大力量而後能壓人心，大識慮而後能消變故。此在廟堂必有成算矣。愚也，白面書生，止知俎豆之事也。倘得進而立玉階方寸地，亦惟曰：「明王慎德，四夷咸賓。」以效梓人之忠。謹對。
translation_en: …disciplinary authority and make military inspections rigorous, then why should the troops be exhausted by attack and defense, financial resources depleted by mobilization, or prefectures and counties burdened by supplying what is required? All this demands great skill in managing affairs before critical developments can be directed, great strength before people’s hearts can be brought into submission, and great discernment and foresight before disruptions can be dispelled. Surely the court already has settled plans for these matters. I, in my ignorance, am merely a young scholar, versed only in the affairs of sacrificial vessels and ritual. Should I be permitted to advance and occupy even a tiny place before the jade steps of the throne, I would say only: “When an enlightened king attends carefully to his virtue, the peoples of the four quarters all submit as guests.” Thus would I offer the loyalty of a master carpenter. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試録後序
嘉靖丁酉秋八月壬申陝西
鄉試録成巡按御史戴〔璟〕以
末簡授〔鳳來〕乃颺言曰蔚乎
休哉關中人文之盛一至是
乎初〔鳳來〕之膺聘戒途也遵
漢中踰鳳翔歷二千餘里而
===
後稅駕因得縱觀吳嶽太白
終南九嵕之勝東望泰華隱
隱天表呈奇貢異綿亘不絶
可不謂雄矣乎逾汧浜浙褒絶
汧沿渭皆波濤洶洶瀠洄萬
狀凝睇之頃渺不知其所之
東會黃河環抱若帶可不謂
punctuated:
陝西鄉試録後序

嘉靖丁酉秋八月壬申，陝西鄉試録成，巡按御史戴〔璟〕以末簡授〔鳳來〕，乃颺言曰：「蔚乎休哉！關中人文之盛，一至是乎！」初，〔鳳來〕之膺聘戒途也，遵漢中，踰鳳翔，歷二千餘里而後稅駕，因得縱觀吳嶽、太白、終南、九嵕之勝。東望泰華，隱隱天表，呈奇貢異，綿亘不絶，可不謂雄矣乎？逾汧浜浙褒，絶汧沿渭，皆波濤洶洶，瀠洄萬狀。凝睇之頃，渺不知其所之，東會黃河，環抱若帶，可不謂
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

On the renshen day of the eighth month, in autumn of the dingyou year of Jiajing (1537), the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination was completed. The Regional Inspector, Dai Jing 戴璟, entrusted the closing pages to me, Fenglai 鳳來. I then exclaimed: “How flourishing and splendid! Has the cultural achievement of Guanzhong reached such heights?”

When I first accepted the invitation and prepared to set out, I traveled through Hanzhong and across Fengxiang, covering more than two thousand li before finally unhitching my carriage. Thus I was able to survey at leisure the magnificent scenery of Wuyue, Taibai, Zhongnan, and Jiuzong. Looking east toward Taihua, I saw it dimly rising beyond the skyline, displaying marvels and wonders in an unbroken succession. Could this fail to be called majestic? I crossed the Qian and Bao waters [?], traversed the Qian, and followed the Wei: everywhere waves surged, and currents swirled in myriad forms. As I gazed intently, their distant courses vanished from sight. Eastward they joined the Yellow River, encircling the land like a sash. Could this fail to be called…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
秀矣乎夫天地不能秘其靈
淑之氣始融結而爲山川則
山川者天地之英華也矧闗
中形勝甲天下固宜其鍾於
人者剛毅正大軒偉而不羣
也既乃得其文而徧觀之則
見其語意簡古弗溺時好蒼
===
然黯然不可迫視者猶山之
雄也其筆勢豪宕理致醇深
繩引珠貫纚纚不絕者猶河
之秀也顧限於
制額取之弗能盡録之弗能周
耳所謂蔚乎休哉者信矣信
矣於是御史忻然謂〔鳳來〕等
punctuated: 秀矣乎？夫天地不能秘其靈淑之氣，始融結而爲山川，則山川者天地之英華也。矧闗中形勝甲天下，固宜其鍾於人者剛毅正大，軒偉而不羣也。既乃得其文而徧觀之，則見其語意簡古，弗溺時好，蒼然黯然，不可迫視者，猶山之雄也；其筆勢豪宕，理致醇深，繩引珠貫，纚纚不絕者，猶河之秀也。顧限於制額，取之弗能盡，録之弗能周耳。所謂蔚乎休哉者，信矣！信矣！於是御史忻然謂〔鳳來〕等
translation_en:
…is this not beautiful? Heaven and earth cannot conceal their spiritually potent and felicitous vital energy; it first coalesces into mountains and rivers. Mountains and rivers are thus the finest essence of heaven and earth. Moreover, Guanzhong’s terrain and scenic grandeur rank foremost under heaven. It is surely fitting that those in whom this energy concentrates should be resolute and upright, lofty in bearing and outstanding among their fellows.

Then, when we obtained their compositions and read them all, we found their language and meaning spare and antique, unswayed by contemporary fashions. Their venerable gravity and dark depth, which one could scarcely gaze upon at close quarters, resembled the majesty of the mountains. Their brushwork was bold and unrestrained, their reasoning pure and profound; their arguments followed like a drawn cord or threaded pearls, flowing on without interruption, resembling the beauty of the rivers. Yet, constrained by the imperially prescribed quota, we could not select all of them or include them all in the record. The saying, “How splendid and beautiful!” is indeed true—indeed true! Thereupon the Censor joyfully addressed Fenglai and the others…

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
曰以人事
君〔璟〕之責也得士如此此責庶塞乎
復矍然曰以言取人惟聖其
難之庸詎知無靜言庸違者
奸其間乎夫安得不憂於是
〔鳳來〕乃進多士而諗之曰今
日之事以言求者以言應之
===
夫言固可以曼詞詭辨而僥
倖聲華也若心術之邪正操
履之汚隆則天地鬼神實臨
之可無憂乎夫不知其人徒
信其言以健羡而引重而借
譽者是謂不明徒飾其言以
衒鬻而憒眊而滑稽者是謂
punctuated: 曰：「以人事君，〔璟〕之責也。得士如此，此責庶塞乎？」復矍然曰：「以言取人，惟聖其難之，庸詎知無靜言庸違者奸其間乎？夫安得不憂？」於是〔鳳來〕乃進多士而諗之曰：「今日之事，以言求者，以言應之。夫言固可以曼詞詭辨而僥倖聲華也。若心術之邪正、操履之汚隆，則天地鬼神實臨之，可無憂乎？夫不知其人，徒信其言，以健羡而引重而借譽者，是謂不明；徒飾其言，以衒鬻而憒眊而滑稽者，是謂
translation_en: …said: “To serve the ruler by providing worthy men is my responsibility, Jing’s 〔璟〕. Having obtained scholars such as these, may I have nearly fulfilled that responsibility?” Then, visibly startled, he said again: “Even the sage considered it difficult to select men on the basis of their words. How can we know that none whose words are agreeable but whose conduct is contrary have insinuated themselves among them? How can one avoid anxiety?” Thereupon Fenglai 〔鳳來〕 summoned the assembled scholars forward and admonished them: “In today’s undertaking, those seeking men do so through their words, and you respond with words. Through words, one can indeed use ornate phrasing and deceptive arguments to gain renown by good fortune. But as for whether your intentions are crooked or upright, and your conduct base or noble, Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, truly watch over these. Can you be without anxiety? To know nothing of a man himself and merely trust his words, eagerly admiring him, advancing his standing, and lending him reputation—this is called a lack of discernment. Merely to embellish one’s words to display and sell oneself, while being muddleheaded, benighted, and glib—this is called …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不忠不明之罪小不忠之罪
大則爾多士之所自憂固有
甚於諸執事者矣傳曰周之
士也貴秦之士也賤夫周秦
所都均是地也其所養所用
均是士也山川之雄秀如舊
也而士習之貴賤頓殊盍亦
===
反其本哉夫審取舍者存乎
介勵進脩者存乎誠樹經濟
者存乎才揚忠貞者存乎節
以是四者而文之以禮樂則
可謂大丈夫矣豈但與周之
士並駕焉陝之山川增重哉
行將勒之鼎彝垂之聲歌曰
punctuated:
不忠。不明之罪小，不忠之罪大，則爾多士之所自憂，固有甚於諸執事者矣。傳曰：「周之士也貴，秦之士也賤。」夫周秦所都，均是地也；其所養所用，均是士也；山川之雄秀如舊也，而士習之貴賤頓殊，盍亦反其本哉？
夫審取舍者存乎介，勵進脩者存乎誠，樹經濟者存乎才，揚忠貞者存乎節。以是四者，而文之以禮樂，則可謂大丈夫矣。豈但與周之士並駕焉？陝之山川增重哉！行將勒之鼎彝，垂之聲歌，曰：
translation_en:
…disloyalty. The fault of lacking discernment is minor; the fault of disloyalty is grave. Thus you assembled scholars indeed have greater cause for concern about yourselves than do the officials conducting this examination. A transmitted text says: “The scholars of Zhou were esteemed; the scholars of Qin were despised.” Zhou and Qin established their capitals in this same land; those whom they nurtured and employed were alike scholars. The grandeur and beauty of the mountains and rivers remained unchanged, yet the nobility or baseness of scholarly conduct differed utterly. Should we not return to its root?
Discerning what to accept and reject depends upon integrity; striving to advance in learning and self-cultivation depends upon sincerity; establishing achievements in governing the realm depends upon ability; manifesting loyalty and steadfastness depends upon moral constancy. Possessing these four qualities and refining them through ritual and music, one may indeed be called a great man. Would such men merely rank alongside the scholars of Zhou? Even the mountains and rivers of Shaanxi would gain in prestige! Soon their deeds will be inscribed on bronze vessels and perpetuated in songs, declaring: …

title: 嘉靖十六年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此茲科鄉試士也豈非諸大
夫主司之大快哉貽我令名
紓我隱憂是在爾多士矣是
在爾多士矣
四川成都府綿州儒學學正
毛鳳來謹序
punctuated:
「此茲科鄉試士也。」豈非諸大夫主司之大快哉！貽我令名，紓我隱憂，是在爾多士矣！是在爾多士矣！
四川成都府綿州儒學學正毛鳳來謹序。
translation_en:
…“These are the scholars of this Provincial Examination.” Would this not be a great delight to the gentlemen presiding over the examination! To bring us an honorable reputation and relieve our unspoken anxieties rests with you, scholars! It rests with you, scholars!
Preface respectfully composed by Mao Fenglai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Mianzhou, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan.
